Title: Accounts, sessions, credentials and the customer's own bookings
Description: Everything between a visitor deciding to buy and that visitor being a row the system can name: registration, sign-in, the JWT session cookie, password recovery, the ownership of a booking, and the list of bookings an account owns. Authentication is own email and password with JWT and never Cognito; a guest may browse but may not hold or book.
SourceRef: SRC-001 §5.4.1 SRC-002 §4.8 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02 E5

Title: Create the users table and register an account in one request
Description: A visitor supplies an email address and a password and receives a customer account and a live session in one request; registration does not bounce them to a second form. The user row has exactly seven columns and no name, phone or address field, because no frozen source asks for one and inventing one would be inventing scope.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/register with {"email":" Ada@Example.com ","password":"correct horse battery"} returns 201, sets a fr_session cookie, and returns {"user_id","email":"Ada@Example.com","role":"customer"} with the email trimmed and its case as entered; SELECT email, role, password_version, last_signed_in_at FROM users WHERE lower(email)='ada@example.com' returns exactly 1 row with role='customer', password_version=1 and last_signed_in_at IS NULL; SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='users' returns exactly id, email, password_hash, role, password_version, created_at, last_signed_in_at and nothing else; password_hash is not equal to the submitted password and the submitted password appears in no log line, no response body and no column; a second POST with "ADA@example.com" returns 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED with the body "An account already exists for that email address. Sign in instead, or reset the password if you have forgotten it."; 20 simultaneous identical registrations report exactly 1 success and 19 conflicts, SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE lower(email)='ada@example.com' returns 1, and no response is a 500; role is never read from the request body -- a request carrying "role":"admin" still produces a row with role='customer'
SourceRef: P-ACC-01 EP-ACC-01 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-052 SRC-001 §5.4.1 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02

Title: Enforce the password rules and hash off the event loop, with one verification on every branch
Description: A length floor, a byte ceiling, no composition rule, bcrypt in a thread, and a comparison that runs even when the email address has no account. The equal-work property is asserted structurally with a counter and never by measuring elapsed time, because a timing assertion is flaky and Art IX.5 makes a test that reads the wall clock a defect. The sentinel-hash clause covers an account created with no usable password by E6 P-ADM-17 without owning that endpoint.
AcceptanceCriteria: With PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH=12: an 11-character password on register or reset-confirm returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with "Your password must be at least 12 characters. It does not have to contain numbers or symbols."; the Devanagari string of 28 code points encoding to 84 UTF-8 bytes returns 422 with details.byte_length=84 and the message quoting 84, not an example value; "correct horse battery" (21 bytes) and " leading space kept " are both accepted and the password is never trimmed, so signing in without the spaces fails; no composition rule is applied -- a 12-character all-lowercase password is accepted; setting PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH=14 makes the same 12-character request return "at least 14 characters", proving the figure is interpolated and not a literal, while 72 stays a literal because it is bcrypt truncation and has no variable behind it; bcrypt is invoked on a worker thread, asserted by a test that fails if threading.current_thread() inside the hash call is the event loop thread; with a counter wrapping the verify function, POST /api/auth/login increments it by exactly 1 for an unregistered address and by exactly 1 for a registered address with a wrong password, both returning 401 CREDENTIALS_INVALID -- and by exactly 1 for an account whose password_hash is the unusable sentinel, so there is no third branch and no early return; no assertion in this story measures elapsed time; every users row has a NOT NULL password_hash, and SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT password_hash) FROM users WHERE last_signed_in_at IS NULL returns 0, so no two no-password accounts share one sentinel value
SourceRef: P-ACC-03 EP-ACC-01 EP-ACC-02 FR-ADR-050 SRC-001 §7.4 SRC-002 §5.4.1

Title: Sign in, record the sign-in instant, and answer identically for an unknown address
Description: Email and password are exchanged for a session. The two failure situations are given one message on purpose -- this is the one place in the product where that happens -- because distinguishing them turns the endpoint into a directory of who has an account. There is no account lockout: no source names a threshold and inventing one would be inventing policy.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/login with the registered address in any case and the correct password returns 200, sets fr_session, and returns {"user_id","email","role"}; SELECT last_signed_in_at FROM users WHERE id=:id equals the injected clock instant and was written by the single statement UPDATE users SET last_signed_in_at = :now WHERE id = :id; SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE user_id=:id returns 0 -- signing in is not a privileged write and writes no audit row; an unknown address and a registered address with the wrong password both return 401 CREDENTIALS_INVALID with byte-identical response bodies containing "That email address and password do not match an account.", and after both attempts SELECT last_signed_in_at FROM users WHERE id=:id is unchanged; a missing or empty field returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED "Enter your email address and password."; an account whose stored password is 10 characters still signs in with 200, because sign-in never length-validates the password; 20 consecutive failed attempts inside the bucket produce 20 x 401 and never a locked or disabled account -- SELECT role FROM users WHERE id=:id is unchanged and the 21st attempt with the correct password returns 200
SourceRef: P-ACC-02 EP-ACC-02 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-018 SRC-001 §5.4.1 SRC-002 §4.8

Title: Issue the session cookie, revoke it on a password change, and keep sign-out public
Description: A session is a JWT in an HttpOnly cookie and there is no server-side session store, because containers are stateless. The pv claim is what makes a stateless session revocable. OPEN-TLS-01 is open and DEFERRED, so COOKIE_SECURE has no default and is off in the deployed environment until a domain and an ACM certificate exist -- this story asserts the flag follows the variable and asserts nothing about what the deployed value will be.
AcceptanceCriteria: The Set-Cookie from a successful sign-in is fr_session=<jwt>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=43200, with the Secure attribute present when COOKIE_SECURE=true and absent when COOKIE_SECURE=false; the process refuses to start when COOKIE_SECURE or JWT_SECRET is unset -- neither has a default and a startup with either missing exits non-zero with the variable named; decoding the JWT payload yields exactly the claims sub, role, pv, iat, exp and no email address and no name; the authorisation dependency reads the users row by primary key on every authenticated request, so a token whose pv is one behind users.password_version returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED "Your session has ended because the password was changed. Sign in to continue.", a token whose users row has been removed returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED "Sign in to continue.", and a token with any one required claim removed is rejected rather than treated as a default; a role changed directly in the database takes effect on the very next request rather than at the next sign-in; POST /api/auth/logout returns 204 with Set-Cookie: fr_session=; Max-Age=0 carrying the same attributes the cookie was issued with, and returns 204 with no cookie sent, with an expired cookie, with a malformed cookie and on a second consecutive call -- it is declared auth: public in EP-ACC-03 and the generated route inventory lists it under Public, no session required, so no build may make it 401; SELECT to_regclass('session') returns null -- no session table exists
SourceRef: P-ACC-05 EP-ACC-02 EP-ACC-03 EP-ACC-04 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-053 FR-ADR-069 SRC-002 §7.3 SRC-003 OPEN-TLS-01

Title: Fix the session lifetime at a single configured value and build no refresh token
Description: One absolute lifetime, no sliding expiry, no silent renewal and no second credential. The 12-hour figure is ASSUMED, not RULED -- no frozen source and no APPROVED ADR names a session lifetime -- so it stays configuration, is stated in exactly one place, and never hardens into a constraint. The shorter of the two candidate lifetimes was taken because the cookie crosses the network in the clear while OPEN-TLS-01 is open.
AcceptanceCriteria: With SESSION_TTL_SECONDS=43200 and the clock injected at 2026-08-14T10:00:00Z, the issued token carries iat=2026-08-14T10:00:00Z and exp=2026-08-14T22:00:00Z and the cookie carries Max-Age=43200, so the cookie and the token cannot outlive each other; with the clock advanced to 2026-08-14T21:59:00Z, GET /api/auth/me returns 200; with the clock advanced to 2026-08-14T22:00:01Z the same request returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED "Your session has ended. Sign in to continue."; every comparison is against the injected clock -- no test in this story sleeps or reads the wall clock, and a build that compares against the container clock fails when the container clock is offset from the injected one; SESSION_TTL_SECONDS=0 and a non-integer value each fail startup validation with the variable named; the generated route inventory contains no refresh, renew or token-exchange route, and the lifetime figure 43200 appears in exactly one place in the codebase -- grep for the literal outside the configuration default returns 0 hits
SourceRef: P-ACC-06 EP-ACC-02 EP-ACC-04 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-053 FR-ADR-018 SRC-002 §7.3

Title: Prove the absence of a verification gate and of any address-change endpoint
Description: v1 has no email-verification gate and that is a recorded accepted weakness, not a design preference: whoever controls the address controls the account, by the reset chain the product already specifies, and the registrant has no route back. That enlarged consequence is filed as OPEN-EMAILOWN-01, open and reserved. This story builds no remedy and specifies no address-change endpoint -- inventing one would be a scope change -- it asserts the specified absences so nobody closes the gap by habit.
AcceptanceCriteria: Immediately after a 201 from POST /api/auth/register the same session reaches every authenticated route with no intermediate step: GET /api/auth/me returns 200 with role "customer" and the response body carries no verified, email_verified or pending field; the registration writes nothing to the queue -- SELECT count(*) FROM outbox_message is identical before and after the request, so no verification message and no welcome message is enqueued; the generated route inventory contains no route that writes users.email: a test enumerating every registered route fails if any PATCH, PUT or POST accepts an account email address for update, and the same test fails if a users.email UPDATE statement exists anywhere outside the registration insert; a customer who registers a second account at a different address does not move their first booking -- SELECT user_id FROM booking WHERE reference=:ref is unchanged and equals the first account id; no response body and no error message anywhere states or implies that an address is unverified
SourceRef: P-ACC-04 EP-ACC-01 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-048 FR-ADR-012 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02 SRC-003 OPEN-EMAIL-01

Title: Send a single-use password reset link and answer identically for an unknown address
Description: Nothing is ever deleted, so a registered address is taken permanently and a reset that works with no help from anyone is the only route back into an account. The endpoint writes the token row and an outbox_message row in one transaction; the actual SES send is E4 P-TKT-12's and phase 5's, so this story asserts the enqueue and not the delivery.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/password-reset/request returns 202 for a registered and for an unregistered address with byte-identical bodies containing "If that email address has an account, a reset link is on its way to it. The link works once and expires in 30 minutes."; the 30 is rendered from PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS / 60 as a whole number of minutes, so with PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS=600 the same string reads "10 minutes" on the 202 body, on SCR-ACC-02's confirmation panel and in the email template, and a grep for the literal 30 in those three renderers returns 0 hits; for a registered address SELECT count(*) FROM password_reset_token WHERE user_id=:id AND used_at IS NULL returns exactly 1 after two consecutive requests, the earlier row having been marked used, so at most one live token exists per account; the stored row carries token_sha256 equal to the SHA-256 hex of the 43-character token and no column and no log line holds the token value itself; expires_at = created_at + 1800 seconds from the injected clock, so a token created at 10:00:00Z has expires_at 10:30:00Z; the token row and one outbox_message row with topic 'password_reset.send' are written in the same transaction -- forcing the transaction to roll back leaves neither row -- and that message payload carries user_id and reset_token_id and no token value; for an unregistered address SELECT count(*) FROM password_reset_token is unchanged and no outbox_message row is written; an empty or malformed address returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED "Enter an email address."; the emailed link is {PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/account/reset/confirm?token=<token> and the process refuses to start when PUBLIC_BASE_URL is unset
SourceRef: P-ACC-07 EP-ACC-05 SCR-ACC-06 FR-ADR-031 FR-ADR-053 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-060 SRC-001 §5.4.1

Title: Complete a password reset once, and only once, ending every existing session
Description: The token is the credential and the old password is neither required nor accepted. The single-use guarantee is the conditional update, not a prior read -- the same shape as the seat guard, where the read cannot protect what the write must. Completing the reset increments password_version, which is what stops every existing session for that account from being accepted.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/password-reset/confirm with a live 43-character token and a valid new password returns 200 and sets a fresh fr_session; in one transaction password_reset_token.used_at is set, users.password_hash is replaced, users.password_version goes from 1 to 2 and users.last_signed_in_at is written from the injected clock; the cookie issued before the reset then returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED on GET /api/auth/me while the new cookie returns 200; the single-use guarantee is the conditional UPDATE password_reset_token SET used_at = :now WHERE id = :id AND used_at IS NULL affecting exactly one row inside the same transaction -- 50 simultaneous submissions of one token report exactly 1 success and 49 x 400 RESET_TOKEN_INVALID "That reset link has already been used. Request a new one.", and SELECT password_version FROM users WHERE id=:id is 2 and not 51; an unknown token returns 400 "That reset link is not valid. Request a new one."; a token past expires_at on the injected clock returns 400 "That reset link has expired. Request a new one."; a token of any length other than 43 returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with no database query issued, asserted from the query log; the request schema has no old_password or current_password field and one supplied is not accepted; no confirmation email is sent -- SELECT count(*) FROM outbox_message is unchanged by a successful reset; the submitted token appears in no log line at any level
SourceRef: P-ACC-08 EP-ACC-06 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-056 SRC-001 §7.4 SRC-001 §5.4.1

Title: Rate limit every credential endpoint, derive Retry-After from the refill rate, and fail closed
Description: Five buckets across sign-in, registration, reset request and reset confirm. Extending the limiter beyond the two endpoints SRC-002 §8.4.1 names is stricter and needs no signature. The reset-confirm bucket is its own and not the request's: sharing one family would let four mistyped passwords lock a customer out of the only route back into an account whose address is permanently taken. The figures are estimates, not measurements, and phase 7's load test replaces them.
AcceptanceCriteria: With Redis up and the clock injected: the 11th POST /api/auth/login for one lower(email) inside 15 minutes returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After: 90 and "Too many sign-in attempts for that email address. Try again in 90 seconds."; the 31st from one IP inside 15 minutes returns Retry-After: 30 and "Too many sign-in attempts from this connection. Try again in 30 seconds."; the 6th POST /api/auth/register from one IP in an hour returns Retry-After: 720 and "Too many accounts have been created from this connection. Try again in 12 minutes."; the 6th reset request from one IP in an hour returns Retry-After: 720 and "Too many reset requests from this connection. Try again in 12 minutes."; the 11th reset confirm from one IP in an hour returns Retry-After: 360 and "Too many attempts from this connection. Try again in 6 minutes."; the confirm bucket is separate from the request bucket -- after 5 requests and 6 confirms in one hour the request bucket is empty and the confirm bucket still admits 4 more calls; every confirm request spends a token including one rejected for a malformed token or a failing password; every Retry-After equals ceil(window_seconds / capacity) computed from the bucket that refused and never a constant, so a caller who empties the sign-in per-email bucket at t=0 and retries at t=30s receives Retry-After: 60 and not 90; two requests from one peer carrying different forged leftmost X-Forwarded-For values are counted in the same bucket, because the key is the rightmost-but-one entry with exactly one trusted proxy; both buckets on an endpoint must have a token -- exhausting either alone produces the 429; with Redis stopped, POST /api/auth/login returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE "Sign-in is unavailable right now. Browsing still works. Try again shortly." and never 200, and GET on a browse route still returns 200 in the same run
SourceRef: P-ACC-14 EP-ACC-01 EP-ACC-02 EP-ACC-05 EP-ACC-06 FR-ADR-058 FR-ADR-028 SRC-002 §8.4.1 SRC-002 §7.9

Title: Bind every booking to one user row with ON DELETE RESTRICT, and red-proof the refusal
Description: The migration author reads the column, not the prose, and RESTRICT was stated everywhere except on the column. CASCADE is refused because it silently destroys paid bookings, their snapshotted per-seat prices and every takings figure derived from them, with nobody having written the word delete; SET NULL is refused because the column is NOT NULL and the database would not accept it. The refusal is proved by watching CASCADE do the damage on purpose and then restoring, not by repeating the sentence.
AcceptanceCriteria: The phase 2 migration declares booking.user_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT; SELECT confdeltype FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid='booking'::regclass AND contype='f' AND confrelid='users'::regclass returns 'r' -- not 'c' and not 'n'; SELECT is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='booking' AND column_name='user_id' returns NO, which is why SET NULL is not a candidate; with one user row and one booking row referencing it, DELETE FROM users WHERE id=:id raises SQLSTATE 23503 foreign_key_violation, the transaction rolls back, and SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE user_id=:id and SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE id=:id both still return 1; the CASCADE refusal is red-proved rather than asserted -- with the constraint temporarily redefined ON DELETE CASCADE the same DELETE succeeds and leaves SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE user_id=:id at 0 with its booking_seat rows and their snapshotted price_paise gone, then the constraint is restored to RESTRICT and the restore is verified by repeating the first delete and observing 23503 again; deleting a user row that no booking references succeeds, and a live session for that row then returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED "Sign in to continue." from GET /api/auth/me, so P-ACC-05 exception 5 is reachable and is not dead code; no endpoint accepts a user_id field in a path, query or body -- the booking owner comes from the authorisation dependency, and the generated route inventory contains no DELETE against users
SourceRef: P-ACC-09 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-013 FR-ADR-014 FR-ADR-039 SRC-001 §9.2 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02

Title: Return the caller's own bookings in two groups, both arrays always present
Description: The list a customer opens at the door. Both arrays are returned on every response whatever group says, so no client ever branches on whether a field exists; page applies to each group independently against its own total_, so a page past the end of one group returns that group empty and is a 200. Money is an integer number of paise on the wire and is formatted only at render time. Nothing on a row exposes cancellation or a refund: SRC-001 §5.4.3 is withdrawn by erratum E-2.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/me/bookings with a valid session returns 200 carrying upcoming, past, page, page_size, total_upcoming and total_past, and both arrays are present in every response -- with ?group=upcoming, past is [] and total_past still carries its true count, never omitted; for a caller with total_upcoming=2 and total_past=37 at page_size=20: ?page=1 returns 2 and 20 rows, ?page=2 returns 0 and 17 rows, ?page=3 returns 0 and 0 rows, and all three are 200 rather than 404 or 422 -- page is never silently ignored; each row carries reference in FR-XXXX-XXXX form, movie_title, hall_name, seat_count between 1 and 10, and group; showtime_starts_at, showtime_ends_at and booked_at are ISO-8601 carrying the cinema row's UTC offset -- "2026-08-20T14:00:00+05:30" and never the same instant as "2026-08-20T08:30:00Z" -- serialised by the server from the cinema row and never by the client; seats is an array of labels ordered by row letter then seat number compared as an integer, so a booking of F2 and F10 returns ["F2","F10"] and a booking of F7, F8, F9 created in the order F9, F7, F8 still returns ["F7","F8","F9"]; total_paise is an integer equal to the sum of the snapshotted booking_seat.price_paise, so three seats at 45000, 54000 and 54000 return 153000 and never 1530.0 and never the string "₹1,530.00"; no row carries status, cancelled_at, a cancel control, a refund amount, a refund state, a cancellation reason, a tax line, a discount, a booking fee or a QR field; page=0, page=1001, page_size=0, page_size=51 and group=other each return 422 VALIDATION_FAILED; with no session the endpoint returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED "Sign in to see your bookings."; a caller with no bookings at all returns 200 with two empty arrays and both total_ counts 0
SourceRef: P-ACC-10 EP-ACC-07 FR-ADR-036 FR-ADR-039 FR-ADR-015 FR-ADR-048 FR-ADR-013 FR-ADR-018 SRC-001 §5.4.2 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01

Title: Classify a booking upcoming or past against ends_at, and order each group totally
Description: The boundary is ASSUMED, not RULED: SRC-001 §5.4.2 names the two groups and no source draws the line between them, so this never hardens into a constraint and is flagged wherever it matters. ends_at rather than starts_at because a customer sitting in the hall is the most likely person to open this list, and because sales can still be open after the advertised start. The tie-breakers are not cosmetic: without a total order, paging shows one booking twice and hides another.
AcceptanceCriteria: With showtime.starts_at=2026-08-20T08:30:00Z and showtime.ends_at=2026-08-20T11:05:00Z and the clock injected: at 2026-08-20T09:30:00Z the booking's group is "upcoming" although the film is running, at exactly 2026-08-20T11:05:00Z it is "past", and at 2026-08-20T11:06:00Z it is "past" -- the rule is now < ends_at for upcoming and now >= ends_at for past, evaluated against the injected clock in UTC and never against the container clock or the client clock; upcoming is ordered by showtime.starts_at ascending then booking.created_at descending then booking.id ascending, and past by showtime.starts_at descending then the same two tie-breakers, proved by seeding five bookings of which three share one starts_at and asserting the exact returned id order, then paging the group at page_size=2 across three requests and asserting every id appears exactly once and none is missing; SELECT is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='showtime' AND column_name='ends_at' returns NO, and ends_at is stored rather than derived from starts_at plus a runtime; no test in this story sleeps or reads the wall clock
SourceRef: P-ACC-11 EP-ACC-07 EP-ACC-08 FR-ADR-018 FR-ADR-043 SRC-001 §5.4.2 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01

Title: Scope every /api/me/ route to the caller on the router, and limit the reference lookup
Description: Authorisation is applied once, on the router, as a dependency -- never per handler, because a handler that reads a user id from the request and checks it itself is the pattern that eventually misses one. The three-assertion shape is required: a test asserting only that another customer's reference is denied passes against a query that returns nothing for anybody. The list endpoint is deliberately unlimited and the single-reference lookup is limited, because only the second takes a guessable identifier.
AcceptanceCriteria: Customer A owns reference refA and customer B owns refB. Signed in as A: GET /api/me/bookings returns a non-empty list containing refA (assertion 1, which proves the query works); GET /api/me/bookings/{refB} returns 404 NOT_FOUND "No booking with that reference is on your account." (assertion 2, which proves it is scoped); signed in as B, GET /api/me/bookings/{refB} returns 200 (assertion 3, which proves the scoping is by identity and not by the data being absent) -- all three are required and a suite carrying only assertion 2 fails this story; a reference that has never existed returns the same 404 with the same body and the same code as refB did for A, so the endpoint is not an oracle; a manager session and an admin session calling GET /api/me/bookings each receive their own bookings only, and no user_id or override parameter is accepted in any path, query or body under /api/me/ -- the generated route inventory contains none; the ownership predicate is in the same statement as the lookup (WHERE reference = :normalised AND user_id = :caller), asserted from the query log showing one statement rather than a fetch followed by an in-handler check; the dependency is declared once on the router and grep finds no per-handler caller-id check under /api/me/; the reference is normalised case-insensitively with hyphens and whitespace ignored and the FR prefix optional, and a character outside the 30-character alphabet is not mapped to anything and produces the same 404; the 21st lookup in a minute for one user returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After: 3 and "Too many lookups. Try again in 3 seconds.", the 61st in a minute from one IP returns Retry-After: 1 and "Too many lookups. Try again in 1 second." in the singular; GET /api/me/bookings itself is unlimited -- 100 consecutive calls all return 200 and none carries Retry-After
SourceRef: P-ACC-12 P-ACC-14 EP-ACC-07 EP-ACC-08 FR-ADR-011 FR-ADR-015 FR-ADR-058 FR-ADR-009 SRC-001 §7.4 SRC-001 §5.4.2

Title: Carry the seat selection through the registration detour without taking a hold
Description: This is the one seam in the product where a guest becomes a customer, so it is where losing the selection costs the sale. fr.pending_selection is written once when an unauthenticated visitor leaves a seat map with a non-empty selection -- by either route out, because which of two controls they pressed two screens earlier may not decide whether they keep their seats -- read once, and deleted on restore. E2 P-SEA-03's fr.selection is a different key with a different write policy and the two-key design must not be collapsed into one.
AcceptanceCriteria: An unauthenticated visitor on /showtimes/412 with seat ids 1187 and 1188 selected who leaves for the authentication screen by either route -- the primary action reading "Sign in to hold these seats" or the header's Sign in link -- has sessionStorage["fr.pending_selection"] equal to {"showtime_id":412,"seat_ids":[1187,1188],"stored_at":"2026-08-14T10:00:00Z"} written before /sign-in opens, and both routes render the context note "Your seats are still selected. Sign in to hold them."; fr.pending_selection and fr.selection are two distinct keys and both are present at that moment, so a build in which one key serves both purposes fails this story; after a 201 from register or a 200 from sign-in the client navigates to /showtimes/412 and refetches the seat map before restoring anything, then re-selects only the stored ids still reported available; stored ids now sold or held_by_other are not selected, are drawn in their real state, and are named -- "C12 and C13 were taken while you were signing in. Your other seats are still selected." at two or more, the same sentence in the singular at exactly one, and "The seats you chose were taken while you were signing in. Choose again from the map." when none survives; the restore then deletes fr.pending_selection and leaves fr.selection holding the restored selection; no hold is taken by the restore -- the network log shows zero requests to the hold endpoint between sign-in and the customer pressing the primary action, which now reads "Hold these seats"; a stored entry whose stored_at is more than 30 minutes before the injected clock is discarded and the map opens with no selection and no message; with sessionStorage unavailable nothing is stored, no message is shown, the sign-in still succeeds and the map opens with no selection; a stored showtime_id that no longer exists returns the visitor to the movie listing with "That showtime is no longer available."; after sign-out, Object.keys(sessionStorage).filter(k => k.startsWith("fr.")).length is 0 -- the whole fr. namespace is swept, not a named list of keys
SourceRef: P-ACC-13 SCR-ACC-01 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-045 FR-ADR-052 SRC-001 §3.1 SRC-001 §5.2.6 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02

Title: Measure the booking run against 120 seconds and report the first-time figure separately
Description: SC-1, measured rather than enforced. The first-time figure includes registration and will not meet the target, so it is reported on its own line with no target attached; one blended number would either fail a criterion the product does meet or hide that the first-time path is slower. The reporting rule is the honesty floor's: the worst run first, then the median, each with its count.
AcceptanceCriteria: A scripted run records t0 as the first paint of the seat map with real seat data -- not the click that requested it and not the paint of the page shell -- and t1 as the paint of the booking reference on the confirmation screen, and reports t1 - t0 over at least 20 signed-in runs in the form "20 runs; slowest 84 s; median 51 s", worst first and always with the count, never "about 50 seconds"; the criterion passes when the slowest signed-in run is under 120 seconds, not when the median is; the first-time run -- no account at t0, including pressing "Sign in to hold these seats", registering and returning through fr.pending_selection -- is reported on its own labelled line with its own slowest and median and no pass or fail attached, and the two figures are never averaged together; the measured path includes the simulated payment's PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS in full (the unit is milliseconds, so a configured 1500 is 1.5 s of the budget, not 1500 s) and both round trips, and no run may skip the simulated payment to improve the figure; a run in which the 180-second hold TTL expires mid-run produces 409 HOLD_EXPIRED with "The hold on your seats has ended and they have been released. You have not been charged." and is reported as a failed run rather than excluded from the count
SourceRef: P-ACC-15 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-041 FR-ADR-027 SRC-001 §3.1

Title: Configure halls, seats, showtimes and pricing
Description: The admin surface that configures the venue, its halls and their seats, schedules every showtime and sets every price. Everything in it writes, every write belongs to the admin alone, and every write carries an audit row in the same transaction.
SourceRef: E6 S4 E6 S5 E6 S6 R-ADM-03 R-ADM-04 R-ADM-05 R-ADM-06 R-ADM-07 R-PRC-02

Title: Author, publish and withdraw films by hand
Description: An admin types every film into FrontRow by hand - title, poster, synopsis, the lookup vocabularies it is built from, and the window it is shown in - and publishes it. There is no external movie API, no import, no upsert and nothing on a schedule.
SourceRef: E6 S4 E6 S5 E6 S6 R-ADM-01 R-ADM-02 SRC-002 §E E-2 SRC-002 §E E-4

Title: Enforce admin authorisation once, on the /api/admin router
Description: Every privileged write in FrontRow belongs to the admin role alone. One dependency on the /api/admin router resolves the session and the role before any handler runs, and no handler contains authorisation code. The manager router mounts safe methods only.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/admin/movies with no session token returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED; with a customer token 403 FORBIDDEN; with a manager token 403 FORBIDDEN; with an admin token 200. A test enumerates every route mounted under /api/admin and asserts each resolves the one shared dependency, and a search over the admin handler modules finds no role comparison, no role string and no per-handler permission check. A test enumerates every route mounted on the manager router and asserts every method is GET or HEAD. The role is read from the user row and never from the token claims: with a valid unexpired admin token, changing that user's role column to customer makes the next request return 403 FORBIDDEN. No response on any of these paths discloses whether the object at the address exists - the 403 body is identical for an existing and a non-existent movie id.
SourceRef: P-ADM-18 E6 S4 FR-ADR-011 FR-ADR-009 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 SRC-001 §7.4

Title: Write an audit row in the same transaction as every privileged write
Description: Every privileged write inserts an audit_log row in the same database transaction as the change, so either both land or neither does. The action string comes from one closed vocabulary and the table is append-only at the database grant level.
AcceptanceCriteria: audit_log carries id, occurred_at, a non-null actor_user_id that resolves to a real user row, actor_role, action, entity_type, entity_id, jsonb before, jsonb after and request_id; no row is ever written with a null actor or a service account. POST /api/admin/screens writes exactly one row with action screen.created, before null, and actor_user_id equal to the calling admin's id. With the audit insert forced to fail, SELECT count(*) FROM screen is unchanged and the response is 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with the registry sentence for that code and no wording minted by this epic. A handler passing an action outside the vocabulary enumerated in P-ADM-19 is refused at the boundary before BEGIN, so no transaction is opened and no row of any table is written. Executed as the application database role, UPDATE audit_log SET action = 'x' raises an insufficient-privilege error and so does DELETE FROM audit_log; SELECT and INSERT succeed. A 220-seat batch through POST /api/admin/screens/{screen_id}/seats writes exactly 220 rows with action seat.created, one per seat primary key, in the same transaction as the seats. One request that changes a movie title and its display_until writes exactly two rows - one movie.updated carrying only the title in before and after, one movie.display_window_changed carrying only the window - and a request that submits two fields and changes one writes exactly one row. No before or after value anywhere contains password_hash or any field derived from it, and none contains poster bytes or card data. showtime.price_changed appears in no handler; a change to a base price writes showtime.base_price_changed.
SourceRef: P-ADM-19 E6 S4 FR-ADR-019 FR-ADR-056 SRC-001 §7.6

Title: Read and edit the venue, its name and its IANA time zone
Description: The cinema row is real data with a name and an IANA zone, and every screen carries a non-null cinema_id. There is a list and an edit; there is no create and no delete, because a second venue changes what the product is.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/admin/cinemas returns an array ordered name ASC, id ASC, each item carrying id, name, timezone, screen_count and version. PATCH /api/admin/cinemas/{cinema_id} with a matching version and a new name returns 200, increments version by exactly 1 and writes one cinema.updated audit row. One request changing both the name and the zone writes exactly two audit rows, cinema.updated and cinema.timezone_changed, in the same transaction. A timezone value the zone database does not resolve returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with nothing written and version unchanged; a name over 120 characters after trimming, or one colliding on lower(trim(name)), returns 422. A stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with nothing written and no audit row. POST /api/admin/cinemas returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED and DELETE /api/admin/cinemas/{cinema_id} returns 405, because no route is mounted for either. POST /api/admin/screens with no cinema_id in the body returns 422, so the field is never defaulted server-side to the only row.
SourceRef: P-ADM-25 E6 S4 FR-ADR-010 FR-ADR-018 SRC-003 C-2

Title: Resolve every local time from the cinema row, never from CINEMA_TIMEZONE
Description: Two places hold a zone and only one of them wins. At read time the cinema row is the sole authority; CINEMA_TIMEZONE seeds that row once and is checked at boot, and no request-path code reads it.
AcceptanceCriteria: A search of the application source for the string CINEMA_TIMEZONE finds it only in the boot configuration check and in scripts/seed.py, and in no handler, query, renderer, report or template. With the cinema row set to Asia/Kolkata and CINEMA_TIMEZONE set to UTC, a showtime stored as 2026-08-14T14:00:00Z renders as 2026-08-14 19:30, and the process logs exactly one WARNING line at boot naming cinema_id, the row zone and the variable value; /health/ready still returns 200. With the cinema row edited to Asia/Dubai, SELECT starts_at still returns 2026-08-14T14:00:00Z - not one stored instant is rewritten - and the same showtime renders as 2026-08-14 18:00. With CINEMA_TIMEZONE unset or naming a zone the database does not resolve, the process refuses to start. With no cinema row at all the process starts and logs exactly one WARNING saying the venue has not been seeded. The boot check runs no migration and issues no UPDATE against the cinema row. A showtime reaches its zone as showtime to screen to cinema.timezone; there is no timezone column on showtime and none on screen.
SourceRef: P-ADM-26 E6 S4 FR-ADR-018 FR-ADR-053 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01

Title: Create, rename and list halls
Description: A hall is created empty and in service, is renamed at any time including after showtimes exist, and is never deleted. The hall list is what the seat editor and the showtime screen are both driven from.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/screens with an existing cinema_id and a name returns 201 with is_active true, has_showtimes false and version 1, and writes one screen.created audit row. A second hall with the same name in that cinema returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and creates no row; a name differing only in case is the same refusal, because the unique index is on lower(trim(name)) within the cinema. A name of 0 or of 61 characters after trimming returns 422. PATCH /api/admin/screens/{screen_id} with a matching version renames the hall, returns 200 with version incremented by exactly 1 and writes one screen.updated audit row, and it succeeds on a hall that already carries showtime rows. GET /api/admin/screens returns every hall, in service and out of service alike, ordered name ASC, id ASC, each carrying cinema_id, is_active, seat_count_total, seat_count_in_service, has_showtimes and version. DELETE /api/admin/screens/{screen_id} returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, because no route is mounted.
SourceRef: P-ADM-13 E6 S4 FR-ADR-016 FR-ADR-012 SRC-001 §4.5

Title: Lay out a hall's seats while it has no showtimes
Description: A seat row is a real, individually sellable seat identified by (screen_id, row_label, seat_number) and drawn at (grid_row, grid_col). While a hall carries no showtime row the layout is freely editable, including deleting a seat. Two open rows sit on the seat label and neither is answered here: OPEN-SEATLABEL-01 asks whether C12 and c12 are one seat or two, and OPEN-SEATALPHA-01 asks whether the letter I may be used at all - so these criteria assert only the 1..4-letters bound the PRD states, normalise no case and ban no letter.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/screens/{screen_id}/seats accepts 1 to 500 seat objects, each carrying row_label of 1 to 4 letters, seat_number of 1 or more, grid_row and grid_col of 1 or more and a seat_category_id that exists; a 220-seat batch returns 201 with 220 items and writes 220 seat.created audit rows in the same transaction. A batch of 501 entries returns 422. A batch of five seats of which C12, C13 and C14 already exist on that hall returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED whose details carry duplicate_labels as the list C12, C13, C14 in the order submitted, whose message names all three, and after which SELECT count(*) FROM seat WHERE screen_id = :id is unchanged - so C11 and C15 were not created either. The same batch offending on one seat only renders the singular sentence; the boundary is exactly one versus two or more. Two seats submitted at one (grid_row, grid_col), or one colliding with a stored seat, return 422 with details carrying duplicate_coordinates and a message naming a count rather than a label. An unknown seat_category_id returns 422; seat_number 0 returns 422; grid_row 0 returns 422; a row_label of 5 characters or containing a digit returns 422. On a hall where SELECT count(*) FROM showtime WHERE screen_id = :id is 0: PATCH /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} changing row_label, seat_number or seat_category_id returns 200 and writes one seat.updated row, and DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} returns 204 and writes one seat.deleted row. GET /api/admin/screens/{screen_id}/seats returns the seats ordered grid_row ASC, grid_col ASC, id ASC together with has_showtimes and showtime_count. Every seat write takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the screen row before writing: a test holding that lock in a second transaction observes the seat insert block until the lock is released.
SourceRef: P-ADM-13 E6 S4 FR-ADR-016 FR-ADR-022 SRC-001 §9.3

Title: Freeze a hall's seat identity the moment any showtime exists on it
Description: Once any showtime row exists on a screen a seat may not be removed, renumbered or moved to another category. Adding a seat, toggling its service state, moving its grid coordinates and renaming the hall all stay permitted. The check is in the domain layer because the admin API is not its only caller.
AcceptanceCriteria: With SELECT count(*) FROM showtime WHERE screen_id = :id greater than 0: PATCH /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} changing row_label returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN and writes no audit row; the same for seat_number and for seat_category_id; DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN. The 409 details carry screen_id, seat_id, showtime_count and frozen_fields listing exactly row_label, seat_number and seat_category_id. In the same state, changing grid_row or grid_col returns 200, setting is_active returns 200, POST /api/admin/screens/{screen_id}/seats returns 201, and PATCH /api/admin/screens/{screen_id} renaming the hall returns 200. The state is decided by the count of showtime rows on the screen evaluated inside the transaction, not by whether they are future or booked: a hall carrying exactly one past showtime with zero bookings is frozen identically to a hall with a future sold-out one. Calling the domain function directly, bypassing the API, produces the same refusal, proving the check is not in the handler. After the freeze the only remedies are to take the mistyped seat out of service and add a correctly labelled one, or to wipe and reseed - and a test asserts no rename path exists.
SourceRef: P-ADM-14 E6 S4 FR-ADR-022 FR-ADR-024 SRC-001 §9.3

Title: Materialise a showtime's seat set at creation and never move it
Description: When a showtime is created the server writes one showtime_seat row for every seat in service on that screen at that instant, in the same transaction and under the same screen lock, and sets seat_count_at_creation to the number of rows it wrote. Nothing edits that set afterwards.
AcceptanceCriteria: On a screen with 90 seats in service, creating showtime 501 writes 90 showtime_seat rows and sets seat_count_at_creation to 90. Adding seat J11 then creating showtime 502 writes 91 rows and 91; taking J11 out of service then creating showtime 503 writes 90 rows and 90; returning J11 to service leaves SELECT count(*) FROM showtime_seat WHERE showtime_id = 503 at exactly 90, the same value it returned before the restoration, and creating showtime 504 afterwards writes 91. Showtime 501 stays at 90 rows throughout, and seat_count_at_creation is never recomputed - a PATCH on any showtime leaves both the stored integer and the row count unchanged. seat_count_at_creation always equals the number of showtime_seat rows for that showtime, asserted by a query comparing the two over every showtime and returning zero disagreements. Creating a showtime on a screen with zero seats in service returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN and writes no showtime row, so no showtime can carry a zero denominator. (showtime_id, seat_id) is unique on showtime_seat, and that index is not the oversell guard - the oversell guard stays the unique constraint on booking_seat (showtime_id, seat_id). No endpoint accepts a write to showtime_seat and any request to an address that would add or remove one returns 404 NOT_FOUND. The showtime row and its seat set commit together: with the seat-set statement forced to fail, SELECT count(*) FROM showtime is unchanged and the response is 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE.
SourceRef: P-ADM-14 E6 S4 FR-ADR-022 FR-ADR-024 SRC-002 §8.1.5

Title: Create a showtime by hand, and let nothing else create one
Description: The admin creates every showtime by choosing a film, a hall, a start, an end, a base price and optionally a format. Nothing in this system creates a showtime on its own, ever. Admin datetimes are naive local Asia/Kolkata in both directions and a zone-carrying value is refused rather than coerced.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/showtimes with movie_id, screen_id, naive local starts_at and ends_at, base_price_paise and an optional format_id returns 201 with version 1 and writes one showtime.created audit row. starts_at 2026-09-04 18:30 and ends_at 2026-09-04 20:58 for a 148-minute film store 2026-09-04T13:00:00Z and 2026-09-04T15:28:00Z, and the 201 body returns both in the same naive local form with no Z and no offset. A starts_at or ends_at carrying a Z, a +hh:mm offset or a zone name returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and is never coerced. The film need not be published: a showtime created against a draft film returns 201. A screen that is out of service returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN; a screen with zero seats in service returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN; an unknown movie_id or screen_id returns 404; ends_at at or before starts_at returns 422. A format_id naming a withdrawn format row is refused, while a showtime already carrying that format keeps it. If the film carries a display window, a starts_at outside display_from <= starts_at < display_until is refused and nothing is written, including no audit row and no showtime_seat rows; a film whose display_from and display_until are both null accepts any starts_at, which is the draft case. A showtime whose starts_at is in the past is accepted, because the seed needs about a month of history. The insert runs inside SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the screen row. A search of the repository finds no scheduler, cron entry, worker job or queue consumer that writes the showtime table; its only writers are the admin create handler, the admin edit handler and scripts/seed.py. ends_at is stored and never derived from runtime_minutes: correcting a film's runtime leaves every stored ends_at unchanged.
SourceRef: P-ADM-07 E6 S4 FR-ADR-018 FR-ADR-022 FR-ADR-037 SRC-001 §9.4 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03

Title: Refuse two overlapping showtimes on one hall
Description: Two showtimes whose half-open intervals overlap on one screen are refused, because a hall is one room with one set of seats and the unique constraint on booking_seat cannot catch it. No minimum turnaround exists in any source and none is invented - OPEN-TURNAROUND-01 is open, so a zero-gap schedule is asserted to succeed because that is what is specified.
AcceptanceCriteria: With showtime 41 on Screen 3 running 2026-09-04 18:30 to 20:58 local: a create at 20:45 to 22:40 returns 409 SHOWTIME_OVERLAP; a create at 20:58 to 22:53 returns 201, because the intervals are half-open and an end instant equal to the next start is not an overlap; a create at 21:15 to 23:10 returns 201. The 409 details carry conflicts as an array whose entries each hold showtime_id, movie_title and naive local starts_at and ends_at, and it is always an array - one entry for one conflict and two entries for two, with the interface branching on the entry count and never on the exception. The predicate is starts_at < :new_ends_at AND ends_at > :new_starts_at, run inside the same SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the screen row as the insert, and excluding the row's own id on an edit. Two overlapping creates fired concurrently against one screen produce exactly one 201 and one 409, and SELECT count(*) FROM showtime WHERE screen_id = :id increases by exactly 1. No changeover minimum is enforced anywhere: no constant, configuration value or check in the code names a turnaround figure.
SourceRef: P-ADM-08 E6 S4 FR-ADR-024 FR-ADR-018 SRC-001 §2.2 SRC-001 §7.1

Title: Edit a showtime, and list one hall's day
Description: The admin changes a showtime's film, times or base price under optimistic concurrency; the hall cannot be changed. The admin's showtime list returns one hall's one local day whole, and include_past means the advertised start instant and nothing else.
AcceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/admin/showtimes/{showtime_id} changing base_price_paise writes exactly one showtime.base_price_changed audit row; changing starts_at writes exactly one showtime.updated; one request changing both writes exactly two rows. A body carrying a screen_id different from the stored one returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and writes nothing. seat_count_at_creation and the showtime_seat row count are unchanged by every edit. Bounds are evaluated against the merged row: a PATCH carrying starts_at alone that would place it at or after the stored ends_at returns 422, and a PATCH carrying ends_at alone that would place it at or before the stored starts_at returns 422; the overlap check also runs against the merged interval, excluding this row. Editing a showtime that already has bookings changes nothing about them: booking_seat prices are unchanged and a customer already holding seats is not ejected when the start is moved earlier past its own cut-off. GET /api/admin/showtimes?screen_id=3&date=2026-09-04 at the injected request instant 2026-09-04T13:05:00Z returns showtimes 601, 602, 603 and 604 ordered by starts_at when include_past is absent or true, and returns only 604 when include_past is false - 603 starting at 13:00:00Z is omitted because the boundary is starts_at <= now, inclusive. The endpoint accepts no page or limit parameter and returns the day whole. A missing or non-integer screen_id returns 422, an unknown screen_id 404, a malformed date 422 and a non-boolean include_past 422. now is taken once per request from the injected clock and no test reads the wall clock.
SourceRef: P-ADM-09 E6 S4 FR-ADR-035 FR-ADR-042 FR-ADR-018

Title: Set a base price per showtime in integer paise
Description: Every showtime carries a non-null base_price_paise set by the admin. Currency is INR, the minor-unit ratio is 100 and it is a named configuration value. That pricing is per showtime rather than global is PROVISIONAL under OPEN-PRICE-01, and there is no business upper bound - OPEN-PRICEBOUND-01 is open and reserved, so a mistyped 2500000 for 25000 is accepted here on purpose and no sanity ceiling is invented.
AcceptanceCriteria: base_price_paise is stored as a bigint and accepted only as an integer number of paise: a decimal in the request body returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and is never rounded. A missing value returns 422; zero returns 422; a negative value returns 422; the minimum accepted value is 1. With the highest stored uplift_basis_points at 3333, base_price_paise 691770197019033 is accepted and 691770197019034 returns 422, because base_price_paise * (10000 + 3333) + 5000 must be at most 9223372036854775807. The same arithmetic ceiling appears on both showtime endpoints in the generated api/contract.json, not in prose alone, and it is written against the highest stored uplift_basis_points rather than a constant so it moves when that value moves. The interface converts rupees to paise at its boundary and the API accepts paise only. The minor-unit ratio 100 and the currency code INR each exist as one named configuration value; a search finds no bare 100 multiplying or dividing a paise quantity anywhere in the code. No business upper bound is enforced: a base_price_paise of 2500000 returns 201 and every seat on that showtime prices from it.
SourceRef: P-ADM-10 E6 S4 FR-ADR-036 FR-ADR-037 FR-ADR-038 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01

Title: Apply one percentage uplift per seat category, uniformly, with integer half-up rounding
Description: Each seat category carries an integer uplift in basis points, set once by the admin and applied uniformly across every hall and every show. One edit changes the price of every future show in the product, so it carries a version, an audit row and a confirmation stating the blast radius. Category names are ASSUMED under OPEN-SEAT-01 and the direction of SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES is PROVISIONAL under OPEN-BOOK-03; neither is treated as ruled.
AcceptanceCriteria: The seat price is seat_price_paise = (base_price_paise * (10000 + uplift_basis_points) + 5000) // 10000, integer throughout with no float and no Decimal in the expression, and with 10000 and 5000 as named constants rather than literals. At base_price_paise 25000 the three categories at 0, 1250 and 3333 basis points produce exactly 25000, 28125 and 33333 paise. The 3333 line is the deciding case and the test asserts it explicitly: the exact value is 33332.5 paise, integer half-up gives 33333 and half-even would give 33332, and the assertion is 33333. The carry is exercised in the other direction too: at base_price_paise 24999 with 3333 basis points the result is 33331, because the exact value 33331.1667 is below a half. Rounding is per seat and the total is never rounded: three seats at 3333 basis points on a base of 25000 total exactly 99999 paise and never 99998. POST /api/admin/seat-categories and PATCH /api/admin/seat-categories/{seat_category_id} accept an integer uplift_basis_points of 0 or more; a negative value returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and a non-integer returns 422; a value breaching the mirror arithmetic ceiling against the highest stored base price returns 422. A name colliding on lower(trim(name)) returns 422, and a fourth category is created successfully; no delete endpoint for a seat category exists. GET /api/admin/seat-categories returns affected_future_showtimes and evaluated_at_utc, where the count is every showtime with starts_at + SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES > evaluated_at across every hall, film and category, including halls out of service; at the injected instant 2026-08-14T09:00:00Z over the four showtimes of P-ADM-11 it returns exactly 3 with SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES at +15, and exactly 1 with the value reversed to -15. The count returned before the write and the count returned after it may legitimately differ by one and neither is compared to the other nor invalidates the confirmation. One request changing a category's name and its uplift writes exactly two audit rows, seat_category.updated and seat_category.uplift_changed. Standard is a row whose uplift is 0 and runs through the same formula with no special case in code.
SourceRef: P-ADM-11 E6 S4 FR-ADR-038 FR-ADR-037 FR-ADR-016 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-01

Title: Refuse a stale admin write, and make a write that changes nothing write nothing
Description: Every mutable admin-owned entity carries an integer version that every read returns and every write must echo. The comparison happens inside the transaction after re-reading the row, and the ordering version, validation, no-op, write is observable and decides the answer.
AcceptanceCriteria: movie, showtime, screen, seat_category and cinema each carry an integer version column; seat carries none and its PATCH endpoint accepts no version field. Every admin read that feeds a form returns version; a write with no version returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and is never treated as last-write-wins. A stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with nothing written, including no audit row; a successful write increments version by exactly 1. The ordering is asserted in three cases: a request carrying a stale version whose fields would change nothing returns 409 and not 200; a request carrying the current version and a field value that fails its bound returns 422 and not a 200 no-op, even when that value equals the stored one; and a request in which every submitted field already equals the stored value returns 200 with the row and its unchanged version, writes nothing, does not increment version and writes no audit row. A request submitting two fields of which one differs writes the change, increments version once and writes exactly one audit row for the action that actually changed. On a seat, setting is_active to the value it already holds returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN while resubmitting an unchanged grid_row returns 200 with no audit row - the exemption is scoped to is_active alone. On the poster upload the version is a second form part of the multipart body, not a header and not a query parameter, and the check order is Content-Length, then version, then content type and magic bytes, then decode and dimensions, then the S3 write - so a stale version leaves no object in the bucket. Every admin form round-trips version as a hidden value, asserted by a test that submits each admin form and finds version in the request body.
SourceRef: P-ADM-12 E6 S4 FR-ADR-035 FR-ADR-039

Title: Charge the price that was current when the hold was granted
Description: The price a customer pays is the price computed when their hold was granted and stored with the hold. An admin price edit is never blocked by an open hold and never changes what a customer already holding seats is charged.
AcceptanceCriteria: At T0 a hold on C12 (Premium, 1250 basis points) and C13 (Standard, 0) on a showtime with base_price_paise 25000 writes per-seat prices 28125 and 25000 into the Redis hold under the hold token, alongside the seat ids and an absolute expiry. At T0+40s an admin sets base_price_paise to 30000; the write returns 200, increments version and writes one showtime.base_price_changed audit row with before 25000 and after 30000 - it is never refused because a hold exists. At T0+95s the confirm reads the held prices and writes booking_seat rows with price_paise 28125 and 25000, base_price_paise_applied 25000 on both and uplift_basis_points_applied 1250 and 0, and booking.total_paise 53125; nothing is recomputed from the showtime row. A hold taken at T0+120s on the same two seats is quoted 33750 and 30000. With SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS at 180, the held prices are gone at T0+181s and no cleanup job runs. Every instant in this scenario comes from the injected clock; no test reads the wall clock. The confirm transaction takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the showtime row for read consistency, and a test asserts that lock does not block the admin price edit.
SourceRef: P-ADM-12 E6 S4 FR-ADR-039 FR-ADR-027 SRC-001 §5.2.4

Title: Take a seat out of service and return it
Description: A seat that must come out of service is marked inactive and never deleted, in either hall state. It stops being offered on showtimes created afterwards and changes nothing about a showtime that already exists.
AcceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} with is_active false returns 200 and writes one seat.deactivated audit row with before is_active true and after is_active false; with is_active true it writes seat.reactivated. Setting is_active to the value the seat already holds returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN with the already-in-that-state sentence, not a 200 no-op. The write takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the seat's screen row, so it cannot land half inside a concurrent showtime creation. A retired seat is absent from the showtime_seat set of every showtime created after the change and present on the set of every showtime created before it: SELECT count(*) FROM showtime_seat WHERE showtime_id = :existing is unchanged by the toggle, and seat_count_at_creation on every existing showtime is unchanged. A seat already sold on an existing showtime stays sold - SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE seat_id = :id is unchanged by the toggle - and the seat row still resolves for every past booking with its original row_label and seat_number. Returning a seat to service does not add it to any showtime created while it was out of service. No endpoint reachable from this action cancels a booking, refunds anybody or removes a seat from a customer who has paid for it.
SourceRef: P-ADM-15 E6 S4 FR-ADR-022 FR-ADR-012

Title: Withdraw a hall without cancelling anything
Description: A retired hall is marked inactive and never deleted. It accepts no new showtimes and it cancels nothing: existing showtimes, seats and bookings all stay and all still resolve.
AcceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/admin/screens/{screen_id} with is_active false and a matching version returns 200, increments version by exactly 1 and writes one screen.deactivated audit row; is_active true writes screen.reactivated. POST /api/admin/showtimes naming a withdrawn screen returns 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN. SELECT count(*) over showtime, seat and booking_seat for that screen is identical before and after the withdrawal, and a receipt already issued still names the hall. A withdrawn hall still appears wherever a historical booking or a dashboard figure names it, because the record points at the row and not at a name string. A stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with nothing written. DELETE /api/admin/screens/{screen_id} returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, because no route is mounted; the screen row is never deleted at any time. Withdrawing a hall is not withdrawing a showtime, and the confirmation copy says so.
SourceRef: P-ADM-16 E6 S4 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-019

Title: Create a manager account and assign it halls
Description: The admin creates a read-only manager account with no password and assigns it one or more halls through a join table. That the manager role exists at all is PROVISIONAL under SRC-003 C-1; whether a manager may buy a ticket is OPEN-MGRBOOK-01 and is not answered here. The product sends no invitation and that gap is written down rather than filled.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/managers with an email and screen_ids creates a user row with role manager and no usable password, one manager_screen_assignment row per screen, one manager.created audit row and one manager.screen_assigned row per assignment, all in one transaction, and returns 201 with the id, email and assigned screen ids. A body carrying a role property returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID and creates nothing, so no endpoint can be induced to create an admin; a search of the routes finds no endpoint that creates an admin account at all. An email already used by any account returns 422; a malformed address returns 422; a screen_id that does not exist returns 422; a duplicate screen_id in the array returns 422. An empty screen_ids array is accepted and returns 201, and that manager's dashboard is empty rather than an error. PUT /api/admin/managers/{user_id}/screens replaces the complete set, writing one manager.screen_assigned row per addition and one manager.screen_unassigned row per removal; the unassignment row's entity_type is manager_screen_assignment, its entity_id is the primary key the removed row held, its before carries user_id and screen_id and its after is null - and nothing joins that entity_id back to the live table. A target user that exists but is not a manager returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED. (user_id, screen_id) is unique on manager_screen_assignment, and no check constraint, trigger or application rule enforces the number two per hall. GET /api/admin/managers returns the accounts ordered email ASC, user_id ASC with has_signed_in derived as last_signed_in_at IS NOT NULL and not stored. The create writes no outbox_message row and enqueues no SES message: SELECT count(*) FROM outbox_message is unchanged across the request. No audit row's before or after ever contains password_hash or any field derived from it.
SourceRef: P-ADM-17 E6 S4 FR-ADR-011 FR-ADR-009 FR-ADR-050 SRC-003 C-1 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03

Title: Withdraw instead of deleting, everywhere
Description: Deletion is not in this system's vocabulary. Withdrawal replaces it per entity, exactly two deletions exist in the whole epic, and the absence of a delete route is itself the control.
AcceptanceCriteria: A test enumerating every mounted route finds exactly one DELETE under /api/admin - DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} - and no DELETE route for movie, showtime, screen, cinema or any lookup table. DELETE against any of those addresses returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, rendered through the product's single error envelope by a global method-not-allowed handler rather than by a mounted route, with the one generic entity-blind sentence and no entity-naming wording. The two permitted deletions are a seat on a screen with zero showtime rows and a manager_screen_assignment row; a source search over the admin handler and repository modules finds DELETE statements against those two tables only. A query over information_schema.referential_constraints returns zero rows with delete_rule = 'CASCADE' on any foreign key on a path that can reach a booking; the default is RESTRICT. After withdrawing a film, a hall and a seat, every historical booking still resolves to the same movie, screen and seat rows with their original values. No pruning job, retention window, scheduled task, cron entry or worker job that deletes anything exists in the repository. Storage growing without limit is stated in the runbook as a figure to watch and no retention window is implemented.
SourceRef: P-ADM-20 E6 S4 FR-ADR-012 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-02 SRC-001 §7.6

Title: Ship no way to withdraw a showtime
Description: Withdrawing a showtime that already has paid bookings is OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01, reserved as money and irreversible. v1 therefore has no such capability at all, and this story encodes that absence rather than an answer.
AcceptanceCriteria: A test enumerating every route under /api/admin finds no DELETE on a showtime, no POST to a withdraw or cancel path and no PATCH field that sets a withdrawal or cancellation state. A query over information_schema.columns for table showtime returns no withdrawn_at column and no cancellation-state column. Any request to a withdraw-showtime address returns 404 NOT_FOUND with the generic page-does-not-exist sentence, the same answer as any other address that does not exist. The showtimes screen renders no withdraw control and no disabled one, and its standing copy says a showtime is never deleted and v1 has no way to cancel one. The booking table keeps status and cancelled_at, and a search finds no v1 endpoint, handler or query that reads or writes either outside the model definition and the migration. No refund path, no customer notification and no copy string for either exists anywhere in the code or the published wording.
SourceRef: P-ADM-21 E6 S4 FR-ADR-023 FR-ADR-013 SRC-003 OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01

Title: Create and list the lookup vocabularies a film is built from
Description: A film cannot be created until a language, a certification and at least one genre row exists, and a customer's format filter cannot return anything until format rows exist. One generic admin surface creates and lists all four vocabularies.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/lookups/{kind} accepts exactly the four kinds language, certification, genre and format; any fifth path segment returns 404 NOT_FOUND and not 422, because it is an address that does not exist. A valid create returns 201 with is_active true and writes one audit row with action language.created, certification.created, genre.created or format.created, before null and after carrying the name. A name that is empty or whitespace only returns 422, and one over 60 characters after trimming returns 422. A second row whose lower(trim(name)) matches an existing active row in that vocabulary returns 422 with the every-entry-needs-its-own-name sentence; one that matches a withdrawn row returns 422 with the restore-that-entry-instead sentence, because withdrawn rows participate in the unique index. The same string in two vocabularies is accepted: Drama as a genre and Drama as a format are two unrelated rows and neither collides. The stored value keeps the case the admin typed and only leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; the lowercased trimmed form is the comparison key and is never displayed. A body carrying is_active or id returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID, rejected and never dropped. GET /api/admin/lookups/{kind} returns items with id, name, is_active, created_at and reference_count, ordered name ASC, id ASC, with include_withdrawn defaulting to false; reference_count counts every referencing row regardless of visibility, so a draft film counts and a showtime past its sales cut-off counts. DELETE at any of these addresses returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, and there is no edit endpoint. On a migrated but unseeded database all four vocabularies are empty and the film form renders an explanation in place of each empty select rather than an empty dropdown.
SourceRef: P-ADM-23 E6 S4 FR-ADR-021 FR-ADR-012 SRC-001 §5.1.3

Title: Withdraw a lookup entry from future use, and restore it
Description: A lookup entry that should no longer be offered is marked inactive. It is never deleted and never renamed, because a rename would change what every past film says it was.
AcceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/admin/lookups/{kind}/{id} with is_active false returns 200 and, in one transaction, writes is_active and one audit row with action language.withdrawn, certification.withdrawn, genre.withdrawn or format.withdrawn, before is_active true and after is_active false, carrying the acting user and the request id; the same request with true writes the matching restored action. The entry is absent from the admin form options on the next request, and every film already referencing it is untouched: the film still renders that language on every customer surface and a customer filtering by it still finds the film. A body carrying name returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID, so a rename can never be silently accepted. is_active missing or not a boolean returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED. is_active already holding the submitted value returns 200 with nothing written and no audit row. An unknown kind and an unknown id return an identical 404 NOT_FOUND, so the response does not reveal which ids exist. DELETE at this address returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED. Correcting a typo is two actions and both stay on the record: withdrawing the wrong entry, then creating the right one and repointing the film, leaving both audit rows in place.
SourceRef: P-ADM-24 E6 S4 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-019 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-02

Title: Create a film by hand as a draft
Description: The admin types every film into the system. The row is created as a draft with no poster and no publication instant, invisible to every customer and guest, and it can already be pointed at by a showtime. There is no external API, no import, no upsert and no scheduled trigger.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/movies returns 201 with published_at null, poster_present false and version 1, and in one transaction inserts the movie row, the movie_genre join rows and one movie.created audit row with before null. A title of 0 or of 201 characters after trimming returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED; a synopsis over 4000 characters returns 422; runtime_minutes missing, zero, negative or non-integer returns 422. A language_id or certification_id that does not exist returns 422; genre_ids empty, over 10 entries, carrying a duplicate, or naming an id that does not exist returns 422. A body carrying published_at or poster_object_key returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID - rejected, never dropped - and creates nothing. Title is not unique: two films with the same title both return 201. On a migrated but unseeded database the create cannot succeed until at least one language, one certification and one genre row exist. GET /api/admin/movies pages ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC with limit defaulting to 50 and returns total; display_from and display_until come back as naive local Asia/Kolkata values carrying no Z and no offset, while published_at stays an ISO-8601 instant with its zone. A search of the repository finds no external movie API client, no import job, no upsert by an external id and no scheduled trigger that writes the movie table.
SourceRef: P-ADM-01 E6 S4 FR-ADR-021 FR-ADR-061 SRC-001 §5.1.1 SRC-001 §E E-4 SRC-003 OPEN-TMDB-01

Title: Edit a film under optimistic concurrency
Description: The admin changes any authored field of a draft or published film, echoing the version they read. Editing a published film takes effect on every customer surface immediately and changes nothing about any booking.
AcceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/admin/movies/{movie_id} with a matching version applies the changes, returns 200 with the new version incremented by exactly 1, and writes one movie.updated audit row whose before and after carry only the fields that changed and their prior and new values. A stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with nothing written, including no audit row; an absent version returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED. Every field bound of the create applies unchanged on the edit. An unknown body property returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID. A repeat of the identical request returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT, because the first attempt incremented version, and no second edit is applied. Editing a published film's title makes every cached listing that could contain the film unreachable once the write commits: the first customer listing read issued after the 200 returns the new title and never the pre-edit one, with no wait and no cache expiry involved. A booking against the edited film is unchanged: its film reference is a foreign key to this row and its money is snapshotted on booking_seat, so SELECT price_paise FROM booking_seat for that booking is identical before and after the edit.
SourceRef: P-ADM-02 E6 S4 FR-ADR-035 FR-ADR-021 FR-ADR-019

Title: Upload a poster to private object storage
Description: One image file per film, validated and uploaded to a private S3 bucket, never written to the container's disk and served only through a short-lived presigned redirect. There is no deletion path for a poster: a replaced object stays in a bucket with a finite 5 GB allowance that nothing watches, and that is stated rather than solved.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/movies/{movie_id}/poster is multipart/form-data carrying exactly one file part and a version form part, and the checks run in the order Content-Length, version, declared content type and magic bytes, decode and pixel dimensions, then the S3 PutObject, then the movie row and its audit row in one transaction. Content-Length absent returns 422; Content-Length above 2097152 bytes returns 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE and the body is never read. A declared content type outside image/jpeg, image/png and image/webp returns 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, as does a declared type that does not match the file's leading bytes, as does a file that will not decode. Pixel dimensions outside 200 by 300 to 4000 by 6000 return 422. Zero file parts or two file parts return 422. A missing version form part returns 422. A stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT before any byte is streamed, and listing the bucket's poster prefix afterwards shows no new object. A success stores the object at posters/{movie_id}/{random} with a server-generated key that never uses the client's filename, sets poster_object_key inside the transaction after re-reading and re-comparing version, increments version, and writes one movie.poster_uploaded audit row on the first upload and movie.poster_replaced on every later one, carrying the previous key in before. The previous S3 object is not deleted, and an audit row's before value still resolves to a real image. GET /api/admin/movies/{movie_id}/poster returns 302 to a presigned GET URL valid for one hour; the bucket has no public-read policy and nothing is hotlinked; a draft film's poster is reachable only through this admin endpoint. A retryable S3 failure - a 5xx or a throttle - returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, and a non-retryable refusal returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with the registry sentence and a request id to quote. Nothing is written to the container's local disk at any point during the request, asserted by a test that watches the working directory and the temp directory for new files. No metric, alarm or endpoint reports the bucket's size, and no lifecycle or deletion path exists.
SourceRef: P-ADM-03 E6 S4 FR-ADR-061 FR-ADR-012 SRC-002 §7.3 SRC-002 §4.9

Title: Set a film's display window in naive local time
Description: The display window is the second of the two gates a customer sees through. Both instants are typed by the admin as local Asia/Kolkata values, stored converted to UTC, and returned in the same naive local form they were accepted in. display_from is inclusive and display_until is exclusive.
AcceptanceCriteria: display_from and display_until are accepted as naive local Asia/Kolkata values; a value carrying a Z, a +hh:mm offset or a zone name returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and is never coerced. Entering display_from 2026-09-04 00:00 and display_until 2026-10-02 00:00 stores 2026-09-03T18:30:00Z and 2026-10-01T18:30:00Z, and reading the film back returns both in naive local form with no Z and no offset. A customer at 2026-10-01T18:29:59Z sees the film and a customer at 2026-10-01T18:30:00Z does not, so the last visible local day is 1 Oct 2026.
