The server adds no day, rounds nothing to midnight and derives neither end from the other. display_until at or before display_from returns 422 with nothing written, no audit row and no version increment. The bound is evaluated against the merged row: with display_from 2026-09-01 00:00 and display_until 2026-09-30 00:00 stored, a PATCH carrying only display_from 2026-10-15 00:00 returns 422 and version is unchanged; a PATCH carrying only display_until can fail the same way. A window entirely in the past is accepted. A successful window change writes exactly one movie.display_window_changed audit row carrying both instants before and after, and a request also changing the title writes a second row, movie.updated. The window may be changed on a published film without unpublishing it, and the film stays published throughout.
SourceRef: P-ADM-04 E6 S4 FR-ADR-021 FR-ADR-018 SRC-003 OPEN-ROLE-01

Title: Publish a film only when it is complete
Description: Publication and the display window are two separate gates and both must pass before a customer sees a film. A film cannot be published without a poster or without a window, checked at publish time inside the transaction rather than by a column constraint.
AcceptanceCriteria: Visibility is published_at IS NOT NULL AND now >= display_from AND now < display_until, computed in the cinema's zone against the injected clock, and a search finds exactly one definition of that predicate and no second copy anywhere. POST /api/admin/movies/{movie_id}/publish with a matching version sets published_at from the injected clock, increments version by exactly 1 and writes one movie.published audit row with before published_at null and after the instant. poster_object_key null returns 409 PUBLISH_BLOCKED with the upload-a-poster-first sentence; display_from or display_until null returns 409 PUBLISH_BLOCKED with the set-the-dates sentence; an already-published film returns 409 PUBLISH_BLOCKED; a stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT. Both preconditions are re-read inside the transaction, so clearing the window between the form load and the submit still refuses. A published film whose window has not opened returns no rows to any customer or guest listing, and the editor states which of the two gates currently passes, never one combined live flag. A body carrying an unknown property returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID.
SourceRef: P-ADM-05 E6 S4 FR-ADR-021 FR-ADR-061 SRC-001 §E E-8

Title: Withdraw a film without deleting anything
Description: Unpublishing sets published_at back to null. The film leaves every customer surface immediately; the row, its showtimes and every booking against it stay and still resolve. This is what deleting a film means in FrontRow.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/movies/{movie_id}/unpublish with a matching version sets published_at to null, increments version by exactly 1 and writes one movie.unpublished audit row carrying the prior instant in before. A film that is not published returns 409 PUBLISH_BLOCKED; a stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with nothing written. SELECT count(*) FROM showtime and SELECT count(*) FROM booking for that film are identical before and after the withdrawal, and a customer's booking list and receipt still name the real title, poster and runtime because they read the movie row directly and not through the visibility predicate. The write makes every cached listing that could carry the film unreachable once it commits: the first customer listing read issued after the 200 does not contain the film, with no wait and no cache expiry involved. Withdrawing a film that has future showtimes with confirmed bookings returns 200 and refunds nobody, cancels nothing and changes no booking row. No delete endpoint exists for a film and DELETE /api/admin/movies/{movie_id} returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, because no route is mounted.
SourceRef: P-ADM-06 E6 S4 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-021 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-02

Title: Keep licensed content out of the product
Description: OPEN-ATTRIB-01 is open and reserved as a legal question: if the posters and titles the client supplies come from a licensed source, an attribution obligation applies. Until it closes, no licensed image, title or synopsis enters this product from the build session. This story encodes that standing constraint on what is written, not an answer to the licence question.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every film title in scripts/seed.py matches the obvious-placeholder pattern DEMO MOVIE nn, and every seeded lookup, cinema and hall name is an equally obvious placeholder; a review of the seed, the test fixtures, the documentation examples and the screenshots finds no real film title, poster, synopsis or brand. The seeded poster is a single asset committed to this repository, shared by every seeded film, carrying no artwork and no text readable as a title. The seed fetches no image from anywhere: a search finds no HTTP client, URL or download call in scripts/seed.py. No provenance or attribution column is added to the movie row and no attribution check exists on the poster-serving endpoint. Nothing in the running system enforces this and no validation is added, because the admin may type any title they like and the material is the client's - the constraint binds the build session and not the product.
SourceRef: P-ADM-22 E6 S4 FR-ADR-007 FR-ADR-067 SRC-003 OPEN-ATTRIB-01

Title: Browse the catalogue and read the seat map
Description: The whole public read path for one cinema with six halls: what is playing, filtering and sorting, a film and its showtimes, and the seat map as a thing to look at. Every surface in it is reachable with no account and nothing in it takes a seat out of sale.

Title: Gate every movie-addressed read on publication and the display window
Description: A film is customer-visible only when published_at IS NOT NULL and display_from <= T < display_until, evaluated at read time from the injected clock because nothing sweeps. The three showtime-addressed and poster endpoints apply no movie gate today; whether they should is OPEN-BRWVIS-01, which is OPEN and reserved, and this story does not answer it - it asserts only the specified behaviour.
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed one movie with published_at=2026-08-10T11:04:22+05:30, display_from=2026-08-14T00:00:00+05:30, display_until=2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30. With the clock injected: GET /api/movies returns it at T=2026-08-14T00:00:00+05:30 and at T=2026-08-20T23:59:59+05:30, and does not return it at T=2026-08-13T23:59:59+05:30 or at T=2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30 (4 assertions, exclusive upper bound); the same row with published_at NULL is absent at all four instants; the same row with display_from NULL, and again with display_until NULL, is absent at all four instants with no COALESCE in the query; at an instant where it is excluded, GET /api/movies/{that id} returns 404 NOT_FOUND with a response body byte-identical to GET /api/movies/{an id that has never existed}, and the rendered copy is 'That movie is not showing.'; GET /api/movies/0 and GET /api/movies/abc return 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and no SQL is executed; the SQL emitted for GET /api/movies contains the two-gate predicate (assert on the compiled statement, no post-fetch filtering in Python); and at T=2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30 GET /api/movies/{id}/poster returns 302, GET /api/showtimes/{a showtime of that film} returns 200 and GET /api/showtimes/{that id}/seatmap returns 200 - the three ungated endpoints.
SourceRef: P-BRW-01 E1 S4 FR-ADR-021 FR-ADR-018 R-BRW-06

Title: Carry the six details a customer chooses between films on
Description: Every movie in the listing carries poster, synopsis, running time, certification, language and genre, plus its exclusive display_until, which is the field the listing date strip is bounded by. Certification and language are lookup objects of {id, name}; there is no code field anywhere.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/movies returns each element with exactly the keys id, title, synopsis, runtime_minutes, certification, language, genres, poster_url, display_until and no others; certification and language are objects with exactly the keys id and name, and the string 'code' appears nowhere in the response; genres is an array of {id, name} and is exactly [] for a movie with no movie_genre row, and the rendered metadata row then contains no genre segment and no word 'unknown'; poster_url equals /api/movies/{id}/poster for every element and contains neither 's3' nor any third-party host; display_until is a string ending '+05:30' and is non-null on every element of the array; a movie whose poster object is missing from S3 still appears in the array and its card renders the perforation motif with the title inside it and no words; a synopsis of 900 characters is returned in full and the card element has a 3-line clamp while /movies/{id} renders it unclamped.
SourceRef: P-BRW-02 E1 S4 SRC-001 §5.1.1 FR-ADR-021 R-BRW-02

Title: Order the listing newest first, by published_at descending with id descending as the tiebreak
Description: With no sort chosen the listing is published_at DESC, id DESC. The sort parameter exists because a customer-chosen sort is required, but only one value is defined; which further sorts exist is OPEN-SORT-01, which is OPEN, so no menu is invented and no sort control renders.
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed A id=7 published_at=2026-08-12T10:00:00+05:30; B id=11 and C id=12 both published_at=2026-08-14T09:00:00+05:30; D id=13 published_at=NULL. GET /api/movies returns exactly the ids [12, 11, 7] in that order, and returns the identical order on 10 consecutive requests (the tiebreak is deterministic, not incidental); D is absent; GET /api/movies?sort=newest returns the identical array; GET /api/movies?sort=title and ?sort=price return 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with the copy 'That sort option is not available.'; the sort value never reaches SQL as an interpolated string (assert the parameter is bound to an enum of one member); applying ?language_id={the language of A and C} returns [12, 7] - filtering narrows the set and does not reorder it; and the rendered listing contains no sort control of any kind.
SourceRef: P-BRW-03 E1 S4 FR-ADR-021 R-BRW-05

Title: Filter the listing by cinema, date, language and format, with one showtime satisfying every showtime filter at once
Description: The four filters combine with AND. language_id is a movie attribute applied to the movie row; date, cinema_id and format_id are showtime attributes and must be satisfied by a single EXISTS over one showtime, never by three independent existence tests. An absent date means every date and does not default to today.
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed one visible film with exactly two showtimes: showtime 1 on 2026-08-17 in Hall 4 with format 2D, showtime 2 on 2026-08-18 in Hall 4 with format 3D. GET /api/movies?date=2026-08-17 returns count 1; ?format_id={3D} returns count 1; ?date=2026-08-17&format_id={3D} returns count 0 with movies [] and the screen renders 'Nothing is showing for the chosen filters.' plus a control reading 'Clear filters'; GET /api/movies with no date returns count 1 (no date predicate is applied and it does not default to today); ?date=2026-08-14 compiles to the predicate starts_at >= 2026-08-13T18:30:00Z AND starts_at < 2026-08-14T18:30:00Z, so a showtime starting 23:45 local on 2026-08-14 is included and one starting 00:10 local on 2026-08-15 is not; the zone name is read from the cinema row and the string 'Asia/Kolkata' is not hardcoded in the query builder; ?date=14-08-2026 and ?date=2026-08-14T00:00:00 return 422 with 'That date is not valid.'; ?language_id=0 and ?format_id=abc return 422 with 'That filter is not valid.'; ?language_id=999999 (well-formed, no such row) returns 200 with count 0; and ?page=2 is ignored and returns the full result.
SourceRef: P-BRW-04 E1 S4 SRC-001 §5.1.3 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-018 R-BRW-03

Title: Serve the filter vocabularies as rows in use, and render a control only at two or more values
Description: GET /api/reference returns cinemas, languages, formats and certifications, each holding only rows referenced by something the caller can currently see. A control renders only when its array holds two or more entries - absent, never disabled and never shown with one option. A reference outage and an empty vocabulary render the same three absences, so exactly one published line separates them.
AcceptanceCriteria: Against the seeded catalogue (3 languages, 2 formats, 1 cinema, 2 certifications, 8 visible films, formats carried by showtimes): GET /api/reference returns languages length 3, formats length 2, cinemas length 1, certifications length 2, and no genres key; the listing then renders a Language control and a Format control and no Cinema control; reseed with 1 language and the Language control is absent from the DOM with no explanatory text anywhere on the page; a lookup row with is_active=false that a currently visible film still carries is present in its array and filtering by its id returns that film; a language row carried by no currently visible film is absent from the array; a format whose only showtime is past its sales cut-off is absent from formats; when GET /api/reference returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE while GET /api/movies returns 200, the listing renders every card, renders no Language, Format or Cinema control, still renders the date strip and 'Clear filters', a filter already present in the URL is still applied by the server, and exactly one line reads 'Filters are unavailable right now.'; on day one with 0 languages and 0 formats the same three controls are absent and that line is NOT present.
SourceRef: P-BRW-04 E1 S4 E1 S6 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-010 R-BRW-03

Title: Bound the listing date strip at the day before the latest display_until in the filtered response
Description: The listing has no chosen movie, so its strip runs from today in Asia/Kolkata to the day before max(display_until) over the array the last response carried - the day before, because the bound is exclusive. It bounds the range and does not promise a showtime on every day inside it. No horizon constant exists anywhere.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the clock injected at 2026-08-14T10:00:00+05:30 and a listing whose display_until values are 2026-08-19T00:00:00+05:30 and 2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30, the strip renders 'Any date' selected plus exactly 7 day buttons, 2026-08-14 through 2026-08-20 inclusive, and no button for 2026-08-21; applying a language filter that leaves only the film ending 2026-08-19 re-renders the strip with exactly 5 day buttons ending 2026-08-18; if 2026-08-20 was the selected day when that filter is applied, the selection returns to 'Any date', the next request carries no date parameter, and the polite live region announces 'The date filter was cleared. Nothing in this list is showing on that day.'; clearing filters restores the 7 buttons; when movies is [] no strip element exists in the DOM at all in both empty states, and the empty-with-no-filters state renders 'Nothing is showing right now.' while the empty-with-filters state renders 'Nothing is showing for the chosen filters.' with 'Clear filters'; every day button is labelled in the form 'Fri 15 Aug' and no button anywhere reads 'Today' or 'Tomorrow'; pressing a day inside the range on which nothing is scheduled renders the ordinary 'Nothing is showing for the chosen filters.' state and is not treated as an error.
SourceRef: P-BRW-04 E1 S5 FR-ADR-018 R-BRW-03

Title: Let anyone browse the whole read path with no account
Description: Every endpoint in this epic is public and no response varies by who is reading it. The stop is at the hold, which is lane E2's endpoint and returns 401 to an unauthenticated caller; this story asserts the read half and the guest rendering, not the hold itself.
AcceptanceCriteria: With no cookie and no Authorization header: GET /api/movies, GET /api/movies/{id}, GET /api/movies/{id}/poster, GET /api/showtimes?movie_id={id}, GET /api/showtimes/{id}, GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap and GET /api/reference all return their success status (200, or 302 for the poster); a test enumerates the mounted routes for those paths and asserts each has an empty dependency list - a read route in this epic carrying an auth dependency fails the test; the /seatmap response body for an anonymous caller and for a signed-in customer is byte-identical (compared as bytes on the same seeded showtime at the same injected instant); a guest rendering the seat map has zero elements in the held_by_me treatment and the primary action reads exactly 'Sign in to hold these seats'; and a signed-in customer whose token has expired keeps receiving 200 from every read above, because the read path reads no token.
SourceRef: P-BRW-05 E1 S4 SRC-001 §4.1 FR-ADR-014 R-BRW-01

Title: List every showtime for a chosen movie and date in Asia/Kolkata
Description: Choosing a movie and a date lists every showtime for that movie on that local day across all six halls, ordered by start time, with the hall and the base price against each. Nothing is omitted for being nearly full, nearly over or already closed. An absent date defaults to today in the cinema zone - the opposite of the listing rule, deliberately.
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed a visible movie with three showtimes on 2026-08-15 at 11:00, 14:30 and 19:30 local across two halls. GET /api/showtimes?movie_id={id}&date=2026-08-15 returns exactly 3 showtimes ordered by starts_at ASC then id ASC; each element carries exactly id, starts_at, ends_at, sales_close_at, sales_closed, screen{id,name}, cinema{id,name}, format ({id,name} or null) and base_price_paise as an integer; every instant string in the response ends '+05:30' and no instant in the response ends 'Z'; base_price_paise is an int and never a float or a formatted string; ends_at equals the stored column and is not starts_at plus runtime_minutes (assert with a showtime whose stored ends_at differs from that sum); with the injected clock at 2026-08-14T19:05:00Z and no date parameter, the response field date is '2026-08-15' and the returned showtimes are the 15th's; a movie failing either visibility gate returns 404 NOT_FOUND rendering 'That movie is not showing.' with a link reading 'Back to what is showing'; date=2026-8-15 returns 422 'That date is not valid.'; and a date with no showtimes returns 200 with an empty array rendering 'No showtimes on this date.'
SourceRef: P-BRW-06 E1 S4 SRC-001 §5.1.4 FR-ADR-018 R-BRW-04

Title: Name the next date the customer can actually buy on, or nothing at all
Description: next_date_with_showtimes is the earliest local date meeting all four conditions at once and met by ONE showtime: strictly after the requested date, inside the display window, holding a showtime whose sales have not closed, and that same showtime matching every filter the request carried. Null when no such date exists, and the button is then not rendered.
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed a visible movie with display_until=2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30 and showtimes: 2026-08-15 19:30 format 2D; 2026-08-16 11:00 format 3D only; 2026-08-17 09:00 format 2D. With SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=+15 and the clock at 2026-08-15T21:00:00+05:30: GET /api/showtimes?movie_id={id}&date=2026-08-15 returns the 19:30 showtime with sales_closed true (the list is NOT emptied) and next_date_with_showtimes '2026-08-16', and the screen renders the closed showtime plus a button reading 'Next: Sun 16 Aug'; the same request with format_id={2D} returns next_date_with_showtimes '2026-08-17', proving conditions 3 and 4 are met by one showtime rather than by different ones; a request with date=2026-08-17 returns next_date_with_showtimes null, the copy 'No showtimes for this movie.' renders and no next-date button element exists in the DOM; a request with date=2026-08-19 never searches past 2026-08-21 (assert the generated query has an upper bound of display_until and no horizon constant appears in the source); and the requested date itself is never returned in the field even when it holds an open showtime.
SourceRef: P-BRW-06 P-BRW-07 E1 S4 E1 S6 R-BRW-04

Title: Show a closed showtime, marked closed, rather than hiding it
Description: sales_close_at is derived at read time from starts_at plus a signed SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES and is never stored. A closed showtime is still listed and still opens its seat map, marked closed. The direction of the offset is PROVISIONAL under SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-03 - this story asserts the specified +15 reading and asserts that reversing the sign is a configuration change and nothing else.
AcceptanceCriteria: With SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=+15 and a showtime at starts_at=2026-08-14T19:30:00+05:30: the response carries sales_close_at '2026-08-14T19:45:00+05:30'; at injected T=2026-08-14T19:44:59+05:30 sales_closed is false and at T=2026-08-14T19:45:00+05:30 sales_closed is true (the boundary instant is closed); with SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=-15 and no other change the same showtime carries sales_close_at '2026-08-14T19:15:00+05:30' and sales_closed true at T=19:20:00+05:30; no column named sales_close_at exists in the schema (assert against the migration metadata); with SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES unset or set to 'fifteen' the process exits non-zero at boot with a message naming the variable and never falls back to 15; a closed showtime button renders the word 'Closed', is absent from the tab order and does not navigate, and its accessible name ends 'sales closed'; opening /showtimes/{id} for a closed showtime returns the full seat map with every seat unselectable and the banner exactly 'Sales for this showtime have closed.'; and that string occurs in exactly one place in the frontend source (no variant in the seat lane's screen file).
SourceRef: P-BRW-07 E1 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-03 FR-ADR-042 R-BRW-04

Title: Serve the seat map as the real layout of the hall, scoped to this showtime's frozen seat set
Description: The map returns this showtime's seat set as materialised at showtime creation, with grid coordinates separate from the printed row and number, aisles as the absence of a seat, and a required is_active boolean for a seat retired since. screen.rows and cols are derived per response as max(gr) and max(gc) over that seat set, never over the screen's current seats. Hall sizes are ASSUMED under SRC-003 OPEN-SCALE-02 and no assertion here depends on the exact size.
AcceptanceCriteria: For a seeded showtime in a hall whose seat set has 220 seats with max(gr)=12 and max(gc)=22: GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap returns screen.rows 12 and screen.cols 22; seats has length 220 and is ordered gr ASC then gc ASC, so the seat labelled A-2 precedes A-12 in the array; a seat carries row 'C', num 12, gr 3 and gc 14 as four separate fields; no object is present for an aisle coordinate and no seat carries a 'blocked' state; the showtime object on this response has exactly the keys id, starts_at, sales_close_at, sales_closed; every seat carries is_active as a boolean and a seat object missing it fails response-model validation rather than serialising; adding a seat to the hall after the showtime was created leaves this showtime's screen.cols unchanged and the new seat absent from seats; retiring one seat returns it with is_active false and its unchanged state; retiring all 220 returns 200 with 220 seats, is_active false on every one, the full grid drawn in the out-of-service treatment, nothing selectable and the banner exactly 'None of the seats in this hall are available.'; a showtime whose seat set has zero rows returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR rendering 'The seat map could not be loaded.' plus a request id; showtime id 999999 returns 404 'That showtime could not be found.' and /seatmap for a non-integer id returns 422 with no query executed.
SourceRef: P-BRW-08 E1 S4 E1 S6 SRC-001 §5.2.1 FR-ADR-016 R-SEAT-01 R-SEAT-07

Title: Serve three objective seat states and let the client compute the fourth
Description: The server sends available, held and sold only, because one cached payload serves every viewer; held_by_me is computed on the client by intersecting the response with the caller's own hold token. An out-of-service seat is a separate boolean, not a fifth state, because a retired seat can also be sold. Every state carries a non-colour cue.
AcceptanceCriteria: For showtime 812 with a booking row for (812, C-12), a live Redis lock for (812, C-13) and nothing for C-14: GET /api/showtimes/812/seatmap returns state 'sold' for C-12, 'held' for C-13 and 'available' for C-14, and no element of seats carries any other state value (the response model rejects a fourth); two callers with different sessions receive byte-identical bodies for the same request at the same injected instant; a client holding a hold token containing C-13 renders exactly one held_by_me cell and a client with no token renders zero; the four rendered states carry four distinct non-colour marks in the DOM - none, one horizontal bar, diagonal hatching, a tick - and none is distinguished by colour alone; a seat with is_active false renders with a 1px dashed border and no fill, keeps its number, keeps its place in the arrow-key grid, has an accessible name ending 'out of service', and does not activate on Enter or Space in any state including sold; the legend renders five swatches, the fifth reading 'Out of service'; when every seat is sold the full grid renders plus the banner 'Every seat for this showtime is sold.' and no empty state is rendered; and a seat that changes state between two polls keeps a 2px ring for the change duration, held statically under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
SourceRef: P-BRW-09 E1 S4 SRC-001 §5.2.2 FR-ADR-045 FR-ADR-030 R-SEAT-01 R-SEAT-06

Title: Send the category and the already-rounded price of every seat
Description: Category price is base_price_paise plus a fixed percentage uplift in basis points, rounded half-up once per seat by the server. The same integer is sent on the category and on every seat, so the client sums integers and performs no rounding of its own. Money is integer paise on the wire and a formatted string only at render. The three category names are ASSUMED under SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-01.
AcceptanceCriteria: With base_price_paise=24999 and categories at 0, 1250 and 3333 basis points, GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap returns categories price_paise of exactly 24999, 28124 and 33331 - the 3333 bp case rounds DOWN from an exact 33331.1667 and the 1250 bp case rounds UP from an exact 28123.875; every seat carries a price_paise integer identical to its own category's value in the same response (assert across all 220 seats); the expression is computed as (base_price_paise * (10000 + uplift_basis_points) + 5000) // 10000 with int operands only and no float appears anywhere in the path (assert the type of every intermediate); three seats of the 3333 bp category sum to 99993 and the total is not re-rounded; the legend renders one row per category reading 'Premium  ₹281.24' and the seat map renders no tax line, no booking fee and no discount field; a category whose price has not yet arrived renders an inset block and never '₹0.00'; and no formatted currency string and no decimal appears in the JSON payload.
SourceRef: P-BRW-10 E1 S4 SRC-001 §5.2.3 FR-ADR-038 FR-ADR-036 R-SEAT-03

Title: Derive the category bands from the payload and say what happens when they interleave
Description: Band position is the primary non-colour carrier of category, so how a band is computed has to be specified rather than left to the implementer. A band is a maximal run of consecutive grid rows carrying exactly one category; a void row does not break it, a mixed row does. categories is ordered by first appearance so the legend and the bands cannot disagree, and no display_order field is added.
AcceptanceCriteria: For a 6-row hall where gr 1, 2 and 4 are all category 1, gr 3 holds no seats, gr 5 holds both categories and gr 6 is all category 2: the derivation produces exactly two bands, category 1 over gr 1-4 and category 2 over gr 6; no dashed band rule element is drawn anywhere on that screen, because the two bands are not adjacent; categories is returned as [{id:1},{id:2}] ordered by lowest gr of first appearance with id ascending as the tiebreak, and the legend renders in that same top-to-bottom order; a category appearing in two separate runs draws two bands and exactly one legend row; when every grid row is mixed, no band gap and no rule element exists in the DOM and one line renders once reading 'Seat categories are mixed within rows. Each seat's category is in the legend and in its label.'; a category with no seat in this showtime's seat set is absent from categories; two seats sharing a gr with different row strings returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with a request id rather than reaching the client; a retired seat still participates in the derivation (retiring one seat of a pure row does not split its band); and the client performs no sort of categories (assert no sort call on that array in the source).
SourceRef: P-BRW-16 E1 S4 FR-ADR-016 FR-ADR-051 FR-ADR-072 R-SEAT-03

Title: Refresh the seat map on the interval the server publishes, and pause it when nobody is looking
Description: The map re-fetches itself every poll_interval_seconds, which is server configuration returned in the payload so the client holds no constant and one value governs. There is no manual refresh control. A failed poll never blanks the map. Worst-case staleness is about 13 seconds and is a property of the system, never a message.
AcceptanceCriteria: With poll_interval_seconds=3 in the payload and a fake client timer: exactly one GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap is issued per 3 seconds of client time; with a response that takes 5 seconds, no second request is issued until the first lands and the interval then restarts (at most one in flight); with document.hidden true no request is issued for 30 seconds of client time, and the visibilitychange to visible fires one request immediately; the rendered screen contains no refresh or reload control; a poll that fails with a network error or a 5xx leaves the previously rendered grid unchanged in the DOM and adds exactly one strip reading 'The seat map is not updating. The seats shown may be out of date.', and a second consecutive failure leaves the map still on screen; the frontend source contains no numeric literal for the poll interval (the value comes only from the payload); the server rejects a missing or non-integer SEATMAP_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS at boot; and with SEATMAP_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS=5 the payload reports 5 and the client issues one request per 5 seconds with no frontend redeploy.
SourceRef: P-BRW-11 E1 S4 E1 S6 SRC-002 §8.6.1 FR-ADR-045 R-SEAT-06

Title: Cache the read path, invalidate the listings by a generation counter, and keep browsing alive when Redis is gone
Description: Every read here is cache-aside. The seat map has one key per showtime and is invalidated by a DEL; the listings are cached per filter combination over an unbounded keyspace, so they are made unreachable by an INCR of cache:listing:generation instead. A failed invalidation is never retried and the staleness is bounded by the TTL rather than hidden.
AcceptanceCriteria: A listing read reads cache:listing:generation and writes cache:listing:{generation}:{fingerprint} with a TTL of 60 seconds; a seat map read writes cache:seatmap:{showtime_id} with a TTL of 10 seconds (assert both with TTL on the key); after an admin publish commits, cache:listing:generation has increased by exactly 1 and the next listing read returns the new film; a Redis command log over one admin write plus one listing read contains INCR and SETEX and contains no SET of a listing body and no SCAN; a booking commit issues DEL cache:seatmap:{id}; with the DEL forced to fail, the transaction is not rolled back, the DEL is not retried, one warning carrying the write's request id is logged, and the entry disappears within its 10-second TTL; on a cache miss exactly one caller acquires cache:seatmap:{id}:rebuild with SET NX PX 2000 and the callers that lose re-read once and then read PostgreSQL directly rather than queueing, and the rebuild code carries the stampede comment; with the counter key deleted, the next INCR yields 1 and the read succeeds; no code path issues SET or DEL against cache:listing:generation (assert by grep over the source); and with Redis stopped, GET /api/movies and GET /api/showtimes both return 200 served from PostgreSQL with no user-facing message.
SourceRef: P-BRW-12 E1 S4 SRC-002 §8.2.1 FR-ADR-030 FR-ADR-028 R-QLY-04 R-SEAT-06

Title: Paginate nothing, and replace the missing latency budget with a Phase 3 measurement
Description: No endpoint in this epic is paginated and no silent cap is applied, because a truncated listing the customer cannot detect is worse than a long one. No frozen source states a latency budget of any kind and none is invented here; what replaces it is a measurement obligation and criteria that are binary on screen. The payload figures are ASSUMED on a 220-seat hall.
AcceptanceCriteria: No endpoint in this epic declares a page, offset, limit or cursor parameter (assert against the generated OpenAPI document); GET /api/movies?page=2&limit=5 returns a body byte-identical to GET /api/movies and the listing carries a count equal to the number of visible films with no cap applied; GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap for the 220-seat hall returns all 220 seats in one response; the Phase 3 measurement records the measured seat-map response size in bytes, the measured response time and the measured cache hit rate, each with the number of samples taken and the worst value stated first, and the estimate of about 26 KB per poll is replaced by the measured figure in the engineering ledger; the source contains no p50, p95, time-to-first-byte or frames-per-second constant (assert by grep); and on the seat map screen the bounding box of the field, the screen bar and the row gutters measured before seat data lands is identical to the box measured after it lands, with no spinner element present at any point.
SourceRef: P-BRW-13 P-BRW-14 E1 S4 SRC-001 §7.3 FR-ADR-045 R-QLY-04

Title: Serve posters from our own bucket by redirect, and never hotlink
Description: The poster endpoint answers 302 with a presigned GET URL for a private bucket, so the API never spends its single worker proxying image bytes. The browser cache lifetime must stay below the presigned expiry or a cached redirect outlives its target. This endpoint applies no visibility gate, so a draft poster id is reachable - stated and accepted, not overlooked.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/movies/11/poster returns 302 with an empty body and a Location header pointing at our own bucket host, carrying a presigned signature with an expiry of 3600 seconds, and no response in this path contains image bytes; the Cache-Control header is max-age=POSTER_REDIRECT_CACHE_SECONDS with a configured value of 300, and the process asserts at boot that this value is strictly less than 3600 and exits non-zero if it is not; a movie whose poster_object_key is NULL returns 404 NOT_FOUND and the card renders the perforation motif with the title inside it, with no words and no broken-image glyph; a movie id that does not exist returns 404 with the same body; the object key used to presign is read from the movie row and a key supplied as a query parameter is ignored (assert the presigned URL is unchanged when ?key=../../etc/passwd is appended); presigning issues no network call to S3 (assert no outbound request during the handler); and a movie that is unpublished or outside its display window still returns 302 here, which is the ungated behaviour of record.
SourceRef: P-BRW-15 E1 S4 SRC-002 §10.6.3 FR-ADR-061 R-BRW-02

Title: Rate limit the seat map per address, split the two 429 states, and fail closed when Redis is gone
Description: The seat map is the only limited endpoint in this epic, at 120 requests a minute per IP with no per-user bucket because it is unauthenticated. A 429 on a poll and a 429 on the first load take different strings, because the polling sentence promises an update that no loop exists to deliver on a first load. The limiter runs before the cache and fails closed, which is the adjudicated PROVISIONAL answer for the seat map when Redis is down.
AcceptanceCriteria: The 121st request within one minute from one address to GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with a Retry-After header, and requests 1 to 120 return 200; six simulated viewers polling that endpoint at 3 seconds from one address (20 requests a minute each, 120 total) all succeed for a full minute and the seventh receives 429 - the arithmetic 60/3=20 and 120/20=6 is asserted, not assumed; a 429 on a poll while a map is on screen leaves the last good map rendered, shows 'Too many requests. The seat map will update again shortly.' and issues the next request no sooner than Retry-After seconds later; a 429 on the first load, with no map and no poll loop, renders 'The seat map could not be loaded.' with a control reading 'Try again' and never renders the polling sentence; with Redis unreachable, GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE rendering exactly 'The seat map is unavailable right now. You can still browse showtimes. Try again in a few minutes.' and that string occurs in exactly one place in the source; and in the same condition GET /api/movies and GET /api/showtimes both return 200, because neither is a limited endpoint.
SourceRef: P-BRW-11 P-BRW-12 E1 S4 E1 S6 FR-ADR-058 FR-ADR-028 R-QLY-04

Title: Checkout and payment
Description: Everything between a live seat hold and a committed booking row: the checkout screen, the money arithmetic behind the figure on it, the single confirm endpoint, and the transaction inside it. Payment is simulated and no provider is ever integrated.
SourceRef: E3 S4 SRC-001 §5.3.1 SRC-003 OPEN-PAY-01 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01

Title: Hold every money value as integer paise
Description: Every money value on the checkout path is an exact whole number of paise held in an integer, with the minor-unit ratio a named configuration value rather than a literal. The ratio of 100 is a one-way door: bookings are permanent, so reinterpreting the unit later silently rewrites what every past customer paid and no migration can recover which rows were written under which interpretation.
AcceptanceCriteria: With CURRENCY_CODE=INR and CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO=100 the API boots; with CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO unset, 0, or non-integer the process exits non-zero before binding a port, stderr names the variable, and a connection to /health/live is refused; every money column on booking, booking_seat and payment is bigint with a name ending in _paise - SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name IN ('booking','booking_seat','payment') AND column_name LIKE '%_paise' returns exactly total_paise, price_paise, base_price_paise_applied, amount_paise and every data_type is bigint; rg -n 'float\(|Decimal' backend/app/domain/pricing.py backend/app/api/bookings.py returns 0 hits; ₹275.00 is stored and returned as the integer 27500 and ₹1,661.46 as 166146; the 201 body of POST /api/bookings carries total_paise as a JSON number equal to 166146 and carries no field holding a formatted currency string, and the only formatted figure in the product is produced in the presentation layer at render time; rg -n 'CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO' backend/app shows the value defined once in config and read by name everywhere else, and no money expression contains a literal 100
SourceRef: P-PAY-02 E3 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01 SRC-001 §7.6 FR-ADR-036

Title: Compute every seat price and every total with one integer half-up function
Description: One function computes a seat price from two integers and every caller in the system uses it - seat map, checkout, receipt, dashboard and seed script. The total is the arithmetic sum of the already-rounded per-seat prices and is never itself rounded, because a total rounded once disagrees with the per-seat figures printed above it on the same screen.
AcceptanceCriteria: seat_price_paise(27500, 1250) returns 30938, seat_price_paise(27500, 3333) returns 36666, seat_price_paise(27500, 0) returns 27500, and seat_price_paise(25000, 3333) returns 33333 - the case where half-even would return 33332; the function raises TypeError on a float argument rather than rounding it, and rejects a negative base_price_paise or uplift_basis_points; the total for three seats at 30938 and two at 36666 is exactly 166146, and a test asserts the value 166144 - the figure produced by carrying exact values and rounding the total once - is produced by no code path; the basis-point denominator 10000 and the half constant 5000 exist as named constants in exactly one module: rg -n '10000|5000' backend/app --glob '!**/pricing.py' returns 0 hits on the money path, and rg -n 'uplift_basis_points' backend/app outside that module shows reads only, never arithmetic; the inputs 27500 base and 0/1250/3333 uplifts are supplied explicitly by the test and are never read from seed data, because the category names and uplifts are ASSUMED under SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-01 and are illustrative only
SourceRef: P-PAY-03 P-PAY-04 E3 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 FR-ADR-037 FR-ADR-038 FR-ADR-039

Title: Fix the price at hold acquisition and snapshot it onto every booked seat
Description: The customer pays the price that was current when their hold was granted: the per-seat figures are computed once at hold acquisition, stored with the hold, and copied onto the booking rows. The three inputs are stored beside the output so the figure can be audited later; nothing on any display path recomputes a price for a booking that already exists.
AcceptanceCriteria: A hold on showtime 7 acquired at 14:00:00Z on the injected clock stores price_paise 30938 for seat F7; an admin raises showtime.base_price_paise from 27500 to 30000 at 14:01:10Z; a confirm at 14:02:40Z returns price_paise 30938 and total_paise 30938; SELECT price_paise, base_price_paise_applied, uplift_basis_points_applied, seat_category_id FROM booking_seat WHERE booking_id = the new id returns 30938, 27500, 1250 and a non-null category id; a hold taken by a second customer at 14:01:20Z stores 33750 and that customer is charged 33750; the confirm path calls no pricing function - rg -n 'seat_price_paise' backend/app/api/bookings.py returns 0 hits; a hold record carrying no price snapshot yields 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with the transaction rolled back, SELECT count(*) FROM booking unchanged, and no recomputed price anywhere in the response or the log; after the booking exists, setting seat_category.uplift_basis_points to 2000 leaves GET /api/bookings/{id} returning price_paise 30938 and total_paise 30938; the admin price edit itself is never blocked and returns its normal success response while the hold is live
SourceRef: P-PAY-05 P-PAY-04 E3 S4 SRC-001 §7.6 FR-ADR-035 FR-ADR-039

Title: Refuse to boot on a payment configuration that could break a confirm
Description: Every payment configuration value is validated at startup, because a misconfiguration must crash at boot rather than at checkout. The failure-trigger prefix is validated against the canonical UUID alphabet so that a browser-minted key can never carry it by chance and fail real confirms at random. E-XCT owns the boot-validation mechanism and the /health/ready payload; this story states what they must carry for payment.
AcceptanceCriteria: With SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=180 the computed bound is 18000 ms: PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS=1500 boots, 17999 boots, 18000 exits non-zero before binding a port with a message naming the variable, the configured value and the computed bound, and 60000 exits the same way; PAYMENT_PROVIDER unset exits non-zero, PAYMENT_PROVIDER=stripe exits non-zero with a message stating that no other provider exists, and rg -n 'PAYMENT_PROVIDER' backend/app shows no default and no fallback to simulated; PAYMENT_SIMULATOR_FAIL_KEY_PREFIX=a exits non-zero and =deadbeef exits non-zero, each with a message naming the variable, the value and the reason that a browser-minted Idempotency-Key could begin with it by chance; FAIL_ boots; an unset value or one longer than 32 characters exits non-zero; on a successful boot the configured provider is written once to the JSON boot log on stdout as simulated, and GET /health/ready returns a body whose payment provider field reads simulated; the delay value 1500 and the prefix FAIL_ are ASSUMED - no source names either - so both are read from configuration and appear as a literal in no expression
SourceRef: P-PAY-07 E3 S4 SRC-002 §7.1 FR-ADR-041 FR-ADR-053

Title: Capture the simulated payment through pending, authorized and captured
Description: Payment is simulated behind an interface carrying real states, and no gateway is integrated at any point in this project. One payment row per booking attempt records the state, the amount in paise, each transition timestamp and the Idempotency-Key that produced it; booking.payment_id points at payment.id because the payment row exists before the booking row does.
AcceptanceCriteria: After a successful confirm of the five-seat selection, SELECT state, amount_paise, idempotency_key FROM payment WHERE id = (SELECT payment_id FROM booking WHERE id = the new id) returns captured, 166146 and the key the request sent, and the row carries a non-null timestamp for each of pending, authorized and captured; SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='payment' AND column_name='booking_id' returns 0 - the foreign key runs booking.payment_id -> payment.id and not the reverse; a capture attempted from pending without authorized is rejected by the state machine and writes nothing; a transition out of failed is rejected and failed remains terminal; exactly one payment row exists per booking attempt: after a single confirm SELECT count(*) FROM payment WHERE idempotency_key = the key sent returns 1, and a second attempt with a fresh key after a rolled-back one leaves 2 rows, one failed and one captured; the artificial delay is an injected sleep - a test substituting it asserts it was called exactly once with 1500 ms, and no test in this story measures real elapsed time; no outbound HTTP client is constructed on this path: rg -n 'httpx|requests\.|aiohttp|urllib' backend/app/domain/payment returns 0 hits
SourceRef: P-PAY-07 P-PAY-01 E3 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-PAY-01 SRC-001 §E E-10 FR-ADR-041

Title: Insert the idempotency record first and answer a duplicate in exactly three ways
Description: The confirm endpoint requires an Idempotency-Key header and the record is a PostgreSQL row inserted first, in the same transaction, before any other work, unique on (user_id, idempotency_key) - the index is the check and the act in one statement, so there is no check-then-act window. A duplicate gets the stored response, a 409 in flight, or a 422 on a different fingerprint, and nothing else.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/bookings with no Idempotency-Key header returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID, opens no transaction and leaves SELECT count(*) FROM idempotency_record unchanged; an empty key or one of 256 characters returns 400; the key is compared as an exact byte sequence and is never trimmed, lowercased or normalised; two requests carrying the same key and the same body, the second sent after the first completes, produce exactly one booking and exactly one payment - SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE user_id=U AND showtime_id=7 returns 1 and SELECT count(*) FROM payment returns 1 - and the second response is byte-for-byte the stored response_body with the original 201 status; a second request sent while the first is still capturing returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT with Retry-After: 3, and its response is received before the first request's response - the duplicate is never made to wait on the winner; the same key with a different hold_token returns 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, and returns it again on every later attempt because the record is never deleted; the same key sent by a different user id inserts cleanly and confirms normally; a key whose transaction rolled back inserts cleanly on the next attempt; rg -in 'DELETE FROM idempotency|idempotency.*(expire|ttl|purge)' backend returns 0 hits and no migration adds an expiry to that table

Title: Run the confirm transaction in the specified order and recover from a crash at every step
Description: One READ COMMITTED transaction runs twelve steps in a fixed order and three more after the commit. The payment is captured before the booking insert because SRC-001 §5.3.1 requires it, which creates a window between capture and commit; the window is empty in effect here only because the simulated provider holds no external ledger. QUEUE_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 is ASSUMED and is replaced with a measured value in phase 7.
AcceptanceCriteria: An instrumented confirm records its steps in exactly this order: idempotency insert, hold re-validation in Redis, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the showtime row, showtime read, price sum from the hold snapshot, payment capture, booking and booking_seat insert, audit no-op, receipt_dispatch insert, outbox_message insert, idempotency record completed, COMMIT - then, after the commit, Redis lock release with the compare-and-delete script plus removal of the token from holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}, DEL cache:seatmap:7, and the bounded queue send; SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is used only on the showtime row and never to test whether a seat is free - rg -n 'FOR UPDATE' backend/app/api/bookings.py shows one occurrence, on the showtime query; step 9 writes receipt_dispatch with dispatch_seq 1, status pending, attempts 0 and every timestamp null, and no committed state exists in which an outbox_message row exists without its receipt_dispatch row - a query joining the two returns 0 orphans after 50 confirms; a fault injected between the capture and the booking insert leaves SELECT count(*) FROM payment, FROM booking and FROM idempotency_record all at 0, and a retry with the same key then produces exactly one payment and exactly one booking; a fault injected after COMMIT but before the response leaves the booking, its seats, the payment, the pending receipt_dispatch, the outbox row and a completed idempotency record, and the retry with the same key replays the stored response without creating anything; the sales cut-off is not enforced here: a confirm on a showtime whose cut-off has passed returns 201, and SALES_CLOSED appears in no response this endpoint can produce; the 201 is emitted only after the queue send returns, fails or times out at QUEUE_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 - with a stubbed queue that never answers, the response is still 201 and the outbox row is still pending, and no work is handed to a background task (rg -n 'BackgroundTasks|create_task' backend/app/api/bookings.py returns 0 hits); booking.total_paise equals the sum of its booking_seat.price_paise rows and the count of booking_seat rows equals the number of seats in the hold, or the transaction rolls back with 500 INTERNAL_ERROR and no partial booking
SourceRef: P-PAY-10 P-PAY-04 E3 S4 SRC-002 §8.1.5 SRC-001 §5.3.1 FR-ADR-029 FR-ADR-030 FR-ADR-031

Title: Serve POST /api/bookings with its published contract, auth and error set
Description: The single write that turns a hold into a booking. It accepts a hold token and a showtime id and nothing else - no seat identifiers and no money field - so a caller cannot confirm seats it never held or a price it was never quoted. Authorisation is a router dependency and the booking is always written against the user id in the token.
AcceptanceCriteria: With no JWT or an expired one the endpoint returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED and the message 'Sign in to complete this booking.'; the check is a router dependency - rg -n 'Depends' backend/app/api/bookings.py shows the auth dependency on the router and the handler body contains no role check; the request body accepts exactly hold_token and showtime_id: a hold_token of 42 or 44 characters, or carrying a character outside the URL-safe base64 alphabet, returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID with Redis stopped, proving the check runs before Redis is touched; a showtime_id that does not match the showtime the hold was taken on returns 400; a body carrying a seats array returns 400; with Redis unreachable the endpoint returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, SELECT count(*) FROM booking is unchanged, and no query against PostgreSQL is issued as a hold-check fallback; the 201 body carries booking_id, booking_reference in the presentation form FR-XXXX-XXXX, showtime_id, movie_title, screen_name, starts_at, seats, total_paise, currency_code INR, payment_status captured and created_at; starts_at and created_at each end with the cinema row's UTC offset - +05:30 for the seeded cinema - and never with Z, and updating the cinema row's timezone changes the offset in the next response without any client-side conversion; the error set the endpoint can return is exactly REQUEST_INVALID, AUTH_REQUIRED, HOLD_EXPIRED, HOLD_NOT_OWNED, SEAT_UNAVAILABLE, IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, PAYMENT_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED, DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and INTERNAL_ERROR, and SALES_CLOSED is not among them; an 11th confirm in one minute from one user id returns 429 with Retry-After: 6 and the message 'Too many attempts. Try again in 6 seconds.', and a 31st from one client IP returns Retry-After: 2; a retry carrying an already-seen Idempotency-Key still spends a token
SourceRef: P-PAY-01 P-PAY-06 E3 S6 EP-PAY-01 SRC-001 §5.3.1 SRC-001 §E E-10 FR-ADR-014 FR-ADR-018

Title: Treat a unique-constraint violation as the guard working
Description: A unique-constraint violation on (showtime_id, seat_id) at the booking-seat insert is not an error - it is the second half of the double-booking guarantee firing. It is caught, translated to 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE, never retried, never returned as 500 and never logged as an exception. The constraint-drop red proof itself is E-XCT's P-XCT-01 Stage B and is not duplicated here.
AcceptanceCriteria: With two live holders of one seat on showtime 7 both confirming, one gets 201 and the other gets 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE whose details.unavailable_seats names exactly that seat, and SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=7 AND seat_id='F7' returns 1; the loser's transaction rolls back in full: SELECT count(*) FROM payment WHERE state='captured' returns 1, not 2, and no partial booking row exists; with two or more seats lost, one 409 names every one of them in details.unavailable_seats in the order they appear in the hold, and the server renders the complete plural sentence itself rather than the client composing it; the violation is logged at info level with a counter incremented, appears in no error-level log line and never as a 500 - a test asserts the captured JSON log for that request has level info; the server makes exactly one insert attempt and never retries a lost race - assert one INSERT in the query log; rg -n 'ON CONFLICT' backend/app returns 0 hits on the booking_seat insert; the unique index on booking_seat (showtime_id, seat_id) has no WHERE clause - SELECT indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename='booking_seat' shows a total unique index - and the database guard is never waived, disabled or made conditional in application code

Title: Accept no card, tax, fee or discount field anywhere on the payment path
Description: The amount charged is the sum of the per-seat prices with nothing added and nothing taken away, and the product never asks for, records or displays card data. Both are prohibitions on the implementation and on its tests: a rejected field's name and value are never echoed into a log or a response, and no space is reserved for a future line item.
AcceptanceCriteria: rg -in 'card_number|cardholder|cvv|cvc|expiry_month|expiry_year|card_expiry' backend frontend scripts returns 0 hits, including in fixtures and seed scripts; a confirm body carrying any of card_number, discount_code, coupon, fee or tax returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID with the message 'This request could not be processed. Return to the seat map and choose your seats again.', and the captured stdout JSON log for that request contains neither the offending field name nor its value; the generated OpenAPI for POST /api/bookings declares additionalProperties false and exactly two properties, hold_token and showtime_id; the 201 body's key set is exactly booking_id, booking_reference, showtime_id, movie_title, screen_name, starts_at, seats, total_paise, currency_code, payment_status, created_at - no tax, fee or discount key and no zero-rate placeholder; the rendered checkout screen contains zero input elements and no element whose text matches Tax, Fee, Discount, Coupon or Promo, and the layout reserves no row beneath the seat lines other than the total; for the five-seat selection the amount captured, the amount stored on the booking and the amount displayed are all 166146, and no other money figure exists for that booking in any table
SourceRef: P-PAY-08 P-PAY-06 E3 S4 SRC-001 §7.4 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-02 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-03 FR-ADR-040

Title: Give the payment path no reverse
Description: A captured simulated payment is never unwound: no refunded state, no refund table, no cancellation reason, no cancellation-policy configuration and no customer-initiated cancellation. booking.status and booking.cancelled_at exist in the schema because SRC-001 §6.6 forbids designing in a way that blocks a later ask, and no v1 endpoint exposes either. Anything beyond publishing the ruled absence would be a money decision, which is reserved.
AcceptanceCriteria: The payment state set is exactly pending, authorized, captured, failed - SELECT unnest(enum_range(NULL::payment_state)) returns those four and no refunded value; no cancellation or refund route is registered: POST /api/bookings/1/cancel and POST /api/bookings/1/refund each return FastAPI's own 404, and the generated OpenAPI contains no path whose string matches cancel or refund; rg -in 'refund' backend/app frontend/src returns 0 hits; a request body setting status or cancelled_at on any v1 endpoint returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID because the property is unknown to the schema; booking.status and booking.cancelled_at exist - information_schema returns both - status is written once at confirmation to the confirmed value, SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE cancelled_at IS NOT NULL returns 0, and neither column appears in any v1 response schema; SCR-TKT-01 renders the line 'This booking cannot be changed, cancelled or refunded.' beneath its entry line - the string is owned and implemented by E-TKT and this story asserts only that the page carries it; no withdraw-showtime capability exists in v1, so no route can strand a captured payment: the admin surface exposes no endpoint that withdraws a showtime holding bookings
SourceRef: P-PAY-12 E3 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-CANCEL-01 SRC-003 OPEN-CANCEL-02 SRC-001 §E E-2 SRC-001 §6.6 FR-ADR-013

Title: Mint, store and re-send the Idempotency-Key from the client
Description: The client mints the key, never the server: once per confirm attempt, bound to the hold token it was minted against, written to sessionStorage before the request is sent, and re-sent unchanged on any ending whose effect is unknown. A fresh key is minted only after a 402, the one response specified to have committed nothing - minting a fresh key for an attempt of unknown outcome is the one manoeuvre that can produce two bookings and two captures for one intent.
AcceptanceCriteria: The key is crypto.randomUUID() in its canonical 36-character form: rg -n 'Math.random' frontend/src returns 0 hits and rg -n 'randomUUID' frontend/src shows exactly one mint site on the confirm path; pressing pay writes sessionStorage['fr.confirm_idempotency_key'] carrying the key and the hold_token it was minted against, and the write is asserted to happen before the fetch is issued; a page refresh mid-flight followed by a second press sends the identical key with the identical body; a simulated dropped connection followed by a second press sends the identical key; after a 402 PAYMENT_FAILED the next press carries a different key; after the hold token changes the next press carries a different key; with no stored key a fresh one is minted; the value is cleared on a 201, on a 402 and on sign-out, and sign-out clears every fr.* value including fr.last_booking_reference and the hold token - assert sessionStorage has no key beginning with fr. after sign-out; with PAYMENT_SIMULATOR_FAIL_KEY_PREFIX=FAIL_ no client-minted key can begin with it, because the prefix contains characters outside the canonical UUID alphabet [0-9a-f-] that randomUUID can produce
SourceRef: P-PAY-09 E3 S4 SRC-002 §8.3.1 FR-ADR-020 FR-ADR-047

Title: Render the checkout panel
Description: The only screen in the product with a pay action. It renders the simulated-payment notice first, the seat lines from the hold's price snapshot, the total, the countdown and one button - and it performs no arithmetic beyond displaying the sum it was given. The seat map's post-hold control is navigation to this route and issues no request.
AcceptanceCriteria: At /showtimes/7/checkout holding F7, F8, F9, J3 and J4 the notice slab is the first element of the panel, above the heading, reading 'No real payment is taken. This is a demonstration system. Nothing is charged and no card details are collected.', with no dismiss control, rendered unconditionally and never below --fr-text-md; the heading reads 'Confirm your booking'; five booking lines render the snapshot figures 309.38, 309.38, 309.38, 366.66 and 366.66 with their category names, and the client recomputes no price from a base price; the total renders as ₹1,661.46 from total_paise 166146, formatted with Indian digit grouping at render time only, and the label reads 'TOTAL'; the pay action's visible label is 'Pay ₹1,661.46' carrying the current total and its accessible name is 'Pay 1,661 rupees 46 paise'; with any seat price missing the total is absent entirely and the pay action is disabled - no partial total is ever displayed; the pay action is disabled when there is no live hold, when the countdown reads 0:00, when a request is in flight, and while any seat price is missing, and one press issues exactly one POST; in flight the label reads 'Confirming…', the countdown keeps running, and the panel's height does not change; the countdown is computed from the server's absolute expires_at with the current instant supplied as an input - the component reads no wall clock and a test drives it by advancing the injected instant; focus order is notice slab, heading, seat lines, total, countdown, pay action, back to seats, with the error banner inserted before the panel in the DOM when present; 'Back to seats' navigates only: it issues no request and does not release the hold
SourceRef: P-PAY-01 P-PAY-04 P-PAY-08 E3 S5 SCR-PAY-01 COMPONENTS.md §5 COMPONENTS.md §8

Title: Handle every ending on the checkout screen
Description: Every outcome of the confirm has a specified rendering: a banner that branches on the error code and never on the message text, an automatic bounded re-send on an in-flight duplicate, a zero state that holds long enough to be read before returning to the seat map, and a stored booking reference that tells 'already confirmed' from 'hold expired' without issuing a request. The four hold-related strings are E-SEA's and are displayed as received.
AcceptanceCriteria: The banner branches on the error code, never on message text, and renders above an unchanged panel: AUTH_REQUIRED 'Sign in to complete this booking.'; IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED and REQUEST_INVALID 'This checkout is out of date. Return to the seat map and choose your seats again.' and 'This request could not be processed. Return to the seat map and choose your seats again.' respectively; PAYMENT_FAILED the single string 'The payment did not go through and you have not been charged. You can try again while the countdown is still running. If it has reached zero your hold has ended and you will need to choose your seats again.'; INTERNAL_ERROR 'Something went wrong and your booking was not completed. No payment was taken. If you need help, quote a1b2c3d4.' with the request id taken from the error envelope; and HOLD_EXPIRED, HOLD_NOT_OWNED, SEAT_UNAVAILABLE and DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE displayed exactly as the server sent them, with this screen holding no copy of its own for those four; no banner on this screen carries a control - assert zero interactive elements inside the banner; on 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT the banner reads 'This booking is still being processed.', the pay action keeps its busy state and stays disabled, and the screen re-sends the identical request with the identical key after Retry-After seconds at most 3 times: a stub answering 409 four times receives exactly 4 requests in total and the button is then re-enabled with the banner still shown; at 0:00 with no confirm in flight the pay action is disabled and labelled 'Hold expired', SCR-SEA-02's zero state renders and is announced once through a polite live region, and only after CHECKOUT_EXPIRY_RETURN_DELAY_MS=5000 has elapsed on the injected clock does the screen return to the seat map with the previous selection re-applied; at 0:00 with a confirm in flight nothing navigates, no return timer starts, the request is not cancelled, and the response is handled exactly as before 0:00; on a 201 the screen writes fr.last_booking_reference with its showtime_id before navigating to the confirmation screen; arriving at this route with fr.last_booking_reference present for showtime 7 redirects to that booking's confirmation screen and issues no request; acquiring a hold for any showtime, including showtime 7 itself, clears the value when the hold response arrives and before any navigation, so a second booking of the same showtime in one tab reaches checkout; sign-out clears fr.last_booking_reference with every other fr.* value, so a second user signing in to the same tab is never redirected to the first user's confirmation URL; the sales cut-off passing while this screen is open changes nothing rendered and issues no request; the error banner is announced through an assertive live region
SourceRef: P-PAY-01 P-PAY-09 E3 S5 SCR-PAY-01 FR-ADR-047 FR-ADR-051

Title: Drive the deliberate payment failure by hand and prove fail, retry, succeed
Description: The failure is deliberate and never random: it fires when the request's Idempotency-Key begins with PAYMENT_SIMULATOR_FAIL_KEY_PREFIX, so it is driven from scripts/ or curl and never from a browser, whose keys cannot carry the prefix by construction. OPEN QUESTION, not answered here: whether hand-only reachability is the right shape has been raised with the client and is unsettled; this story is written against what P-PAY-07 says today and adds no control to the product to reach it.
AcceptanceCriteria: With PAYMENT_SIMULATOR_FAIL_KEY_PREFIX=FAIL_ and a live hold on showtime 7, a curl POST to /api/bookings with header 'Idempotency-Key: FAIL_9f2c1d4e-7b83-4a16-9c05-2e6f8a31b7d0' returns 402 PAYMENT_FAILED; SELECT state FROM payment WHERE idempotency_key='FAIL_9f2c1d4e-7b83-4a16-9c05-2e6f8a31b7d0' returns failed and that row is committed in its own transaction, while SELECT count(*) FROM booking returns 0 and SELECT count(*) FROM idempotency_record WHERE idempotency_key='FAIL_9f2c1d4e-7b83-4a16-9c05-2e6f8a31b7d0' returns 0 - the booking transaction rolled back in full, taking its idempotency record with it; repeating the identical call returns 402 again and creates nothing; a third call against the same still-live hold carrying a key without the prefix returns 201, and SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE showtime_id=7 AND user_id=U returns 1 and SELECT count(*) FROM payment WHERE state='captured' returns 1 - fail, retry, succeed proved in three commands with no double charge; no control in the product sets this header: rg -n 'FAIL_|PAYMENT_SIMULATOR_FAIL' frontend/src returns 0 hits; the same drill run through the browser is impossible by construction, because a boot check rejects any prefix drawn entirely from [0-9a-f-]
SourceRef: P-PAY-07 P-PAY-09 P-PAY-01 E3 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-PAY-01 FR-ADR-041

Title: Build the manager and admin reporting dashboard
Description: Phase 8. A manager or administrator signs in and reads takings, occupancy and per-film performance for a whole calendar day, ISO week or calendar month in Asia/Kolkata, scoped to the screens they are assigned to; an administrator alone reads the change log. Nothing on this surface writes anything and nothing produces a file. The manager role itself is PROVISIONAL (SRC-003 C-1) and one client message deletes this persona.
SourceRef: E7 S4 E7 S5 E7 S6 SRC-003 OPEN-SCOPE-01 SRC-003 OPEN-REPORT-01 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 SRC-002 §12

Title: Resolve the reporting period in Asia/Kolkata and convert both edges to UTC
Description: Every figure in this epic is a sum over a time window, and the window must be computed as whole local calendar periods in the cinema's stored zone before it touches a timestamptz column. A window taken in UTC moves by five and a half hours and files a late show on the wrong date.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the injected clock at 2026-08-14T12:50:00Z and the cinema row carrying zone Asia/Kolkata, GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day with date omitted returns period_start_utc 2026-08-13T18:30:00Z and period_end_utc 2026-08-14T18:30:00Z; period=week returns 2026-08-09T18:30:00Z and 2026-08-16T18:30:00Z, ISO-8601 Monday-first; period=month returns 2026-07-31T18:30:00Z and 2026-08-31T18:30:00Z, a calendar month and never a rolling thirty days; the interval is half-open, so a showtime with starts_at 2026-08-14T19:00:00Z (Sat 15 Aug 00:30 local) is absent from date=2026-08-14 and present in date=2026-08-15; the zone is read from the cinema row and not from a constant; and grep -rn for datetime.now, utcnow and time.time over the reports module returns 0 hits, the clock being injected in every path including the default anchor date
SourceRef: P-RPT-01 E7 S4 FR-ADR-043 FR-ADR-018 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01

Title: Validate period and date, and keep boundary instants separate from rendered instants
Description: The two query parameters every reports endpoint shares are validated once, and the two kinds of instant on this surface are serialised differently on purpose: a _utc suffix marks a boundary that is never rendered, and a field without it is rendered and carries the cinema's offset.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/reports/dashboard with period absent returns 422 code VALIDATION_FAILED and the message 'Choose day, week or month.'; period=year returns the same; date=14-08-2026 returns 422 with 'The date must be written as YYYY-MM-DD.'; date=2026-02-30 returns 422 with 'That date does not exist.'; date=1990-01-01 and date=2099-01-01 both return 200, because P-RPT-01 places no bound on the anchor in either direction; every 200 body carries period_start_utc, period_end_utc and evaluated_at_utc as bare UTC ending in Z; EP-RPT-02 rows[].starts_at renders as 2026-08-14T19:30:00+05:30 and EP-RPT-04 rows[].occurred_at as 2026-08-12T15:40:00+05:30, both with the cinema offset, neither with a _utc suffix, and both accompanied by a timezone field reading Asia/Kolkata; and no reports field named with a _utc suffix is read by any frontend rendering path
SourceRef: P-RPT-01 E7 S4 E7 S6 FR-ADR-018 FR-ADR-052

Title: Resolve the caller's role and screen scope once, on the reports router
Description: Authorisation is a router dependency, never a per-handler check, and scope attaches to the screen rather than the cinema: with one cinema, cinema-level scoping would scope nothing. Both the role dependency and the scope resolver are PROVISIONAL, because the manager role is (SRC-003 C-1).
AcceptanceCriteria: The reports router is mounted with one role dependency admitting exactly manager and admin, plus a report_scope dependency, and grep over every handler in the reports package finds no handler reading screen_id from the request and checking it itself; an unauthenticated GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED with 'Sign in to see the dashboard.'; the same request as a customer and as a guest returns 403 FORBIDDEN with 'This page is for managers and administrators.'; for an administrator the resolver applies no screen filter and the response screen_ids lists every screen id, never an empty array and never omitted; for manager M holding assignment rows for screens 3 and 5 screen_ids is [3,5]; &screen_id=3 as M returns screen_ids [3]; &screen_id=1 as M returns 403 FORBIDDEN with 'That hall is not assigned to this account.'; &screen_id=9 naming no existing hall returns that same 403 to M, so the response is not an oracle for which screen ids exist, while &screen_id=9 as an administrator returns 404 NOT_FOUND with 'That hall does not exist.'; screen_id=abc returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED; and a screen whose is_active is false is still a valid narrowing value and its past figures are unchanged
SourceRef: P-RPT-02 E7 S4 SRC-003 C-1 SRC-003 C-2 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 FR-ADR-009 FR-ADR-010 FR-ADR-011

Title: Prove screen scope with both halves, so the access test cannot pass vacuously
Description: The single most important test in this lane. A test asserting only that another hall is denied passes against a dashboard that returns nothing for anybody, so the non-empty non-zero half and the strictly-less-than comparison against an administrator are written as assertions in the same test.
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed manager A assigned to screen 1 only, and confirmed bookings with payment.state captured on screen 1 and on screen 2, both inside the local day 2026-08-14 Asia/Kolkata; then in one test: (1) GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day&date=2026-08-14 as A returns 200 with takings_paise greater than 0 and seats_sold greater than 0 - the non-empty non-zero half; (2) that takings_paise equals the value of SELECT COALESCE(SUM(bs.price_paise),0) over screen 1's in-window confirmed captured booking_seat rows exactly; (3) that takings_paise is strictly less than an administrator's takings_paise for the same period, which is the assertion that fails against a query ignoring the filter; (4) the same request with &screen_id=2 as A returns 403 FORBIDDEN - the denied half; (5) the administrator's response for the same period has screen_ids containing both 1 and 2 and seats_sold equal to the sum over both screens; (6) manager B with zero manager_screen_assignment rows returns 200 with scope_empty true and takings_paise 0, not 403 and not the cinema's figure. A test suite containing assertion 4 alone is a failing implementation of this story
SourceRef: P-RPT-02 P-RPT-03 E7 S4 FR-ADR-011 SRC-001 §7.4

Title: Short-circuit an empty scope, and render the two zeros as two different facts
Description: A manager with no assignment sees an empty dashboard and that is the correct state for a new account, not an error. It is a fact about the account, and it must not be byte-identical to the different fact that an assigned manager's halls sold nothing.
AcceptanceCriteria: With manager P holding zero manager_screen_assignment rows, GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=month&date=2026-08-14 returns 200 - not 403, not 404, not 500 - with scope_empty true, screen_ids [], shows 0, seats_sold 0, capacity 0, takings_paise 0, occupancy_pct null and films []; the statement log for that request contains no aggregate query at all, proving the handler short-circuited and never built a predicate from an empty list; a test that deliberately removes the short-circuit and asserts the response is NOT the whole cinema's takings is present as a required negative test; GET /api/reports/showtimes?period=month for P returns 200 with total 0 and rows []; for manager Q assigned to a hall with showtimes but no captured bookings the same request returns scope_empty false, capacity greater than 0, takings_paise 0 and occupancy_pct 0.0; for Q on a date with no showtimes at all it returns scope_empty false, capacity 0 and occupancy_pct null; and the three response bodies differ from one another on scope_empty and occupancy_pct so no two can be rendered identically
SourceRef: P-RPT-08 P-RPT-02 E7 S4 FR-ADR-011 SRC-003 C-1

Title: Sum takings from snapshotted per-seat prices, as integer paise
Description: Takings are the sum of booking_seat.price_paise for confirmed bookings whose payment reached captured, for showtimes whose starts_at falls in the period and whose screen is in scope. Takings are counted on the date of the show, which is RULED and batched for the client to reverse.
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed base price 25000 paise with uplifts 0 basis points Standard and 3333 Premium (both example inputs, seat categories being ASSUMED under SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-01), ST-101 on screen 3 at 2026-08-14T14:00:00Z with 90 Standard and 7 Premium seats on confirmed captured bookings plus one 3-seat booking whose payment.state is failed plus one live 2-seat hold, ST-102 on screen 5 at 2026-08-14T18:15:00Z with 12 Standard, ST-103 on screen 1 at 2026-08-14T14:00:00Z, and ST-104 on screen 3 at 2026-08-14T19:00:00Z; GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day&date=2026-08-14 as manager M assigned screens 3 and 5 returns takings_paise exactly 2783331 as a JSON integer, asserted with isinstance(body['takings_paise'], int) after json.load, never a float and never a formatted string; the failed payment contributes 0, the hold contributes 0, ST-103 is excluded as out of scope and ST-104 is excluded as out of window; a period with no captured bookings returns takings_paise 0 and never null, because the SUM is wrapped in COALESCE; the SUM is cast back to an integer type inside the SQL so no Decimal reaches the serialiser; and the rendered form appears only at the edge as ₹27,833.31
SourceRef: P-RPT-03 E7 S4 FR-ADR-036 FR-ADR-038 FR-ADR-039 FR-ADR-041 SRC-001 §5.5.2

Title: Compute occupancy capacity-weighted, in integer arithmetic, against a frozen denominator
Description: Occupancy is total seats sold over total capacity, never the mean of the per-show percentages, and the denominator is showtime.seat_count_at_creation so retiring a seat next month cannot change last month's figure. Hall sizes are ASSUMED under SRC-003 OPEN-SCALE-02, so the formula is what is fixed and the example capacities are not.
AcceptanceCriteria: With ST-101 selling 97 seats of seat_count_at_creation 150 and ST-102 selling 12 of 220, GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day&date=2026-08-14 as manager M returns seats_sold 109, capacity 370 and occupancy_pct 29.5, computed as (109*2000+370)//(2*370) = 218370//740 = 295, and explicitly not 35.1 which is the mean of the per-show 64.7 and 5.5; a showtime inside the period and scope with zero sales still contributes its seat_count_at_creation to capacity, verified by a case whose occupancy falls when an empty show is added; 1 seat sold of capacity 16 returns 6.3 and not 6.2, fixing half-up rounding; capacity 0 returns occupancy_pct null and never 0.0; a showtime row whose seat_count_at_creation is 0 or null makes the request return 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with 'This period's figures could not be loaded. If you need help, quote a1b2c3d4.' and no partially rendered body; the denominator is never computed from SELECT count(*) FROM seat and never from seat.is_active, asserted by grep over the occupancy query; and no float type appears anywhere in the computation
SourceRef: P-RPT-04 E7 S4 FR-ADR-022 SRC-003 OPEN-SCALE-02 SRC-001 §5.5.2

Title: Group per-film performance inside the caller's scope, under a total order and a 100-row cap
