Description: The same two figures grouped by movie_id, ordered takings_paise descending then title ascending then movie_id ascending. All three keys always: a film has no unique title, and a cap over a non-total order makes which film falls off the end nondeterministic.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day&date=2026-08-14 as manager M returns films holding exactly one row - title DEMO MOVIE 01, shows 2, seats_sold 109, capacity 370, occupancy_pct 29.5, takings_paise 2783331 - and no row for DEMO MOVIE 02 whose only showtime is on screen 1 outside M's scope, while the administrator's response for the same period carries both rows; with two distinct movie rows sharing the title DEMO MOVIE 01 and equal takings_paise, ten consecutive identical requests return the two rows in the same order every time, ordered by takings_paise DESC then title ASC then movie_id ASC; seeding 101 distinct films inside one period returns len(films) == 100 and films_truncated true, and seeding 100 returns films_truncated false with every film present; each film row's figures are that film's performance inside the caller's effective scope, asserted by a manager row differing from the administrator row for the same film; and the headline figures in the same response are never derived by summing films
SourceRef: P-RPT-05 E7 S4 FR-ADR-021 SRC-003 OPEN-SEED-01

Title: Serve EP-RPT-01 from one snapshot: a complete period or nothing
Description: The headline figures and the per-film breakdown come from one request inside one transaction at one snapshot, so the parts sum to the whole. The identity is conditioned on films_truncated being false, and the truncated case asserts the inequality instead of being skipped.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day&date=2026-08-14 runs at REPEATABLE READ, or as a single statement, and returns period, period_start_utc, period_end_utc, evaluated_at_utc, timezone, scope_empty, screen_ids, takings_paise, seats_sold, capacity, occupancy_pct, shows, films and films_truncated in one body; when films_truncated is false the test asserts sum(f['takings_paise'] for f in films) == takings_paise and sum(f['seats_sold'] for f in films) == seats_sold; when films_truncated is true the test asserts both sums are strictly less than the headline and len(films) == 100, and this case is asserted rather than skipped; a test that commits a captured booking from a second connection between the headline computation and the per-film computation still finds both identities hold; injecting a failure into the per-film query returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with 'This period's figures could not be loaded. If you need help, quote a1b2c3d4.' and a body containing no takings_paise key at all, so no partial figures are ever returned; and the request id line is present on the 500 and absent from every 4xx on this endpoint
SourceRef: P-RPT-07 P-RPT-03 P-RPT-04 P-RPT-05 E7 S4 E7 S6 FR-ADR-052 SRC-001 §7.6

Title: Serve the paginated per-show listing on its own endpoint
Description: A month across six halls is on the order of a thousand showtime rows, which would be an unbounded payload on a host with roughly 1 GB of memory in total, so the detail view is a separate paginated endpoint. The interface renders these rows and never sums them into a headline figure.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/reports/showtimes?period=day&date=2026-08-14&limit=50&offset=0 as manager M returns total 2 and two rows ordered by starts_at ascending then screen_id ascending; row one is showtime_id ST-101 with starts_at 2026-08-14T19:30:00+05:30, screen_id 3, screen_name Hall 3, title DEMO MOVIE 01, seats_sold 97, capacity 150, occupancy_pct 64.7, takings_paise 2483331 and has_started false; row two is starts_at 2026-08-14T23:45:00+05:30, screen 5, seats_sold 12, capacity 220, occupancy_pct 5.5, takings_paise 300000, has_started false; has_started is derived from the injected clock 2026-08-14T12:50:00Z against starts_at and reads true for a showtime that precedes it; both rows carry non-zero takings while has_started is false, because takings attach to the show's date; limit=0 and limit=201 each return 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with 'Ask for between 1 and 200 rows.' and offset=-1 returns 422 with 'The row offset cannot be negative.'; omitting limit and offset applies 50 and 0 and the body echoes both; total counts every in-scope showtime in the period and not the page, verified with 214 showtimes returning total 214 with 50 rows; and the endpoint accepts no sort parameter

Title: Serve the scope endpoint so the screen's controls and the server's filter come from one source
Description: The interface cannot render the hall filter or the scope line without knowing which halls the caller may narrow to, and it must not guess. EP-RPT-03 returns exactly what the router dependency resolved.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/reports/scope as manager M assigned screens 3 and 5 returns 200 with role manager, scope_empty false, all_halls false, screens as an array of objects each carrying screen_id, screen_name and is_active in screen_id ascending order and holding exactly halls 3 and 5, timezone Asia/Kolkata, and today 2026-08-14 derived from the injected clock in Asia/Kolkata; as an administrator it returns all_halls true and every screen including any whose is_active is false; as a manager with no assignment it returns scope_empty true and screens []; as a customer 403 FORBIDDEN and unauthenticated 401 AUTH_REQUIRED; a manager's screens array never names a hall absent from their manager_screen_assignment rows, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate which screen ids exist; and the resolver behind this endpoint is the same dependency EP-RPT-01 and EP-RPT-02 filter on, asserted by a test that changes an assignment row and sees all three responses change together
SourceRef: P-RPT-02 P-RPT-08 E7 S6 FR-ADR-011

Title: Mount no write route on the reports router, and answer a non-GET in the standard envelope
Description: The dashboard writes nothing and a manager who reaches an administration write path is refused by that router's role dependency before the body is parsed. A non-GET on a reports path is 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED inside the one error envelope, agreeing with P-XCT-11 and the generated registry.
AcceptanceCriteria: grep over the reports package for router.post, router.put, router.patch and router.delete returns 0 hits; POST /api/reports/dashboard, PUT /api/reports/showtimes, PATCH /api/reports/scope and DELETE /api/reports/audit each return 405 with the standard envelope carrying code METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED and the message 'That action is not available. Nothing was changed.', rendered by the application-level handler mounted on the app and on no router; METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED appears in the errors array of none of EP-RPT-01, EP-RPT-02, EP-RPT-03 or EP-RPT-04, and the API contract generator builds without raising; PATCH /api/showtimes/101 with body base_price_paise 30000 and a manager session returns 403 FORBIDDEN with 'This action is for administrators.', SELECT base_price_paise FROM showtime WHERE id=101 is unchanged, SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log is unchanged before and after, and exactly one structured JSON log line carries the request id, the actor and the refused route; and opening the dashboard as a manager writes no audit_log row, because FR-ADR-019 audits writes only
SourceRef: P-RPT-09 E7 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 FR-ADR-009 FR-ADR-019 FR-ADR-052

Title: Ship no export of any kind, and return no customer-level row from any reports endpoint
Description: The client answered No to an export, and this surface additionally returns no customer name, email, booking reference or per-booking row anywhere, so even a screenshot discloses no customer. A browser's own print and save-page are outside this product's control and no claim is made about them.
AcceptanceCriteria: No response from any /api/reports/ path carries a Content-Disposition header of any disposition; GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day with the header Accept: text/csv returns 200 with Content-Type application/json, content negotiation being unimplemented; GET /api/reports/dashboard.csv returns 404 because no such route exists; grep -rn over the dashboard and change-log frontend modules for download, Blob, createObjectURL, Content-Disposition, text/csv and xlsx returns 0 hits, and no print stylesheet paginates either screen; and a test walks the full JSON of EP-RPT-01, EP-RPT-02, EP-RPT-03 and EP-RPT-04 against the union of every seeded customer name, customer email address and booking reference and finds zero occurrences
SourceRef: P-RPT-10 E7 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-REPORT-02 FR-ADR-043

Title: Serve the administrator-only change log, filtered and cursor-paginated
Description: This is the reading surface for audit_log and it answers the client's own question - who changed a price and what was it before. Admin-only is a stricter adoption than SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 requires and is recorded as one, so widening it to managers later is a decision rather than a drift.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/reports/audit?from=2026-08-12&to=2026-08-12&action=showtime.base_price_changed as an administrator returns 200 with window_start_utc 2026-08-11T18:30:00Z, window_end_utc 2026-08-12T18:30:00Z and one row carrying id, occurred_at 2026-08-12T15:40:00+05:30, actor_user_id, actor_email, actor_role admin copied at write time, action showtime.base_price_changed, entity_type showtime, entity_id 101, before {base_price_paise: 25000}, after {base_price_paise: 30000} and request_id, with before and after returned verbatim and never unit-converted; the same request as a manager returns 403 FORBIDDEN with 'This page is for administrators.' and as a customer or guest returns 403 or 401; rows are ordered by id descending and next_cursor is the lowest id returned or null at the end; from later than to returns 422 with 'The start date must be on or before the end date.'; a malformed date returns 422 with 'The date must be written as YYYY-MM-DD.'; limit=0 and limit=201 return 422 with 'Ask for between 1 and 200 rows.'; entity_id sent without entity_type returns 422 with 'Choose a record type before filtering by record id.'; cursor=0 and cursor=abc return 422 with 'That page of results is no longer valid. Start again from the newest change.' while cursor=999999 naming no audit_log row returns 200 with the rows whose id is lower and no message about the cursor; a well-formed non-member action and a well-formed non-member actor_user_id each return 200 with rows []; from and to default to today and thirty days before it from the injected clock; and SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log is identical before and after every request above, reading the log being unaudited
SourceRef: P-RPT-11 E7 S4 E7 S6 FR-ADR-019 FR-ADR-012 SRC-001 §7.6 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03

Title: Derive both change-log option sets from the date window alone
Description: available_actions and available_actors are the distinct values present inside from..to, ignoring the action filter, the actor filter and the page. Under the other reading each select collapses to the option already chosen and the two selects rewrite each other, which is not a pair of filters.
AcceptanceCriteria: Seed three audit rows inside [2026-08-11T18:30:00Z, 2026-08-12T18:30:00Z) - id 31 showtime.base_price_changed by actor 1, id 30 movie.published by actor 1, id 29 movie.published by actor 4; GET /api/reports/audit?from=2026-08-12&to=2026-08-12&action=showtime.base_price_changed returns rows of length 1 while available_actions equals the two-element list movie.published then showtime.base_price_changed in ascending order and available_actors equals the two entries for actor 1 and actor 4 ordered by actor_email ascending; adding &actor_user_id=4 returns rows [] with both option sets byte-identical to the previous response; adding &limit=1 and paging with &cursor=30 leaves both sets byte-identical; changing only from and to is the sole way either set changes, and narrowing to a window holding no rows returns both as []; widening to from=2026-08-01 grows each set to the distinct values actually present and never to every member of the published action vocabulary and never to every account holding the admin role; each available_actors entry carries actor_user_id and actor_email and no role; and an account that acted under two roles inside one window appears once in available_actors and twice in rows with a different actor_role on each
SourceRef: P-RPT-11 E7 S4 E7 S6 FR-ADR-019

Title: Compute every figure live from stored rows, with the required indexes and no rollup
Description: Nothing in this system runs on a schedule, so nothing is precomputed: no rollup table, no materialised view, no nightly summary, no cached report and no background warm-up. A cached report is a stale report a manager will act on.
AcceptanceCriteria: grep over migrations and the application for MATERIALIZED VIEW, rollup and report cache returns 0 hits in the reports path, and no Redis key holds a dashboard response - two identical GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day&date=2026-08-14 requests separated by one captured booking return different takings_paise; the Alembic history creates indexes showtime(starts_at), showtime(screen_id, starts_at), booking(showtime_id), booking_seat(booking_id), booking(payment_id) and payment(state); EXPLAIN of the day aggregate shows the plan driving from showtime on showtime(starts_at) or showtime(screen_id, starts_at) and not a sequential scan of booking_seat; the payment join is written payment.id = booking.payment_id and no query references a payment.booking_id column, which does not exist; no figure on this surface is read from /metrics; and no reporting work is performed inside the booking confirmation transaction, asserted by grep over the confirmation path for any reports module import
SourceRef: P-RPT-12 E7 S4 FR-ADR-005 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-057 SRC-003 OPEN-PROC-01 SRC-002 §5.4.1

Title: Rate-limit the reports router per user, and fail closed when Redis is unreachable
Description: One per-user token bucket named REPORTS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER_PER_MINUTE with a starting value of 60, an estimate to be tuned once measured. No per-IP bucket, because every caller here is authenticated and a per-IP bucket would put twelve managers in one building into one bucket.
AcceptanceCriteria: REPORTS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER_PER_MINUTE is validated at boot as a positive integer and the application exits non-zero with a message naming the variable when it is absent, empty or non-numeric; with it set to 60, the 61st GET /api/reports/dashboard from one user inside a 60 second window returns 429 with code RATE_LIMITED, a Retry-After header of 1, and the message 'Too many requests. Try again in 1 second.' in the singular; the wait is computed at render time as ceil(window_seconds / capacity) = ceil(60/60) = 1 and grep over the frontend finds no hardcoded retry number and specifically no occurrence of the string 30 seconds; a second user's first request inside that same window returns 200, proving the bucket is per user, and no per-IP bucket exists; the bucket is shared across EP-RPT-01, EP-RPT-02, EP-RPT-03 and EP-RPT-04, verified by exhausting it on one and being refused on another; with Redis stopped every /api/reports/ endpoint returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with 'The dashboard cannot be loaded right now. A service it depends on is unreachable.' and never serves an unlimited response; and this bucket appears as one row in the cross-cutting rate-limit table and configuration inventory and nowhere else
SourceRef: P-RPT-12 E7 S4 FR-ADR-028 FR-ADR-058 SRC-002 §7.1

Title: Build the dashboard's opening load, scope line and hall filter
Description: The screen opens on period=day with date omitted and issues three requests, not one: EP-RPT-03 and EP-RPT-01 together on mount, EP-RPT-02 after EP-RPT-01 returns. Hall names live on EP-RPT-03 alone, because EP-RPT-01's screen_ids is an array of integers. The out-of-service hall rule is P-ADM-16's, applied here and not restated.
AcceptanceCriteria: On mounting /dashboard the screen issues exactly two requests in parallel - GET /api/reports/scope and GET /api/reports/dashboard?period=day with date omitted - and issues GET /api/reports/showtimes?period=day&limit=50&offset=0 only after the dashboard request resolves, asserted in a component test with a mocked fetch that records call order and timing; the Day tab is selected on arrival and exactly one period tab is selected at all times; date is omitted rather than computed on the client, and grep over the dashboard module finds no client-side date or timezone arithmetic; the scope line renders 'Halls shown: Hall 3, Hall 5.' for manager M by looking each id of EP-RPT-01's screen_ids up in EP-RPT-03's screens array in screen_id ascending order, and never renders 'Halls shown: 3, 5.'; for an administrator it renders 'Halls shown: every hall.'; applying &screen_id=3 changes the line to name Hall 3 alone while the hall filter still offers both; the hall filter's first option is 'All my halls' for a manager and 'All halls' for an administrator and submits no screen_id, the remaining options are EP-RPT-03's screens in screen_id ascending order labelled with screen_name, and a hall whose is_active is false renders its name followed by ' — out of service' and remains selectable with figures unchanged; and when scope_empty is true both the scope line and the hall filter are absent from the DOM rather than rendered empty
SourceRef: P-RPT-02 P-RPT-08 E7 S5 FR-ADR-011

Title: Render the dashboard's figures, its states and its period line
Description: Money is formatted from integer paise at render time only, a figure renders only when the whole response has arrived, and the three empty states render three different ways. The week period line owes two forms, because a week whose two dates fall in different years reads a wrong year against a money figure under the one-year form.
AcceptanceCriteria: takings_paise 2783331 renders as ₹27,833.31 with Indian digit grouping and tabular figures, formatted at the edge only, and no response body anywhere in this lane contains a formatted money string; the four figures render together and no test state exists in which one figure has a value while another shows a loading block, and a period change clears the previous figures rather than leaving them under a spinner; the period line renders 'Friday 14 August 2026' for day, 'Monday 10 August to Sunday 16 August 2026' for a week inside one year, 'Monday 29 December 2025 to Sunday 4 January 2026' for ISO week 1 of 2026 whose dates fall in two years, and 'August 2026' for month, all derived from a local anchor date by calendar arithmetic with no instant converted on the client; scope_empty true renders all four figures as '—', the occupancy bar absent, both tables absent, and the single line 'No halls are assigned to this account. Ask an administrator to assign one.' with no danger surface, no error banner and no alert role; capacity 0 renders takings ₹0.00, occupancy '—' with the bar absent, and 'No shows were scheduled in this period.'; capacity above 0 with seats_sold 0 renders ₹0.00, 0.0 % with the bar at zero width, and 'No seats were sold in this period.'; films_truncated true renders 'Showing the top 100 films by takings. The figures above cover every film in this period.' and leaves the four figures unchanged and unstyled as an error; the per-film caption reads 'Per film, in your halls' for a manager and 'Per film' for an administrator; the live-figures note renders two sentences for a manager and the first alone for an administrator, and no change-log link appears in a manager's DOM; and a per-show row with has_started false renders 'Still selling'
SourceRef: P-RPT-04 P-RPT-05 P-RPT-07 P-RPT-08 P-RPT-11 E7 S5 FR-ADR-036

Title: Make the dashboard operable and announced, with only the per-film table sortable
Description: The per-show table cannot honestly be sortable, because EP-RPT-02 accepts no sort parameter and a client-side sort would reorder one page while claiming to describe the period. Every control in the focus order has a published string.
AcceptanceCriteria: Keyboard traversal of /dashboard visits period tabs, then the period stepper, then the hall filter, then the change log link for an administrator only, then the per-film table, then the per-show table, then the per-show pagination, in that order, with a visible focus ring at every stop; the period stepper's accessible names read 'Previous day' and 'Next day' on the day view, 'Previous week' and 'Next week' on the week view, and 'Previous month' and 'Next month' on the month view; the per-film table's six headers are buttons carrying aria-sort and the per-show table's seven headers are plain column headers with no button, no aria-sort and no sort affordance; a sortable header's accessible name is its text plus ', sort by this column' when unsorted, ', sorted highest first. Activate to sort lowest first' when descending and ', sorted lowest first. Activate to sort highest first' when ascending, and the takings header carries the descending form on first render; every client-side re-sort of the per-film table falls back to title ascending then movie_id ascending, so toggling a column and toggling back restores the original row order exactly; the occupancy bar is aria-hidden and the percentage text is present whenever the bar is; a polite live region announces the period and the headline figures once per period change and announces 'Shows 51 to 100 of 214' on a page change, rendering 'Showing the only show in this period' when total is 1; a pagination control at the end of its range is absent from the DOM rather than disabled; when scope_empty is true the hall filter, both tables and the pagination are absent from the focus order and nothing is rendered disabled to hold a place; each table scrolls inside its own overflow-x auto container and the page body does not scroll horizontally at 320 px width; and an automated accessibility scan of the screen reports 0 violations
SourceRef: P-RPT-05 P-RPT-06 E7 S5 FR-ADR-051

Title: Build the change-log screen, with both selects populated from the response
Description: The action select and the administrator select are populated from available_actions and available_actors and from nothing else - no hardcoded list, no second endpoint, and no staff directory exists in this product. Filters submit only on Apply, because a date pair is two fields.
AcceptanceCriteria: On /dashboard/audit the Action select's options come from available_actions and the Administrator select's from available_actors, and grep over the module finds no hardcoded action list and no request to any endpoint listing staff accounts; the first options are 'Any action' and 'Any administrator' and submit nothing; an empty option set renders the any option alone plus the help lines 'Nothing was changed in this period.' and 'Nobody changed anything in this period.' with both selects still enabled; the filters do not auto-submit, so typing a from date later than the current to fires no request and no 422 is raised while the reader is still typing; a date change that removes a selected option clears that filter and announces 'The action filter was cleared. No change of that kind was recorded in this period.' or 'The administrator filter was cleared. That account made no changes in this period.' through the same live region as the result count, and selecting an action never changes the administrator options and vice versa; the result count region reads '1 change.' at exactly one and '0 changes.' and '12 changes.' otherwise; a before/after pair renders base_price_paise with 25000 and 30000 side by side, verbatim with the field name and never as ₹250.00 and ₹300.00; occurred_at renders '12 Aug 2026, 3:40 pm' and never 15:40 and never with a zone suffix, the panel's zone note carrying the zone once; the row list is a table with column headers 'When', 'Who', 'Action', 'Record', 'Before', 'After' and pages with 'Load older changes', ending on 'That is the oldest change in this period.'; a manager reaching the route sees the whole panel replaced by the single line 'This page is for administrators.' with no filters and no empty list; and the module contains no export, download or copy-all control
SourceRef: P-RPT-11 P-RPT-10 E7 S5 FR-ADR-019 FR-ADR-051

Title: Prove the exclusions by absence
Description: The eighteen P-SCP rows describe capabilities this product deliberately does not have. This epic turns each into a test that fails if somebody builds the excluded thing by accident, and — where SRC-001 6.6 preserves an affordance for later — proves the affordance is still there and still exposed by nothing.

Title: Freeze the mounted route set against the published contract
Description: The 58-endpoint inventory in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json is the scope boundary in machine-readable form. A route mounted that is not in it is scope creep with a URL. This guard runs from the first phase that mounts a router and every later phase inherits it. It is one-directional on purpose: a mounted route absent from the contract fails, a contract route not yet mounted does not, because completeness belongs to the other lanes.
AcceptanceCriteria: A test collects every route mounted on the FastAPI application and asserts (a) the set difference mounted-minus-contract is empty against the 58 (method, path) pairs in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json, whose endpoint_count field reads 58; and (b) no mounted path matches the case-insensitive regex cancel|refund|validat|check-?in|export|download|\.csv|import|sync|tmdb|scan|pos/|till. Against the running application GET /api/export/bookings.csv, POST /api/bookings/by-reference/FR-ABCD-2345/cancel, POST /api/bookings/by-reference/FR-ABCD-2345/validate, POST /api/admin/movies/import and GET /api/pos/sales each return 404 NOT_FOUND rendered by the global exception handler, with no request id because it is a 4xx.
SourceRef: P-SCP-05 P-SCP-06 P-SCP-10 P-SCP-11 P-SCP-14 S2 S3.8 SRC-001 §6

Title: Hold the process and dependency inventory to three processes and no excluded machinery
Description: Three long-running processes exist, not four, and nothing runs on a schedule. A scheduler, a QR encoder, a spreadsheet writer or a model SDK entering the dependency list is how an excluded capability arrives before anyone writes a screen for it, so the manifest is guarded, not only the code.
AcceptanceCriteria: docker-compose.yml defines exactly three application services — api, worker and the static frontend — and no service whose name, image or command matches sched|cron|beat|celery; grep -riE 'apscheduler|celery|dramatiq|BackgroundScheduler|schedule\.every|crontab' over backend/ frontend/src/ scripts/ returns zero matches after lines whose first non-whitespace characters are # or // are stripped, so a comment saying no scheduler exists does not fail the check; backend/requirements.txt and frontend/package.json list no entry matching qrcode|segno|barcode|zxing|reportlab|openpyxl|xlsxwriter|weasyprint|openai|anthropic|langchain|tmdb; and a test that patches the HTTP client's send method fails the suite on any outbound request whose host is not one of the configured SES, S3 and SQS endpoints — the simulated payment provider makes no outbound request at all.
SourceRef: P-SCP-06 P-SCP-07 P-SCP-09 P-SCP-14 P-SCP-17 S2 FR-ADR-005 FR-ADR-006

Title: Enumerate configuration so no excluded capability can be switched on by a variable
Description: Configuration is the other door an excluded capability walks through. The settings model names every variable it reads, so a TMDB key or a sweep interval cannot be added without changing that enumeration. PAYMENT_PROVIDER carries the sharpest rule in the specification: it has no default, because a default is how a deployment becomes a fake shop silently.
AcceptanceCriteria: The settings model's field list contains no name matching TMDB|MOVIE_API|API_KEY|SCHEDULE|CRON|INTERVAL|SWEEP, asserted by iterating the model's declared fields; starting the API with PAYMENT_PROVIDER unset exits non-zero before it binds a port and the message names the variable; starting it with PAYMENT_PROVIDER=stripe exits non-zero and the message names simulated as the only permitted value; and with PAYMENT_PROVIDER=simulated, GET /health/ready returns 200 with body field payment_provider equal to the string simulated.
SourceRef: P-SCP-06 P-SCP-07 P-SCP-12 S2 S7.9 FR-ADR-041

Title: Assert the excluded tables and columns are absent from the migrated schema
Description: A column is cheaper to add than to remove once rows exist, so the schema is where an excluded capability becomes permanent. This asserts the absences the specification names. Note one near-miss the test must not trip over: used_at exists legitimately on password_reset_token and is forbidden only on booking.
AcceptanceCriteria: After alembic upgrade head against an empty database, SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='booking' returns no name matching used_at|discount|fee|tax|refund|points|concession; SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public' returns no name matching refund|loyalty|point|tier|membership|discount|coupon|voucher|convenience_fee|tax|concession|order_line|checkin|check_in; and the same query against table_name='user' returns no column name matching tier|points|loyalty|membership. The password_reset_token.used_at column is explicitly excluded from the check and must still exist.
SourceRef: P-SCP-02 P-SCP-03 P-SCP-10 P-SCP-16 S2 FR-ADR-040 FR-ADR-048

Title: Assert the preserved affordances exist and are not mistaken for excluded surfaces
Description: Excluded is not blocked. Three things exist in the schema precisely because v1 does not use them, and a later session reading the exclusions could delete all three as dead weight. This story fails if any of them is missing — asserting their absence would be the defect, not the guard. Their non-exposure is a separate story, S-SCP-14, because it cannot be tested until a booking exists.
AcceptanceCriteria: After alembic upgrade head, information_schema.columns shows table booking carrying a status column and a cancelled_at timestamp column that is nullable with no default; SELECT count(*) FROM cinema returns exactly 1 after the seed runs; table screen carries a NOT NULL cinema_id foreign key referencing cinema(id); and GET /api/reference returns a cinemas array of length 1 — the filter capability is present in the payload whether or not the control renders, which is E-BRW's rule and not this story's. All four assertions are positive: each fails if the thing is absent.
SourceRef: P-SCP-11 S2 S2.5 SRC-001 §6.6 FR-ADR-010 FR-ADR-013

Title: Hold the role set at exactly four and prove no cinema-staff role exists
Description: SRC-001 4.3's staff member scanning a ticket is withdrawn and 5.5.3 with it. Four roles exist: guest, customer, manager, admin. The role set itself is PROVISIONAL under SRC-003 C-1 and this story asserts the count that is written down, not a count it chose; what is not provisional is the removal of the staff role, which the ruling kills explicitly.
AcceptanceCriteria: The role enumeration in backend/app/ satisfies set equality against exactly {guest, customer, manager, admin} and len() == 4; no member name matches staff|usher|door|gate|scanner|attendant; grep -riE 'cinema_?staff|door_?scanner|ticket_?validat' backend/app/ frontend/src/ matches nothing; and POST /api/auth/register with a body carrying role: staff returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID because no request schema in the product accepts a role property at all.
SourceRef: P-SCP-10 P-SCP-15 S2 S3.1 FR-ADR-009 SRC-003 C-1

Title: Prove the admin has no way to withdraw a showtime, without ruling what withdrawal would do
Description: P-SCP-18 is not an exclusion — it is OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01, reserved as money and irreversible, and this story answers none of it. It asserts only what v1 is specified to do: the capability is absent from every surface. An unbuilt capability is recoverable and an unrefunded customer is not, which is why absence is the right shape while the row is open. No withdrawal flow, refund behaviour, notification or policy may be introduced by this story, not even as a placeholder.
AcceptanceCriteria: No route mounted under /api/admin/showtimes accepts DELETE and no mounted path contains withdraw or cancel: DELETE /api/admin/showtimes/1 returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED from the global handler and POST /api/admin/showtimes/1/withdraw returns 404 NOT_FOUND; the admin showtime list and edit screens render no control whose accessible name matches withdraw|cancel|delete|pull; and PATCH /api/admin/showtimes/{showtime_id} with a body property status, withdrawn or cancelled_at returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID as an unknown property.
SourceRef: P-SCP-18 S2 FR-ADR-023

Title: Prove the seat map carries no accessible marking, no pair linkage and no gap rule
Description: Every seat is sold individually and any available seat may be chosen. The guard matters most for the lock: a paired seat would turn a per-seat lock into a per-group lock, which is a materially harder concurrency problem, so the absence of pairing is a property the concurrency proof depends on. Recorded, not challenged: a real cinema in India operates under accessibility obligations and this rests on there being no real customers.
AcceptanceCriteria: The seat objects in GET /api/showtimes/{showtime_id}/seatmap carry no key matching accessible|wheelchair|pair|couple|companion|gap|group, asserted against the response schema in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json and against a live response; information_schema.columns for table seat returns no column name matching those tokens; POST /api/showtimes/{showtime_id}/holds for seats A-01 and A-03 on a row where A-02 is available returns 201 — no rule refuses the single-seat gap; and that hold creates exactly two Redis lock keys, one per seat, asserted by counting keys matching the hold key pattern.
SourceRef: P-SCP-13 S2 FR-ADR-016 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-02 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-03 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-04

Title: Prove one responsive web interface exists and no native or installable artefact does
Description: The substitute the client named themselves is a website that works well on a phone. The guard has two halves: no native or app-store artefact anywhere in the repository, and the hardest case the responsive interface has actually working — the largest hall's seat map on a 375-pixel screen. The 220-seat figure is ASSUMED under OPEN-SCALE-02 and this story cites it as the design target the PRD names, not as a ruled hall size.
AcceptanceCriteria: The repository contains no path matching ios/|android/|*.xcodeproj|AndroidManifest.xml|*.webmanifest|capacitor.config.*, and frontend/package.json lists no dependency matching react-native|capacitor|cordova|expo; no file under frontend/src/ registers a service worker or adds a beforeinstallprompt listener, asserted by grep -riE 'serviceWorker|beforeinstallprompt'; and at a 375-pixel viewport the 220-seat hall's seat map scrolls horizontally inside its own container while document.body.scrollWidth equals document.body.clientWidth, and the rendered seat cell's computed width equals the design system's seat-cell token value unchanged from the value it computes to at a 1280-pixel viewport — the cell is never shrunk to avoid the scroll.

Title: Prove the public surface offers no upcoming section, no language switch and no recommendation
Description: Three exclusions share one surface — the shell, the listing and its controls — so they share one guard. Two near-misses must be checked and cleared rather than assumed: the Language filter is the film's language and not the interface's, and the default listing order is an ordering with a stated tiebreak, not a recommendation. Which sort orders a customer may choose is OPEN-SORT-01 and this story asserts only that the order is deterministic and identical between callers, not what the order should be.
AcceptanceCriteria: The frontend router registers no route for /upcoming or /coming-soon and both render the 404 view; the shell renders no control whose accessible name matches language|locale|translate|coming soon|pre-sale|notify me|recommend|for you, and grep -riE 'i18n|react-intl|formatjs|gettext|recommend' frontend/package.json frontend/src/ matches nothing; the listing's Language control sends language= as a query parameter to GET /api/movies and changes no interface string, asserted by comparing the rendered chrome before and after a change; and two consecutive calls to GET /api/movies with no sort parameter, one anonymous and one as a signed-in customer, return identical id sequences in the documented default order with the documented tiebreak.
SourceRef: P-SCP-04 P-SCP-08 P-SCP-17 S2 FR-ADR-021 FR-ADR-044 SRC-003 OPEN-MODEL-01

Title: Prove no point-of-sale integration exists and name the writers against the seat constraint
Description: Seats sold online are the only seats this system knows about. The guard is that nothing imports or exports counter sales and that the set of code paths writing seat occupancy stays small enough to enumerate — which is also what would make a counter sale safe to add later, since it would be another writer against the same unique constraint. The operational consequence, that a seat sold at the counter renders available, is recorded in P-SCP-05 and needs no code.
AcceptanceCriteria: No mounted route, module or configuration variable matches pos|till|counter_sale|terminal_sale, asserted by grep -riE '\bpos\b|till|counter_?sale|terminal_?sale' backend/app/ frontend/src/ plus the route guard in S-SCP-01; and a test that registers a SQLAlchemy before_insert listener on booking_seat, records the module of each calling frame across the whole suite, and asserts that set of caller modules is exactly two — the booking confirmation path and scripts/seed.py — failing if a third appears. A textual grep for INSERT is explicitly not the check, because an ORM insert contains no such string.

Title: Prove no card data and no real provider exist anywhere, and that the demonstration line always renders
Description: A simulated payment that looks real to a customer is the worst failure this product can produce: it takes their seat, takes nothing else, and they find out at the door. So the guard is both halves — nothing card-shaped exists to be filled in, and every screen says so in words. No real provider is ever integrated, which makes the no-card-data rule trivially satisfiable; the point of the test is that it stays satisfied after someone adds a fixture out of habit.
AcceptanceCriteria: No Pydantic request model in backend/app/ declares a field matching card|pan|cvv|cvc|expiry|expiration|cardholder, asserted by iterating every model's fields; grep -riE 'card_?number|cvv|cvc|expiry_?(month|year)|stripe|razorpay|payu|paypal|braintree|adyen' backend/ frontend/src/ scripts/ matches nothing except the literal copy string below; the checkout screen renders no input whose name, id, autocomplete or label matches those tokens; the exact string 'Demonstration environment. Payments are simulated and no card details are ever taken.' renders inside the single contentinfo landmark on every route, checked on /, the listing, the seat map, checkout and the confirmation page; and a confirmed booking writes a payment row driven pending then authorized then captured with zero outbound HTTP requests, asserted by the host allow-list test in S-SCP-02.
Labels: backend frontend security money test scope-guard
SourceRef: P-SCP-12 S2 S7.9 FR-ADR-041 SRC-003 OPEN-PAY-01

Title: Prove the charged total is the sum of the seat prices and carries no other line
Description: Four exclusions land on one figure — no food and beverage line, no loyalty balance, no discount or concession rate, no booking fee and no separate tax line. The limit is stated rather than discovered: the stored total is a single figure and cannot be split into net and tax retrospectively, because nothing records what portion was ever meant to be what. Adding a component later works going forward only.
AcceptanceCriteria: For a booking of three seats priced 25000, 25000 and 30000 paise, POST /api/bookings stores total_paise = 80000 and SELECT sum(price_paise) FROM booking_seat WHERE booking_id = :id returns 80000; no response schema in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json and no live response body carries a key matching fee|booking_fee|convenience|tax|gst|vat|discount|promo|coupon|concession|loyalty|points|food|beverage|order_line; POST /api/bookings with a promo_code or discount_code property returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID as an unknown property; and the confirmation page and the receipt each render exactly one total line with no sub-line and no space reserved for one.
SourceRef: P-SCP-02 P-SCP-03 P-SCP-16 S2 FR-ADR-038 FR-ADR-040

Title: Prove booking status and cancelled_at are exposed by no endpoint and settable by none
Description: The columns exist because excluded is not blocked; S-SCP-05 proves they exist. This story proves the other half — nothing reads them out and nothing writes them in — and publishes the ruled absence to the customer in words, because silence does not tell a ruled absence from a feature they have failed to find. A customer who cannot attend loses their money: recorded, not challenged.
AcceptanceCriteria: For a confirmed booking, the bodies of GET /api/me/bookings, GET /api/me/bookings/{reference} and GET /api/bookings/by-reference/{reference} contain no booking-level key status or cancelled_at, asserted key-by-key against the live responses and against their response schemas in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json; POST /api/bookings carrying status or cancelled_at returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID; SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE cancelled_at IS NOT NULL returns 0 after the full suite has run and SELECT DISTINCT status FROM booking returns exactly one value; and the confirmation page renders the exact string 'This booking cannot be changed, cancelled or refunded.' beneath the entry line on first render and on a later visit alike.
SourceRef: P-SCP-11 S2 FR-ADR-013 SRC-003 OPEN-CANCEL-01 SRC-003 OPEN-CANCEL-02

Title: Prove no scannable artefact is generated in the receipt or on screen
Description: No image is generated anywhere, in the email or on screen. Entry is a person reading FR-XXXX-XXXX aloud and typing it. The story is phased at 5 because that is the first phase where both surfaces exist — the confirmation screen from 4 and the receipt message from 5 — and a guard that only covers one of the two is not the guard. OPEN-REFCHAR-01 asks whether the reference needs a check character or a narrower alphabet and is open and reserved: this story asserts the alphabet P-TKT-01 publishes and adds nothing to it.
AcceptanceCriteria: The receipt message the worker hands to the mail transport, captured from the stub transport's stdout and parsed as MIME, contains no img element, no cid: reference, no attachment part and no data:image URI; the confirmation page and the booking detail page render no img, svg or canvas element inside the reference block; grep -riE 'qrcode|qr_code|barcode|segno|zxing|pyzbar' backend/ frontend/src/ matches nothing; and the reference renders as text whose content matches the pattern P-TKT-01 publishes and contains none of the characters 0 1 I L O U.
SourceRef: P-SCP-09 P-SCP-10 S2 FR-ADR-015 SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-01

Title: Prove the dashboard offers no export, download or print-to-file path
Description: This is more than a missing feature: it keeps customer-level booking data off any download path, so the exposure is removed rather than managed. Phased at 8 because that is the phase the dashboard exists to guard; the endpoint half of the same rule is already guarded from phase 1 by S-SCP-01.
AcceptanceCriteria: No dashboard route renders a control whose accessible name matches export|download|csv|excel|spreadsheet|pdf|save as, and no anchor on any dashboard route carries a download attribute, asserted over the rendered DOM; responses from GET /api/reports/dashboard, GET /api/reports/showtimes, GET /api/reports/scope and GET /api/reports/audit each carry Content-Type application/json and no Content-Disposition header; and GET /api/reports/dashboard.csv, GET /api/reports/export and GET /api/admin/bookings.csv each return 404 NOT_FOUND.
SourceRef: P-SCP-14 S2 FR-ADR-043 SRC-003 OPEN-REPORT-02

Title: Seat selection and the hold
Description: Everything between a customer looking at a seat map and a customer having seats that are provably theirs for 180 seconds: what a tap does, what the running total says, and the hold itself - acquiring it, its expiry, giving seats back and every way it can fail. A Redis lock provides the hold; the database's unique constraint on (showtime_id, seat_id) provides the truth.
Labels: backend frontend concurrency money a11y test
SourceRef: E2 S4 E2 S5 E2 S6 SRC-001 §2.2 SRC-001 §5.2.5 SRC-002 §7.1 SRC-002 §7.9 SRC-002 §E E-1 SRC-003 OPEN-HOLD-01 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-01 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02

Title: Render the four seat states from the three wire values
Description: The seat map carries exactly four rendered states - available, sold, held_by_other, held_by_me - over an enum the server emits with only three values, because the map is one shared cached payload and the server does not know whose session is reading it. The client decides held_by_me against held_by_other from its own hold token, and a chosen-but-not-yet-held seat reuses the held_by_me treatment.
AcceptanceCriteria: Given a seat-map payload in which seat 402 carries state `held`, with no hold token in sessionStorage the cell renders the held_by_other treatment (fill --fr-seat-held-other, solid horizontal bar) and its accessible name ends `held by another customer` and it is not tappable; with a hold token in sessionStorage whose seat list contains 402, the identical payload renders 402 as held_by_me (fill --fr-seat-mine, 2px --fr-seat-edge-mine, tick) with its accessible name ending `held by you`; a seat id present in fr.selection but in no hold also renders the held_by_me treatment, and no fifth rendering exists in the component (asserted by a count of the state branches returning 4); a payload seat whose state is `held_by_me`, `held_by_other`, or any value outside the three wire values `available` / `sold` / `held` is rejected client-side and the screen renders `The seat map could not be loaded.` with a control reading `Try again`; a seat object arriving with no is_active field is rejected identically, and the test asserts the rejection rather than a default of true; a seat with is_active false renders with no fill, a 1px dashed --fr-rule border and a --fr-ink-muted number, keeps its place in the arrow-key grid, reads `Row C seat 12, Premium, out of service`, and does not activate on Enter or Space in any of the four states; the map is one tab stop and not 220, asserted by counting tabbable elements inside the map container as exactly 1.
SourceRef: P-SEA-02 E2 S4 E2 SCR-SEA-01 FR-ADR-045 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-051 SRC-001 §5.2.2

Title: Choose and unchoose seats without taking anything
Description: Selecting and deselecting is entirely client-side: no request is sent, no Redis key is written, no row is inserted, and nothing on the server distinguishes a guest looking at a seat map from a customer looking at one. Scarcity is consumed only at the hold. The live selection lives under the sessionStorage key fr.selection, which is a different key from fr.pending_selection (owned by E5 / P-ACC-13) and may not be collapsed into it.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the map loaded, tapping seat C12 whose state is `available` adds it to the local selection, writes fr.selection in sessionStorage containing that seat id, and issues zero network requests (asserted by a request spy reporting 0 calls); tapping it again removes it and rewrites fr.selection; tapping a seat whose state is `sold`, a seat rendered held_by_other, or a seat whose is_active is false changes neither the selection nor fr.selection and issues zero requests; with ten seats chosen, an eleventh tap does not add the seat, the map does not change, and the note under the total reads `Up to 10 seats.` with the number interpolating MAX_SEATS_PER_BOOKING; reloading /showtimes/7 restores the selection from fr.selection and re-checks it against the freshly fetched map; fr.selection is deleted when the selection empties and when those seats become a hold; this story's code never writes or reads fr.pending_selection, asserted by a grep of the seat-map module finding zero occurrences of that key; closing the tab with a selection and no hold issues zero requests and leaves zero Redis keys, asserted by `redis KEYS lock:seat:7:*` returning empty.
SourceRef: P-SEA-01 P-SEA-03 E2 S4 E2 SCR-SEA-01 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-014 SRC-001 §4.1

Title: Show the running total in integer paise, summing only
Description: The price summary shows a total that changes with every selection and that is the figure the payment step will charge. The seat-map payload carries price_paise per seat already rounded by the server, and the client only sums integers - one implementation of the arithmetic, which is what removes the two-screens-disagree risk.
AcceptanceCriteria: With base_price_paise = 25000 and category uplifts Premium 1250 and Recliner 3333 basis points, so that the payload carries server-rounded price_paise of 28125 for Premium and 33333 for Recliner: selecting two Premium seats then three Recliner seats renders the total after each tap as `₹281.25`, `₹562.50`, `₹895.83`, `₹1,229.16`, `₹1,562.49`, and the final running sum is the integer 156249 paise; the rejected round-once-at-the-end path would give 156248 and the test asserts 156249; the client performs no multiplication, no division and no rounding - a grep of the price-summary module finds no occurrence of uplift_basis_points, no `/`, no `//` and no rounding call; with no seats chosen the panel keeps its full height, the total reads `₹0.00` and the note reads `Up to 10 seats.`; if any selected seat has no known price the total is not rendered at all (asserted by the total element being absent, not empty) and the primary action is disabled; a price_paise that is not a non-negative integer causes the payload to be rejected with `The seat map could not be loaded.` and a control reading `Try again`; the figure is rendered in --fr-font-mono with Indian digit grouping and the ₹ symbol, from integer paise, at render time only - no float appears anywhere in the module; there is no tax line, no discount field and no booking fee element in the rendered DOM.
SourceRef: P-SEA-04 E2 S4 E2 SCR-SEA-01 FR-ADR-038 FR-ADR-036 FR-ADR-040 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01 SRC-001 §5.2.4

Title: Announce a chosen seat that has gone, with no request sent
Description: A poll, a reload or a return to the tab re-checks the local selection against a fresh map and a chosen seat has gone. Nothing was requested so nothing answered: this notice carries no error code, and before this story the only announced surface on the screen branched on a code (journey defect J-XCT-08). The return-from-sign-in case is a different situation with a different string and belongs to P-ACC-13 in lane E5 - it is not rendered by this code path.
AcceptanceCriteria: After a poll, a reload or a return to the tab re-checks fr.selection against a freshly fetched map and finds chosen seat C12 is no longer `available`, the SCR-SEA-03 banner renders exactly `C12 is no longer available. It has been removed from your choices.`; the rendered banner state carries no error code, asserted by the rendered props containing no `code` field; it is announced exactly once through the live region (asserted by one aria-live insertion), offers no in-banner action, and is dismissible; the seat leaves the selection, its line leaves the price summary and the total drops by exactly that seat's price_paise; zero network requests are issued for the selection itself, asserted by a request spy reporting 0 calls beyond the map fetch; the banner renders in the page's own scroll context pinned to the top of the viewport and reserves its own height, asserted by a seat cell holding keyboard focus remaining fully within the viewport with the banner live; with two chosen seats gone in one re-check, one banner is shown and not two, asserted by a count of banner elements returning 1; P-ACC-13's return-from-sign-in string appears nowhere in this module, asserted by grep.
SourceRef: P-SEA-03 E2 SCR-SEA-03 E2 SCR-SEA-01 FR-ADR-046 J-XCT-08

Title: Acquire a multi-seat hold all-or-nothing, in ascending seat-id order
Description: One hold request names a set of seats and succeeds or fails as a whole; it never returns a partial success. Each seat's lock is one Redis key acquired with SET key token NX PX ttl in a single command - a process that dies between SETNX and EXPIRE leaves a seat unbuyable forever. One token per hold, not one per seat; a second request on the same showtime extends the existing hold under its existing token and its unchanged expires_at.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/showtimes/77/holds with seat_ids [418, 402, 410] from an authenticated customer issues exactly three Redis commands of the form `SET lock:seat:77:<id> <token> NX PX <ttl_ms>` in the order 402, 410, 418, each one single command - asserted against a Redis command log containing zero SETNX and zero EXPIRE on this path; on success it returns 201 with one hold_token of exactly 43 characters from the URL-safe base64 alphabet, one expires_at, every seat now under that token each with its own price_paise, and total_paise equal to their sum; when SET NX returns nil for 410 and a GET on that key returns a value that is not this customer's hold token, `lock:seat:77:402` is removed by the compare-and-delete Lua script, `lock:seat:77:418` was never written, the response is 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE with details.unavailable_seats ["C10"], and `redis EXISTS lock:seat:77:402` and `lock:seat:77:418` both return 0 - zero seats are held afterwards; when SET NX returns nil and the key's value IS this customer's existing hold token, the request does not roll back, that key is not added to the rollback set, its PTTL is not raised, and the response is 201; a second request naming new seats returns 201 carrying the SAME hold_token and the SAME expires_at as the first, with each new key's PTTL at most the milliseconds remaining to that instant and never a fresh 180000; the response body carries every seat under the token and not only the seats this request added; after step 7 finds a committed booking_seat row for a seat whose lock was won, the request takes the rollback path and returns 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE; the hold's token is added to `holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}` and each key to `instance:{instance_id}:holds`, both with the hold's TTL, asserted by SMEMBERS and TTL; `DEL cache:seatmap:77` is issued after the Redis lock writes and never before, asserted by command ordering in the log; no row is written to any PostgreSQL table by this endpoint, asserted by a SQL statement log containing zero INSERT and zero UPDATE.

Title: Validate every seat id server-side before any lock is touched
Description: The interface limit is a convenience; the hold endpoint is the enforcement point. Every seat_id must be an integer, must exist, must be a member of THIS SHOWTIME'S materialised seat set (P-ADM-14, lane E6 - not the screen's current seats, which are a different set), and must be active. Any failure rejects the whole request before any lock is touched.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the interface bypassed, POST /api/showtimes/77/holds returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and leaves `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` byte-identical to its pre-call value, for each of: seat_ids [402, 402] with message `Seat C12 was listed twice. Each seat can only be chosen once. No seats were held.`; a seat that exists on the screen but is absent from showtime_seat for showtime 77 with message `Seat C12 is not part of this hall. No seats were held.`; a seat whose is_active is false with message `Seat C12 is out of service. No seats were held.`; and seat_ids [] with message `Choose at least one seat.`; the membership test is against the materialised set and not the screen, asserted by a test that inserts a new seat into screen 3 AFTER showtime 77 was created and observes the hold refused with `Seat C12 is not part of this hall. No seats were held.` while the same seat is holdable on a showtime created after it; membership and active are independent checks, asserted by a seat that is in showtime_seat but has is_active false being refused by the active message and not the membership one; POST /api/showtimes/999999/holds returns 404 NOT_FOUND with `That showtime could not be found.`; the validation runs before the cap check and before any Redis command, asserted by the command log for each of the five cases being empty of any SET.
SourceRef: P-SEA-01 E2 S4 E2 EP-HLD-01 FR-ADR-016 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-02 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-03 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-04

Title: Hold seats for 180 seconds from configuration, with the expiry fixed at acquisition
Description: The hold lasts 180 seconds read from SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS. SRC-002 §8.1.1's 7 minutes is superseded by erratum E-1 and is dead text; any document, test, fixture or comment stating 7 minutes is a defect. The expiry instant is computed once and never moves - not by polling, not by re-selecting a held seat, not by adding a seat, and there is no endpoint that moves it.
AcceptanceCriteria: With SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=180 and the injected clock at 2026-08-14T14:02:37.412Z, a granted hold returns expires_at 2026-08-14T14:05:37.412Z in UTC with milliseconds and every one of its keys reports PTTL in the range (179000, 180000]; a grep of backend/, frontend/, scripts/ and tests/ finds zero occurrences of the string `7 minutes`, zero of `420` used as a hold duration and zero literal `180` used as a hold duration - the value is read from SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS at every site; re-sending the hold naming a seat this customer already holds returns 201 and leaves expires_at byte-identical and the key's PTTL not raised; adding a further seat with the injected clock at acquisition+60s returns the same expires_at and writes the new key with PTTL in (119000, 120000] rather than a fresh 180000; the generated OpenAPI document contains no operation that accepts or returns a new expiry for an existing hold, asserted by a search of its paths; boot exits non-zero when SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS is absent, non-integer or <= 0, and when PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS is greater than or equal to SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS * 1000; when the TTL elapses the keys are gone with no process of ours having run - asserted by grep finding no scheduler, no cron entry and no sweep task in the codebase.
SourceRef: P-HLD-02 E2 S4 FR-ADR-027 FR-ADR-025 SRC-003 OPEN-HOLD-01 SRC-002 §E E-1 SRC-002 §7.1 SRC-001 §5.2.5

Title: Decide expiry by asking Redis, never by comparing clocks
Description: The server never compares the current time against expires_at to decide whether a hold is alive; it asks Redis whether the key exists and whether its value is this hold's token. expires_at exists for one purpose - to be rendered as a countdown on the client. A malformed token is 400 REQUEST_INVALID before Redis is touched and never 409 HOLD_EXPIRED, because a token of the wrong shape names no hold that ever existed and telling the customer their hold ended would be a false statement.
AcceptanceCriteria: With a hold acquired at 2026-08-14T14:02:37.412Z and SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=180, so expires_at is 2026-08-14T14:05:37.412Z: with the injected clock at expires_at minus 1s a confirm returns 201; with the injected clock at exactly expires_at and at expires_at plus 1s the same request returns 409 with error.code HOLD_EXPIRED; no test in this story calls sleep or reads the wall clock, asserted by grep over the story's test files finding zero occurrences of time.sleep and zero of datetime.now without an injected clock; the liveness function takes no clock argument and performs no comparison against expires_at, asserted by its signature and by grep of its body; GET /api/holds/{token} with a well-formed 43-character token matching no key returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED with `The hold on your seats has ended and they have been released. You have not been charged. Choose them again if they are still free.`; with a key present whose value is a different token it returns 403 HOLD_NOT_OWNED with the same sentence; with a token of 42 characters, of 44 characters, or of 43 characters containing `+`, `/` or `=`, it returns 400 REQUEST_INVALID with `This request could not be processed. Return to the seat map and choose your seats again.` and the Redis command log for that request is empty; a client whose clock is one minute slow still succeeds while the key lives, and one whose clock is fast is still accepted - both asserted by the server's answer being independent of any client-supplied instant, and the endpoint rejecting any body or query carrying an expiry.
SourceRef: P-HLD-03 E2 S4 E2 EP-HLD-02 FR-ADR-018 FR-ADR-025 FR-ADR-027 FR-ADR-047 SRC-002 §8.1.4

Title: Cap a customer at ten seats held at once on one showtime
Description: A customer may hold at most MAX_SEATS_PER_BOOKING seats at any one moment on one showtime, counted from their live holds plus this request, checked before any lock is taken. The cap bounds CONCURRENT HOLDS and the size of one booking. It does NOT bound how many seats one customer may buy on that showtime over successive bookings - nothing does, that is OPEN-BULKBUY-01, open and reserved, and this story asserts the specified 201 rather than inventing a limit.
AcceptanceCriteria: MAX_SEATS_PER_BOOKING=10, interface bypassed. A first request naming 11 seats returns 422 SEAT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with `You can hold up to 10 seats for one showtime. You chose 11.` and `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` is unchanged; a customer already holding 6 seats on showtime 77 requesting 5 more returns 422 SEAT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with `You can hold up to 10 seats for one showtime. You are holding 6 and chose 5 more.`, and the six existing keys keep their PTTL and the hold keeps its expires_at byte-identical; the same customer requesting 4 more instead returns 201 and the hold then carries 10 seats; a customer holding 10 on showtime 77 requesting 4 on showtime 88 returns 201 - the cap is per showtime; a customer who has BOUGHT 10 seats on showtime 77 and immediately requests 10 more on showtime 77 returns 201, and the test suite contains no assertion that this is refused (asserted by grep for a lifetime-limit assertion returning nothing); the count is read from the set `holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}` and the Redis command log for the cap check contains zero SCAN and zero KEYS commands; with MAX_SEATS_PER_BOOKING set to 6 the note renders `Up to 6 seats.` and the seventh seat is refused, proving no literal 10 is shipped in any of the three strings.
SourceRef: P-HLD-04 E2 S4 FR-ADR-026 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-01

Title: Stop the guest at the hold, on the router, and not at the seat map or at payment
Description: A guest may browse, open a seat map, select seats and watch the total build. A guest cannot acquire a hold - the hold is the first authenticated action, which is the stricter option because an unauthenticated hold endpoint would let anyone lock a whole hall for three minutes with no account. Authorisation is applied once, on the router, as a dependency. Whether a MANAGER may buy a ticket is unruled (OPEN-MGRBOOK-01, open and reserved), so this story adds no prohibition and asserts the specified acceptance.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /api/showtimes/77/holds with no Authorization header returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED with `Sign in to hold seats. Your selection has been kept.`, and returns the same with an expired JWT; in both cases `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` is unchanged; GET /api/showtimes/77/seats returns 200 for the same unauthenticated caller, so the guest is stopped at the hold and not at the map; the check lives on the router and not in the handler, asserted by replacing the hold handler body with a bare return and observing the 401 still produced; a hold request from a manager account and from an admin account each return 201, exactly as for a customer; with a guest selection present the primary action reads `Sign in to hold these seats` and pressing it writes the selection and opens the authentication step without issuing any request to the hold endpoint (request spy reports 0 calls); on return from authentication the primary action reads `Hold these seats`, the selection has been restored and re-checked against a freshly fetched map, and NO hold has been taken automatically - asserted by `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` returning empty until the action is pressed.
SourceRef: P-HLD-05 E2 S4 FR-ADR-014 FR-ADR-046 FR-ADR-009 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-02 SRC-003 OPEN-ROLE-01 SRC-001 §4.1 SRC-001 §7.4

Title: Check the sales cut-off at the hold and never at confirmation
Description: Sales close at starts_at + SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES, derived at evaluation time and never stored on the showtime row. PROVISIONAL: SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES = +15 means fifteen minutes AFTER the advertised start (SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-03, FR-ADR-042). The alternative reading is fifteen minutes BEFORE and the two are half an hour apart; one message from the client reverses it, and reversing it changes one configured value, its sign, and three assertions in this story.
AcceptanceCriteria: SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=+15, showtime 77 starting 2026-08-14T19:30:00+05:30, the cinema row carrying the IANA zone Asia/Kolkata. A hold request with the injected clock at 2026-08-14T19:44:59+05:30 returns 201; at 19:45:00+05:30 and at 19:45:01+05:30 it returns 409 SALES_CLOSED with `Sales for this showtime closed at 7:45 pm. Choose another showtime.` and `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` is unchanged - the comparison is now >= sales_close_at; a hold acquired at 19:44:59 is still confirmable at 19:47:00, and the confirm code path contains no cut-off evaluation at all, asserted by grep for SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES and sales_close_at over the confirm module returning nothing; sales_close_at appears in no column of the showtime table, asserted against schema.sql; the comparison is evaluated in the cinema's zone read from the cinema row and never in the container's local time, asserted by a test running with TZ=UTC and still refusing at 19:45:00+05:30; GET /api/showtimes/77/seats after the cut-off returns 200 with every seat unselectable and a closed flag, and the banner reads `Sales for this showtime have closed.`, or `Sales for this showtime have closed. You can still pay for the seats you are holding.` for a customer holding seats; setting SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES=-15 with no code change moves the three assertions to 19:14:59 accepted and 19:15:00 and 19:15:01 refused; boot exits non-zero when SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES is absent or non-integer, and accepts a negative value.
SourceRef: P-HLD-06 E2 S4 FR-ADR-042 FR-ADR-018 FR-ADR-045 SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-03 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01 SRC-001 §10.12

Title: Name the seats that went, immediately, and never blame the customer
Description: When one or more seats a customer wanted has gone, the response is 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE and details.unavailable_seats carries the seat LABELS the customer reads, never internal ids. The interface names them, marks them unavailable on the map immediately, and leaves the rest of the selection exactly as it was. A first hold is all-or-nothing so nothing is held afterwards and the message says so; a request that EXTENDS a live hold is the one path on which seats genuinely are still held, and it is told so.
AcceptanceCriteria: A first hold for five seats losing C12 and C13 returns 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE with details.unavailable_seats ["C12","C13"] - customer-facing labels, asserted by the values matching seat.row_label plus seat_number and not seat.id - and message `C12 and C13 were taken by another customer. No seats were held. Your other choices are still selected — change these two and press Hold these seats again.`; losing exactly one returns details.unavailable_seats ["C12"] and `C12 was taken by another customer. No seats were held. Choose a different seat and press Hold these seats again.`; the same two failures on a request that EXTENDS a live hold return `C12 and C13 were taken by another customer. Your hold is unchanged. Your other choices are still selected — change these two and try again.` and `C12 was taken by another customer. Your hold is unchanged. Choose a different seat and try again.`, and in both cases the existing hold's expires_at is byte-identical and every one of its keys' PTTL is unchanged; a seat found already sold by the post-acquisition booking_seat check produces the same one-seat sentence; the client marks each named seat held_by_other and never sold, asserted by the rendered cell treatment; every other chosen seat remains in fr.selection after the failure, asserted by reading the key; details.unavailable_seats is a non-empty array on every SEAT_UNAVAILABLE response, asserted across all four cases; the interface branches on error.code, asserted by replacing message with arbitrary text and observing the same banner state; no message on this path contains an apology, an exclamation mark, or the word `sorry`, asserted by grep over the published strings.
SourceRef: P-HLD-07 E2 S4 FR-ADR-026 FR-ADR-052 FR-ADR-029 SRC-001 §5.2.6

Title: Let a customer give seats back - one at a time, all at once, and after the hold has already gone
Description: Tapping a held seat gives that seat back; the secondary control gives the whole hold back. Both are the compare-and-delete Lua script against the hold's token, so a client can only release a lock it owns. The rest of the hold survives with the same expires_at. The whole-hold path is its own seven-step procedure and is NOT the per-seat one in a loop. A release racing a confirm is settled by ordering, with no in-flight flag and no error code of its own.
AcceptanceCriteria: DELETE /api/holds/{token}/seats/402 on a live three-Recliner-seat hold at 33333 paise each returns 200 carrying two seats, total_paise 66666, and expires_at byte-identical to before; `redis EXISTS lock:seat:77:402` returns 0 and the other two keys' PTTL are unchanged; the delete is the compare-and-delete script, asserted by issuing the same call with a different hold's token and observing the key still present and the response 403 HOLD_NOT_OWNED; releasing the LAST seat returns an empty seats array, deletes the hold record and removes the token from `holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}` (asserted by SCARD returning 0), after which the same customer immediately taking ten seats on that showtime returns 201; DELETE /api/holds/{token} returns 204 with no body, compare-and-deletes every key in ascending seat_id order, removes them from `instance:{instance_id}:holds`, deletes the hold record, removes the token from the cap index, and issues `DEL cache:seatmap:77` AFTER the releases - asserted by the Redis command log ordering, with zero DEL of the cache key appearing before the first release; a compare-and-delete returning 0 for one seat because that key had already expired does not stop the loop, the remaining seats are still released and the response is still 204; DELETE of a seat that is not in the hold returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with `That seat is not part of your hold.`; DELETE of an already-expired hold returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED and issues NO `DEL cache:seatmap:77` at all, asserted by that key being absent from the command log for the request; a release landing before a confirm's Redis re-validation makes that confirm return 409 HOLD_EXPIRED with zero payment attempts recorded and nothing charged; a release landing after the booking committed deletes nothing and the booking stands, asserted by `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=77 AND seat_id=402` returning 1; no error code refusing a release while a confirm is in flight exists in the error registry, asserted by grep.
SourceRef: P-HLD-08 E2 S4 E2 EP-HLD-03 E2 EP-HLD-04 FR-ADR-025 FR-ADR-026 FR-ADR-029 FR-ADR-045 SRC-002 §8.1.3 SRC-001 §5.2.2

Title: Count down from a server-issued instant, warn once at sixty seconds, and claim nothing at zero
Description: The hold response carries an absolute expires_at in UTC, not a duration and not a remaining-seconds count. The client renders m:ss by subtracting from its own clock and the server never trusts that arithmetic, so a wrong client clock produces a wrong display and never a wrong outcome. At zero the client stops, disables the payment action and states the hold has ended - it does not delete anything, release anything, or claim the seats are free, and it names no cause because a TTL, a shutdown drain and a re-acquired key are indistinguishable from inside the browser.
AcceptanceCriteria: The hold response carries expires_at as an ISO-8601 UTC instant with milliseconds and carries no duration field and no remaining-seconds field, asserted against the response schema; the countdown component takes the current instant as a parameter and never reads a clock itself, asserted by its props and by grep for Date.now inside the module returning nothing - rendering it with now = expires_at minus 75s shows `1:15`, and with now = expires_at minus 60s shows `1:00` with the warning line `Less than a minute left. At 0:00 your seats are released and you will need to choose them again.` present, the bar and digits switching to --fr-countdown-urgent, and exactly one live-region announcement fired; at now >= expires_at it renders `0:00` and never a negative value, disables the payment action and shows `Your hold has ended and your seats have been released. You have not been charged.`; with a confirm already in flight the same instant instead shows `Your hold has ended. We are waiting for the answer to your payment. Do not close this page.` and the in-flight request is not cancelled, asserted by the request spy showing no abort; the seat cells are NOT pre-emptively repainted at 0:00, asserted by each held cell keeping its held_by_me treatment until the next poll payload arrives; the digits are not inside a live region, asserted against the rendered DOM; the label reads `TIME LEFT`; the hold token and the Idempotency-Key are in sessionStorage and not localStorage, asserted by localStorage.length being 0; after a reload, GET /api/holds/{token} returns the same expires_at and the countdown resumes at the correct remaining time; closing the tab issues zero requests, asserted by a spy on unload and beforeunload reporting 0 calls and by `redis EXISTS` on the hold's keys still returning 1.
SourceRef: P-HLD-09 E2 S4 E2 SCR-SEA-02 E2 EP-HLD-02 FR-ADR-047 FR-ADR-027 FR-ADR-051 SRC-001 §5.2.5 SRC-001 §5.2.6

Title: Fail the hold, the hold read and the release loudly when Redis is unreachable
Description: If Redis is unreachable the hold endpoint returns 503 and never falls back to the database for locks, never proceeds without a lock and never degrades quietly. Confirmation also returns 503, because confirming without a live hold would rely on the database constraint alone - safe against overselling but wrong for the customer, who would discover at payment that they were confirming seats someone else was holding. A test that mocks a connection error proves the handler; only stopping the container proves the client's timeout configuration.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the Redis container actually stopped - not a mocked connection error: POST /api/showtimes/77/holds returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with `Seat holds are unavailable right now. You can still look at showtimes and seat maps. Try again in a few minutes.` and returns within the configured command timeout rather than hanging, asserted by the response arriving in under 2x that timeout; DELETE /api/holds/{token} and DELETE /api/holds/{token}/seats/{seat_id} return the same status, code and sentence; GET /api/holds/{token} returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE; the confirm endpoint returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with `We cannot complete your booking right now. You have not been charged. Try again in a few minutes. If you need help, quote a1b2c3d4.` and the simulated provider records zero capture attempts; no code path substitutes PostgreSQL for a lock, asserted by the SQL statement log during the outage containing zero SELECT ... FOR UPDATE against seat or showtime for a hold request, and by grep finding no lock acquisition query outside the Redis module; GET /health/ready returns 503 while GET /health/live returns 200 during the same outage; the Redis client is constructed with explicit connect and command timeouts, asserted by reading the client's configuration object in a test and finding both set to a finite value; the failure handler issues no Redis command, asserted by the command log for the failing request being empty; when Redis returns, the next hold request returns 201 and the holds taken before the outage are gone, asserted by `redis KEYS lock:seat:77:*` returning empty.
SourceRef: P-HLD-10 E2 S4 FR-ADR-028 FR-ADR-025 FR-ADR-058 FR-ADR-052 SRC-002 §7.9 SRC-002 §7.4 SRC-002 §5.2.3

Title: Snapshot each seat's price at hold acquisition and never recompute it
Description: At acquisition the API computes the per-seat prices and stores them with the hold in Redis under the hold token; at confirmation those stored prices are used, not recomputed. The price a customer pays is the price that was current when their hold was granted, and the protection window is bounded by the hold itself so it needs no separate expiry. Extending a hold reprices nothing, so one hold may legitimately carry seats priced from two different base prices - that is this rule working, not a defect.
AcceptanceCriteria: Each seat's price is computed once as seat_price_paise = (base_price_paise * (10000 + uplift_basis_points) + 5000) // 10000 in integer arithmetic, asserted by grep of the pricing module finding no float literal, no `/` division and no Decimal inside that expression; with base_price_paise 25000 and Recliner uplift 3333, two seats held at 19:32:37 store 33333 paise each under the hold token in Redis with the hold's TTL, asserted by reading the stored value and its TTL; an admin raising the showtime's base_price_paise to 30000 at 19:33:10 leaves those two stored prices at 33333 and the hold's total_paise at 66666, and the customer's total does not move; a third Recliner seat added to the same hold at 19:33:45 stores 39999, giving three seats, total_paise 106665 and expires_at still 19:35:37; confirming at 19:34:20 charges exactly 106665 paise and writes base_price_paise_applied 25000 for the first two booking_seat rows and 30000 for the third; the confirm path reads the stored prices and calls the pricing function zero times, asserted by a spy on that function; the next customer to take a hold after the change pays 39999 per Recliner seat; if Redis is unreachable at confirm so the stored prices cannot be read, the response is 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and nothing is charged; every money value on this path is a Python int and every money column is bigint, asserted against schema.sql, and a caller that skips the rounding function and passes a non-integer raises a type error rather than persisting.
SourceRef: P-HLD-11 E2 S4 FR-ADR-035 FR-ADR-038 FR-ADR-039 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 SRC-001 §5.2.4 SRC-001 §7.6

Title: Release this instance's holds on SIGTERM, and never depend on it
