Description: Each API instance registers the keys of every hold it grants in a Redis set with the hold's TTL, and on SIGTERM it drains and runs the compare-and-delete release over that set. The registry lives in Redis and not in process memory because containers are stateless and a SIGKILLed process loses in-memory state before it can act on it. Expiry is the guarantee; this release is an optimisation on top of it, and correctness never depends on it running.
AcceptanceCriteria: A hold granted by instance i-1 adds each of its keys to `instance:i-1:holds` with the hold's TTL, asserted by SMEMBERS listing them and TTL matching the keys' PTTL to within one second; sending a real SIGTERM to that running container causes it, in order: to stop accepting new connections, to let in-flight requests finish, then to compare-and-delete every key in `instance:i-1:holds`, delete each affected hold record, remove each token from `holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}` and issue `DEL cache:seatmap:{showtime_id}` once per showtime touched, then exit with code 0 - after which `redis EXISTS lock:seat:77:402` returns 0, SCARD on the cap index returns 0, and the same customer immediately re-requesting that seat receives 201; a key in the registry whose current value is another hold's token is left present, asserted by GET returning that other token unchanged; SIGKILLing the container instead leaves the keys present and they are gone by expires_at with no process of ours having run, asserted by grep finding no scheduler, no cron entry and no sweep task in the codebase; a confirm in flight when SIGTERM arrives completes and its booking_seat rows are committed, asserted by `SELECT count(*)` returning 1 for that pair after the exit; the release step is best-effort - a test that makes the compare-and-delete fail for one key still sees the process exit 0 and the remaining keys released.

Title: Prove exactly one winner among fifty simultaneous hold requests
Description: The never-waivable concurrency gate. This is Stage A of the proof and it fires at the HOLD endpoint, where the Redis lock decides the winner. The constraint-drop red proof is Stage B, it belongs to P-XCT-01 in lane XCT, and it may not be run against this criterion: with the constraint dropped this same run still produces exactly one winner because every loser was refused by SET NX and the constraint was never reached, so reading that as a red proof proves nothing and reading it as a failure blocks a story for a defect that is not there.
AcceptanceCriteria: `scripts/stress_seats.py --showtime 77 --seat 402 --n 50 --base-url <url>` run with fifty distinct seeded authenticated customers reports exactly 1 response of HTTP 201 and exactly 49 responses of HTTP 409 whose error.code is SEAT_UNAVAILABLE and whose error.details.unavailable_seats is ["C2"]; the script records each request's start instant and exits non-zero with `not concurrent` when the spread between first and last exceeds the configured threshold, default 100 ms - a run whose spread is inside the threshold is required for a pass; after the winner confirms, `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id = 77 AND seat_id = 402` returns exactly 1; zero winners fails, and any loser returning 500 rather than 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE fails; the rate limiter runs normally throughout and the script exposes no flag that disables it, asserted by grep of the script for any limiter bypass returning nothing; the same script run against the deployed environment by changing only --base-url produces the same three figures; this story asserts nothing about a dropped unique constraint and its test file contains no DROP CONSTRAINT - the red proof is P-XCT-01 Stage B; the unique constraint on (showtime_id, seat_id) is total with no WHERE clause and is created in the Phase 2 migration, asserted by reading pg_constraint and by the migration's ordinal.

Title: Publish this lane's message set, with a stable code and one substitution rule
Description: Every failure on this lane's endpoints returns one envelope; the interface branches on code and never on message text. Two rules govern the whole set: singular at exactly one offending seat and plural at two or more, counted over offending seats and not over the request; and a closing clause with two forms - `No seats were held.` on a first hold, `Your hold is unchanged.` on a request that extends a live hold, because on an extend the first sentence would be contradicted by the countdown, the held cells, the heading and the cap, all on the same screen.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every failure response on the four hold endpoints is `{"error":{"code":...,"message":...,"details":...,"request_id":...}}` with request_id present including on 500s; a table-driven test asserts the exact HTTP status, error.code and verbatim message for all 24 rows of the lane's message set, including `Seat C12 was listed twice. Each seat can only be chosen once. No seats were held.` at one offending seat and `Seats C12 and C13 were listed more than once. Each seat can only be chosen once. No seats were held.` at two; the singular renders at exactly one offending seat and the plural at two or more, counted over offending seats - asserted by a five-seat request carrying one duplicate rendering the singular; every offending seat is named, in submission order, joined `C12, C13 and C14` with no serial comma, never truncated and never summarised as a count; the closing clause substitution applies to exactly eight rows - the two SEAT_UNAVAILABLE-at-hold pairs and the six seat-level VALIDATION_FAILED strings - and to no other row, asserted by a test that runs each of the 24 rows once as a first hold and once as an extend and finds exactly eight sentences differing; the extend forms end `try again` and name no button label, asserted by grep for `press Hold these seats again` in the extend branch returning nothing; request_id is rendered to the customer on 5xx only, asserted by a 422 body containing no `quote` and a 500 body containing `If you need help, quote `; a 429 carries Retry-After 3 with `Too many attempts. Try again in 3 seconds.` when the per-user bucket refused and Retry-After 1 with `Too many attempts. Try again in 1 second.` when the per-IP bucket refused, the header value and the number in the sentence being the same value; no message contains a stack trace, SQL text, an exception class name, a hostname or a database table name, asserted by a regex sweep over every published string; each of the codes on this lane has a negative test asserting both its status and its code.

Title: Implement the seat lifecycle exactly as the normative state machine
Description: One seat, for one showtime, as seen by one customer session, is in exactly one of five states at every instant, and every one of twenty-nine inputs has a defined result in every state. The machine is normative: a behaviour not in the table is a defect, and an input handled differently from the table is a defect. held_by_me_paying is a lifecycle state and not a fifth rendered map state - it renders identically to held_by_me.
AcceptanceCriteria: The machine-readable transition block is committed as a data file and a test enumerates it: 5 states times 29 inputs equals exactly 145 transitions, none blank, asserted by a count and by an assertion that no cell is null; for every one of the 145 pairs the implemented result state equals the table's result state; the reachability assertions hold - held_by_me from available by HOLD_ACQUIRE_OK, held_by_me_paying from held_by_me by CONFIRM_START, sold from held_by_me_paying by CONFIRM_COMMIT, held_by_other from available by OTHER_ACQUIRES; SIGN_OUT from held_by_me yields available, releases the keys and clears every `fr.` prefixed value from sessionStorage, asserted by sessionStorage holding zero keys with that prefix; TAB_CLOSED from held_by_me yields held_by_me and issues zero requests, asserted by a spy on unload; SALES_CUTOFF_PASSES is a self-loop in all five states and changes no seat's state, asserted by comparing the seat's state before and after; CONFIRM_PAYMENT_FAILED_HOLD_LIVE from held_by_me_paying yields held_by_me and CONFIRM_PAYMENT_FAILED_HOLD_GONE yields available; INSTANCE_KILLED_PRECOMMIT from held_by_me_paying yields held_by_me and INSTANCE_KILLED_POSTCOMMIT yields sold; held_by_me_paying and held_by_me produce the identical rendered cell, asserted by a DOM comparison, so the map still carries exactly four rendered states over three wire values; each transition the table marks impossible carries a test that attempts it and observes the alternative the guard names - for example a confirm against a seat in available takes CONFIRM_HOLD_GONE and returns 409 HOLD_EXPIRED before any payment; no input named SHOWTIME_WITHDRAWN exists in the machine, asserted by grep, because no withdraw capability exists in v1 (OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01 is open and reserved).

Title: Let sold win over any lock when the seat map is assembled
Description: A seat's map state is computed from two sources - a booking_seat row in PostgreSQL and a lock key in Redis - and sold always wins. Locks are released after commit, not before, so there is always a window in which both exist; if the container dies inside it the lock survives against a seat that is already sold. Without an explicit precedence rule two correct sources produce two different answers for the same seat.
AcceptanceCriteria: With a committed booking_seat row for (77, 402) AND a live key `lock:seat:77:402`, GET /api/showtimes/77/seats reports seat 402 with state `sold` and never `held`; with only the lock present it reports `held`; with neither it reports `available`; with only the booking row it reports `sold`; the set of distinct state values across every seat in the payload is a subset of {available, sold, held}, asserted by a set comparison - neither held_by_me nor held_by_other can be emitted by the server; a residual lock on a sold seat produces no message and the cell is drawn sold with its hatch mark; with Redis unreachable the endpoint returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and the customer sees `The seat map is unavailable right now. You can still browse showtimes. Try again in a few minutes.` - the map is not served without hold state, because the rate limiter reads Redis and fails closed before the cache is consulted; the precedence is implemented once, asserted by grep finding a single site that resolves the two sources.
SourceRef: P-SEA-05 E2 S4 FR-ADR-024 FR-ADR-029 FR-ADR-045 FR-ADR-058 SRC-002 §8.1.5

Title: Receipt and entry
Description: Everything between the money being taken and the customer standing at the entrance: the booking reference, the confirmation page, the transactional outbox, the SQS worker, the SES send, the resend control and the manual door check. The emailed receipt carrying a unique booking reference is the customer's only proof of purchase and their only way into the hall, and there is no QR code, no scanner and no validation endpoint.
SourceRef: E4 S4 SRC-003 OPEN-EMAIL-01 SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-01 SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-02

Title: Generate a unique booking reference inside the confirm transaction
Description: Every confirmed booking is given one 8-character reference drawn from a 30-character alphabet by a cryptographically secure source, stored uppercase under a UNIQUE constraint, generated inside the booking transaction with no endpoint that mints one. OPEN-REFCHAR-01 is open and untouched here: the alphabet keeps the confusable pairs 2/Z, 5/S, 8/B and 6/G and carries no check character, and the row stops being answerable at the first confirmed booking because a reference already issued cannot be re-cut.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the draw stubbed to known values, a confirmed booking gives `SELECT length(reference), reference = upper(reference) FROM booking WHERE id=:b` returning `8, true`; over 1000 generated references `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE reference !~ '^[23456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ]{8}$'` returns 0, so none contains 0, 1, I, L, O or U and none carries the FR prefix or a hyphen; a second INSERT of an existing reference raises a unique-constraint violation, which is the guard rather than the collision arithmetic; with the draw stubbed to return an already-stored value 4 times then a free one, the confirm returns 201 and `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE reference=:free` returns 1; with the draw stubbed to collide 5 times the confirm returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR, `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE user_id=:u` returns 0 and `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=:s` returns 0; the generator module imports `secrets` and contains no occurrence of `random.`
SourceRef: P-TKT-01 FR-ADR-015 SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-01 E4 S4

Title: Normalise a typed reference and correct nothing
Description: A reference supplied as input is uppercased and stripped of whitespace, hyphens and an optional leading FR, then matched by equality. Nothing is mapped, aliased or guessed, because a system that guesses can admit the wrong person, and the three ways a lookup can fail are made indistinguishable so the endpoint is not an enumeration oracle.
AcceptanceCriteria: For a booking whose stored reference is `ABCDEFGH`, `GET /api/bookings/by-reference/{r}` as its owner returns 200 for each of `FR-ABCD-EFGH`, `fr abcd efgh`, `abcdefgh` and `  FR-abcd-EFGH  `; it returns 404 NOT_FOUND for `FR-0BCD-EFGH` (a zero typed for O), `FR-1BCD-EFGH` (a one typed for I) and `FR-ABCD-EFG` (7 characters), and the zero is not mapped to O; a 65-character path value returns 404 with a database query counter of 0 for the request; the match is an equality predicate, asserted by the statement log for the request containing no LIKE, no ILIKE and no similarity( call, and by the uppercase being ASCII-only; the raw response body and status of a malformed reference, an unknown well-formed reference and another customer's well-formed reference are compared pairwise and are byte-identical.
SourceRef: P-TKT-02 FR-ADR-015 EP-TKT-01 E4 S4

Title: Read one booking by its reference, on ownership alone
Description: EP-TKT-01 returns the facts a customer needs at a door for a booking whose user_id equals their own. The role is never consulted, so an admin reads their own bookings and nobody else's, and the receipt's dispatch state is deliberately not in the response because rendering a failed state is OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01, which is open and reserved.
AcceptanceCriteria: `GET /api/bookings/by-reference/FR-ABCD-EFGH` as the owner returns 200 whose body keys are exactly `reference, film_title, hall_name, starts_at, seats, total_paise, paid_at, receipt_email_address`; with the stored showtime instant `2026-08-21T13:45:00Z` and the cinema row's offset at +05:30, `starts_at` is `2026-08-21T19:15:00+05:30` as one field, and no second local-time field exists; `seats` is `[F7, F8, F9]` for seat rows inserted in the order F9, F7, F8; `total_paise` is `84372` read from the stored column, asserted by mutating the seeded base price after the booking and re-reading the same value; the identical request made by a signed-in admin who does not own the booking returns 404 with a body byte-identical to the unknown-reference 404; the body contains none of the keys `status`, `cancelled_at`, `receipt_status`, `dispatch_seq`; the ownership rule is a router dependency, asserted by the handler function containing no user_id comparison.
SourceRef: P-TKT-09 P-TKT-02 EP-TKT-01 FR-ADR-013 FR-ADR-018 E4 S6

Title: Show the reference on the confirmation page, independently of the email
Description: SCR-TKT-01 renders the reference and the booking facts the moment a booking is confirmed and on every later visit; it never states that an email has been sent, because at that moment it has not been. The receipt sentence is shown only when the confirm response is present in the client's navigation state, so a reload renders the later-visit state, and no replacement sentence is written for it because OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01 reserves what a customer is told about a receipt that may already have failed.
AcceptanceCriteria: Rendering `/bookings/FR-ABCD-EFGH` with the confirm response present in navigation state shows the h1 `Your booking is confirmed.`, the label `BOOKING REFERENCE`, the reference `FR-ABCD-EFGH`, the fact labels `FILM HALL SHOWTIME SEATS PAID`, the entry line `Show this reference at the entrance. A person will check it.`, the policy line `This booking cannot be changed, cancelled or refunded.` and exactly one occurrence of `A receipt is on its way to name@example.com.`; rendering the same route with no navigation state shows the same h1, reference block, facts, entry line and policy line and zero occurrences of each of `on its way`, `has been sent`, `was sent` and `delayed`; the loading state renders the reference element empty rather than containing any 8-character placeholder; the reference element's accessible name is `F R, A B C D, E F G H`; focus is on the h1 after arrival and the focus order is heading, reference, copy control, facts, resend control; the copy control writes `FR-ABCD-EFGH` to the clipboard and announces `Reference copied.` in a live region.
SourceRef: P-TKT-03 FR-ADR-048 SCR-TKT-01 E4 S5

Title: Commit the receipt_dispatch and outbox rows with the booking
Description: The receipt job exists only if the booking does: one receipt_dispatch row and one outbox_message row are inserted inside the booking transaction, immediately before commit, so there is no post-commit send with no record. No customer data travels in the payload, and the topic vocabulary has exactly two members because the account lane's password-reset email uses the same table, relay and worker.
AcceptanceCriteria: After one confirmed booking, `SELECT status, dispatch_seq, attempts, claimed_at, sent_at, ses_message_id, last_error FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` returns exactly one row reading `pending, 1, 0, null, null, null, null`, and `SELECT topic, status, attempts FROM outbox_message WHERE payload->>'booking_id'=:b` returns exactly one row reading `receipt.send, pending, 0`; the sorted payload key set equals `booking_id, dispatch_seq, message_version, request_id` and the payload text contains no @ character, no seat label and no amount; an insert with `topic='receipt.render'` raises rather than committing, and a `receipt.send` payload with a fifth key or with message_version missing raises; a `password_reset.send` payload whose key set is exactly `message_version, request_id, reset_token_id, user_id` is accepted; forcing the outbox insert to fail leaves `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE reference=:r` at 0 and `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=:s` at 0; `receipt_dispatch` carries a UNIQUE constraint on booking_id, proved by a second insert for the same booking raising.
SourceRef: P-TKT-04 FR-ADR-031 FR-ADR-032 FR-ADR-059 E4 S4

Title: Bound the fast-path queue send and relay what it leaves behind
Description: The queue send runs inside the confirm request after the commit and the response is emitted after it returns, so it is bounded by QUEUE_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS (2000, ASSUMED, no source states a figure) with SDK-level retry disabled so the bound is the value and not a multiple of it. Anything it leaves pending is relayed on the worker's existing receive loop; there is no scheduler and none may be added.
AcceptanceCriteria: With `QUEUE_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS=2000` and the queue client stubbed to block against an injected clock, the confirm returns 201 no later than commit plus 2000 ms, the stub records exactly 1 SendMessage attempt, `SELECT status FROM outbox_message WHERE id=:o` reads `pending`, one ERROR line carrying the request_id is emitted and the response body carries no mention of the queue; with the queue reachable the same confirm leaves that row `sent` with sent_at non-null while `SELECT status FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` still reads `pending`; with `OUTBOX_RELAY_MIN_AGE_SECONDS=30` a worker poll at commit plus 29 s selects zero rows and a poll at commit plus 31 s selects the row with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED in a bounded batch, sends it and marks it `sent`; `QUEUE_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS` is at most one tenth of SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (20 s), asserted at boot in the configuration check; the repository contains no scheduler entry point, asserted by a search of backend/ for APScheduler, celery beat and cron returning no registration.
SourceRef: P-TKT-04 FR-ADR-031 FR-ADR-059 SRC-003 OPEN-PROC-01

Title: Claim the send before calling SES so one booking has one sender
Description: The worker branches on topic first, then claims the receipt send with a conditional UPDATE on the row the booking transaction already created; it transitions that row and never inserts one. Zero rows means another delivery owns the send, it is already sent, or the message carries a stale dispatch_seq. The claim makes two senders impossible; it does not make two sends impossible, which S-TKT-08 states.
AcceptanceCriteria: Delivering the same receipt.send message twice produces exactly 1 SES SendEmail call, asserted by the mail-port stub's call count, and `SELECT status, attempts FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` reads `sent, 1`; with `RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS=900` and an injected clock, a delivery against a `sending` row whose claimed_at is 120 s old makes 0 SES calls, deletes the message, leaves attempts unchanged and logs one INFO line, while the same delivery at 960 s reclaims the row, increments attempts by 1 and makes 1 SES call; deliveries against `sent`, against `suppressed`, and against a row at dispatch_seq 2 when the message carries 1 each make 0 SES calls and delete the message, and the suppressed case logs one WARNING naming the booking_id; a message whose topic is `receipt.print` makes 0 SES calls and is NOT deleted, asserted by the queue stub still holding it; a receipt.send message whose booking_id resolves to no confirmed booking is deleted and logged, and the same deletion rule is not applied to password_reset.send; the worker module contains no INSERT against receipt_dispatch; row 9 of docs/30 Deployment/AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md states both orderings the deployment owes - visibility timeout below RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS, and maxReceiveCount above ceil(stale / visibility), which is 8 at the worked pair of 900 and 120.
SourceRef: P-TKT-05 FR-ADR-032 FR-ADR-056 FR-ADR-059 E4 S4

Title: Bound the SES call, and treat a timed-out send as failed and retryable
Description: SES_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS (5000, ASSUMED, replaced by the phase 7 load test) stops a hung call holding the claim in sending for the full 900-second stale threshold. A timed-out send is recorded failed and is retried, so a send that in fact succeeded can deliver a second identical receipt: that is a stated limit on FR-ADR-032's guarantee, chosen deliberately because the alternative leaves a paying customer with nothing.
AcceptanceCriteria: With `SES_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS=5000` and the mail-port stub blocking against an injected clock, the worker abandons the call at exactly T plus 5000 ms and `SELECT status, sent_at, ses_message_id, last_error FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` reads `failed, null, null` with last_error containing `timeout` and not containing the SES refusal string; the queue message is not deleted, asserted by the stub still holding it; redelivering that message claims the failed row and produces a SECOND SES call, and the test asserts that second call is made rather than asserting it is prevented, so no test in this lane claims a duplicate receipt is impossible; an SES error response produces the same failed row with last_error carrying the SES error string, distinguishable from the timeout case by that string; the worker module contains no literal 5000 and reads the value from configuration; the process refuses to start when MAIL_PROVIDER or SES_SENDER_ADDRESS is unset, asserted by a non-zero exit and no port bound.
SourceRef: P-TKT-05 FR-ADR-032 FR-ADR-060 FR-ADR-053 E4 S4

Title: Render the receipt with everything needed at a door and nothing else
Description: SCR-TKT-02 carries the reference, seats, hall, showtime, film and amount in a plain-text part and a matching minimal HTML part, addressed to the account's own email address and never to an address taken from a request. No QR code, no barcode, no image, no attachment, no card data and no token that signs anybody in.
AcceptanceCriteria: For booking FR-ABCD-EFGH, three Premium seats inserted in the order F9, F7, F8 in Hall 3, showtime stored `2026-08-21T13:45:00Z`, total `84372` paise, the plain-text part equals these lines in this order: `Your booking is confirmed.`; `Booking reference: FR-ABCD-EFGH`; `Film      DEMO MOVIE 01`; `Hall      Hall 3`; `Showtime  21 Aug 2026, 7:15 pm (Asia/Kolkata)`; `Seats     F7, F8, F9`; `Paid      Rs 843.72`; `Show this reference at the entrance. A person will check it.`; the booking URL built from PUBLIC_BASE_URL on its own line; `This booking is final. There is no cancellation and no refund.`; the subject equals `Your FrontRow booking FR-ABCD-EFGH`; the HTML part renders the amount as `₹843.72` with the rupee symbol while the plain-text part uses `Rs`, carries the anchor text `See this booking again`, contains zero occurrences of `<img`, zero external URLs other than the single booking link, and no layout table; the message has 0 attachments and no part whose content type begins `image/`; a resend renders a body byte-identical to the first send; every rendered field is read from PostgreSQL in the send and none is read from the queue payload, asserted by the payload carrying only the four keys.
SourceRef: P-TKT-06 FR-ADR-036 FR-ADR-018 FR-ADR-040 FR-ADR-014 SCR-TKT-02

Title: Re-send a receipt on the owner's request, and refuse without cost when there is nothing to send
Description: The booking's owner, and nobody else with no role exempt, can re-enqueue their receipt: the request raises dispatch_seq and inserts one outbox row in one transaction, or refuses. It is a convenience for a customer who deleted the email and is not the answer to SES failing, because a customer who never received anything may not know to look.
AcceptanceCriteria: `POST /api/bookings/by-reference/FR-ABCD-EFGH/resend-receipt` as the owner against a `sent` row returns 202 with body keys exactly `queued, email_address`, `queued` true and `email_address` equal to the account address, and `SELECT dispatch_seq, status FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b` moves from `1, sent` to `2, pending` with exactly one new outbox_message carrying dispatch_seq 2; against a `pending` row with attempts 0 it returns 202 with `queued` false, inserts no outbox row, leaves dispatch_seq at 1 and spends no rate-limit token, proved by an immediately following resend being accepted once the row reaches `sent`; against `sending`, and against `pending` with attempts above 0, it returns 202 `queued` false and inserts nothing; against a `suppressed` row it returns 409 RECEIPT_SUPPRESSED on the first call and on the hundredth, changes no column and spends no token; as a signed-in non-owner, including an admin, it returns 404 with a body byte-identical to the unknown-reference 404; `SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log` is unchanged on every branch; a queued message still carrying dispatch_seq 1 after the row reached 2 produces 0 SES calls.
SourceRef: P-TKT-07 EP-TKT-02 FR-ADR-048 FR-ADR-032 FR-ADR-067

Title: Rate limit the reference lookup and the resend, failing closed
Description: Three limiters guard this lane: a per-user and a per-IP lookup bucket shared by both endpoints, and a per-booking resend interval of RECEIPT_RESEND_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (300, ASSUMED). Retry-After carries whichever one refused and is derived, never typed. It sits in phase 7 because phase 7 delivers rate limiting.
AcceptanceCriteria: With `RATE_LIMIT_LOOKUP_USER_PER_MIN=20`, the 21st `GET /api/bookings/by-reference/{r}` from one user inside one injected-clock minute returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with header `Retry-After: 3`, which equals ceil(60/20), and the rendered copy is `Too many attempts. Try again in 3 seconds.`; with `RATE_LIMIT_LOOKUP_IP_PER_MIN=60`, the 61st request from one address across different user accounts returns `Retry-After: 1` and the copy is `Too many attempts. Try again in 1 second.` with the singular noun; with `RECEIPT_RESEND_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300`, a second resend 60 injected seconds after an accepted one returns 429 with `Retry-After: 240` and the copy `A receipt was requested recently. You can request another in 4 minutes.`, and at 250 s elapsed the header reads 50 and the copy renders seconds; with Redis unreachable both endpoints return 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and the PostgreSQL query counter for the request is 0, so no fallback occurs; no Retry-After figure appears as a literal inside any copy string, asserted by the rendered number being substituted from the header.
SourceRef: P-TKT-02 P-TKT-07 P-TKT-09 FR-ADR-058 EP-TKT-01 EP-TKT-02

Title: Build nothing for the door, and prove nothing was built
Description: Entry is a person at the entrance reading the reference and checking it by hand: no scanner, no validation endpoint, no door screen, no staff account and no state anywhere marking a reference as used. OPEN-DOORVERIFY-01 - the venue cannot tell a real reference from an invented one, because no surface returns a booking to anyone but its owner - and OPEN-DUPREF-01 - who is admitted when one reference is presented twice - are both open, and this story invents neither a door surface nor an admission policy.
AcceptanceCriteria: The generated API contract contains no path matching `/validate`, `/scan`, `/checkin`, `/door` or `/tickets`, asserted by listing every path in docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json; exactly two endpoints return a booking reference in a response body, EP-TKT-01 and EP-TKT-02, and both are authorised on ownership alone with the role not consulted; `SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='booking' AND column_name IN ('used_at','admitted_at','scanned_at','checked_in_at')` returns 0; presenting a reference twice writes nothing, asserted by no route, worker branch or audit action existing for an entry event and by the audit action vocabulary containing no door action; SCR-TKT-01 and the plain-text part of SCR-TKT-02 each render the line `Show this reference at the entrance. A person will check it.`; no QR code, barcode or image is generated anywhere in the product, asserted by no QR or barcode library appearing in backend/ dependencies.
SourceRef: P-TKT-08 SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-02 SRC-001 §E E-9 SRC-002 §E E-5

Title: Keep the receipt's dispatch state off the customer API and write no message for a failed send
Description: OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01 is open and reserved to the client: what a customer is told when a receipt definitively fails, and whether the booking stays valid, is not decided here. Phase 5 ships the mechanism and not the message, and no operator action on a failed receipt is built either, because an administrative action taken on a customer's booking after a post-capture send failure is the substance of that row.
AcceptanceCriteria: For two bookings identical except that one receipt_dispatch row reads `sent` and the other `failed`, `GET /api/bookings/by-reference/{r}` returns bodies that differ only in the reference value, and SCR-TKT-01 renders DOM that differs only in the reference and the booking facts, so queued, in flight, sent and failed are indistinguishable on the customer API; a failed send changes no column on the booking row, asserted by capturing every booking column before the worker marks the row failed and comparing after; no endpoint, screen or job resends a receipt on another user's behalf, asserted by every route touching receipt_dispatch requiring booking.user_id to equal the caller's id; no SNS subscription, bounce handler or complaint handler exists in backend/, and no code path marks an email address invalid; no refund path and no write to cancelled_at exists anywhere in the codebase; no customer-facing string mentioning a failed, delayed or undelivered receipt exists in frontend/.
SourceRef: P-TKT-10 P-TKT-11 P-TKT-09 FR-ADR-049 FR-ADR-060

Title: Say in the runbook that sent means SES accepted, never that the customer received
Description: receipt_dispatch records SES acceptance only; bounces and complaints publish to SNS and nothing subscribes, so a bounced or spam-filed receipt sits in the table as sent and is indistinguishable from one that reached the inbox. Dead letter queue depth is not alarmed, outbox pending count is not alarmed, the SES bounce rate is not alarmed, and /metrics is not scraped - the runbook must say all of it in these terms, because the short version is the one that ends a support conversation wrongly.
AcceptanceCriteria: The phase 7 runbook contains a receipt section in which the strings `evidence of dispatch, never of receipt`, `depth is not alarmed` and `nothing scrapes it` each appear at least once; it states that the one ruled alarm watches the ECS running task count below 1 and names the four things that are not alarmed; it gives two runnable queries, one grouping receipt_dispatch by status and one counting outbox_message rows in status pending, and states that no product action exists to resend a receipt on a customer's behalf and that a dead letter redrive is a Zone C console action specified in no file; it contains no sentence asserting that a sent row means a customer received the receipt, asserted by every occurrence of the words delivered and received in that section being negated or attributed to what the product cannot observe.
SourceRef: P-TKT-11 FR-ADR-068 FR-ADR-060 FR-ADR-057 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-01

Title: Send the password-reset email exactly once per request
Description: The same outbox, the same relay, the same worker and the same SES port carry the account lane's reset email, so it is specified to the same standard as the receipt rather than left as a branch. The token row is the claim and it carries the stale branch, because a worker that dies between the claim and the send must not cost a locked-out customer the only route back into their account, and the token value never travels in the queue.
AcceptanceCriteria: Delivering the same password_reset.send message twice produces exactly 1 SES call and `SELECT email_claimed_at IS NOT NULL, email_sent_at IS NOT NULL FROM password_reset_token WHERE id=:t` reads `true, true`; with the worker killed after the claim and before the send the row reads email_claimed_at set and email_sent_at null, a redelivery at claim plus 120 injected seconds makes 0 SES calls and deletes the message, and a redelivery at claim plus 901 seconds with `RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS=900` reclaims the row and makes exactly 1 SES call; an SES refusal, and a call abandoned at SES_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS, each set email_claimed_at back to null, leave email_sent_at null and do not delete the queue message; a redelivery arriving 24 injected hours after email_sent_at was set makes 0 SES calls, because email_sent_at is never cleared; the enqueued payload key set is exactly `message_version, request_id, reset_token_id, user_id` and searching the payload text for the token value finds no match; the worker's booking-resolution deletion rule is not applied to this topic, asserted by a password_reset.send message surviving a worker in which every booking lookup fails.
SourceRef: P-TKT-12 FR-ADR-031 FR-ADR-032 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-059

Title: Hold the cross-cutting floors every other lane is built on
Description: Everything that is true on every request, every screen and every process, and that no single feature owns: the two-layer seat guarantee, integer money, the audit row, authorisation on the router, credentials and sessions, the rate limiter, the cache, health and readiness, logging, configuration, secrets, shutdown, statelessness, migrations, backups, the memory budget, accessibility, the zone boundary, scope governance and the seed. Each of these is a defect a customer eventually meets, and each has a wrong implementation that passes ordinary tests.

Title: Prove no seat is sold twice under fifty simultaneous hold requests
Description: The product's central invariant, proved rather than asserted (SRC-001 §3.2). This is Stage A of the drill: the fifty-request gate at the hold endpoint. It proves the Redis lock layer and the end-to-end result, and it is recorded as exercising the unique constraint zero times, which is why Stage B (S-XCT-02) exists and may not be skipped. This gate is never waived, never skipped and never marked expected-to-fail.
AcceptanceCriteria: scripts/stress_seats.py --showtime 41 --seat 312 --n 50 run against the local compose stack reports exactly 1 HTTP 201 and exactly 49 HTTP 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE - exactly one, never 'at most one', and zero winners is also a failure; the winner then confirms and SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=41 AND seat_id=312 read directly from PostgreSQL returns exactly 1; the script records the start instant of each of the fifty requests and asserts the spread between first and last is under STRESS_CONCURRENCY_SPREAD_MS (default 100 ms), exiting non-zero with 'not concurrent' rather than 'passed' when it is not; the run reports unique-constraint violations = 0, because all 49 losers are refused by Redis at SET ... NX and the constraint is never reached at the hold endpoint; the run is made as fifty distinct authenticated customers and no rate-limit control is disabled for it; the same script runs against the deployed environment by changing a base URL only; the outcome is recorded with who ran it and the date, because an undated claim that it was run is not evidence.

Title: Watch the unique constraint fail and work again with two live holders on one seat
Description: Stage B of the red-proof drill, added on 2026-08-22 because the single-stage drill could not work: the fifty-request gate fires at the hold, where the constraint is never reached, so dropping it changed nothing and the never-waivable gate reported failure against a correct implementation. Stage B produces the only state from which two confirms both reach the insert. Nothing is disabled - a lock key is made to disappear, which is a fault the database half exists to survive.
AcceptanceCriteria: With PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS=1500 in the local compose stack: customer A holds seat (41, 312) and issues a confirm asynchronously; inside that delay window the drill runs DEL lock:seat:41:312 directly in Redis; customer B then holds the same seat and receives 201 with token tB, because SET ... NX succeeds on the missing key and no committed booking_seat row exists yet - two live holders on one seat; B confirms and both transactions reach the seat-occupancy insert. With the constraint present the run produces exactly 1 HTTP 201, exactly 1 HTTP 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE and exactly 1 booking_seat row for (41, 312), and that 409 is the constraint firing, observed. The constraint is then dropped with ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT and the steps repeated: the run produces exactly 2 HTTP 201s and SELECT count(*) returns exactly 2 - the seat sold twice. If it still returns 1 the drill is recorded as failed, the whole proof is void, and that is a stop-the-line finding. The constraint is restored, the repeat produces 1 row again, and it is read back from pg_constraint and found present. Stage A run with the constraint dropped produces one winner and that is the expected result and not a finding. Local environment only; both stages recorded with operator and date.
SourceRef: P-XCT-01 SRC-002 §9.1 FR-ADR-034 FR-ADR-024 E8 S7.1

Title: Enforce the seat guarantee in two independent systems and waive neither half
Description: A Redis lock provides the hold and a unique constraint plus row locking provides the truth. The database half may not be waived at any confidence for any reason - waiving a quality check is reserved to the client, and this is the check. The two layers catch different events: the lock refuses a second customer while a first holds the seat, the constraint refuses a second confirm after Redis was wrong.
AcceptanceCriteria: A total UNIQUE (showtime_id, seat_id) constraint exists on the seat-occupancy table with no WHERE clause, verified by SELECT conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'booking_seat'::regclass returning a definition containing no WHERE; grep -rn 'ON CONFLICT' backend/ returns no hit anywhere touching the seat-occupancy table; no pre-insert SELECT to see whether a seat is free exists on the confirm path, and SELECT ... FOR UPDATE appears only against the showtime row - a row lock on rows that do not exist locks nothing, so two transactions would both find no row and both insert; a unique violation at insert is caught and returned as HTTP 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE, never HTTP 500, is not retried, and is logged at INFO with the seat_conflicts_total counter incremented rather than as an exception; the sentence a customer sees for that 409 is P-HLD-14 row 4 (one seat lost) or row 4b (two or more), the at-confirm sentences, and this floor publishes none of its own; the isolation level is READ COMMITTED and the guarantee is asserted to hold at it.

Title: Create the seat-occupancy unique constraint in the Phase 2 migration
Description: The constraint is created before any code can write a booking, so no window exists in which bookings are written without it. Removing it is a schema change and the only permitted removal is the local red-proof drill.
AcceptanceCriteria: The Alembic migration that creates the seat-occupancy table creates UNIQUE (showtime_id, seat_id) in the same migration, verified by running alembic upgrade head against an empty database and then SELECT conname FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'booking_seat'::regclass AND contype = 'u' returning exactly one row; no later revision up to head drops it, verified by grep for DROP CONSTRAINT across backend/migrations/ returning no hit; no revision that can write a booking row precedes the revision that creates the constraint; the constraint carries no WHERE clause and is not a partial index.
SourceRef: P-XCT-01 P-XCT-19 FR-ADR-062 E8 S7.1 E8 S7.18

Title: Compute and store every money value as integer paise through one function
Description: Currency is INR, the minor unit is paise and the ratio is 100. Decimal at the parsing boundary, bigint in persistence, a formatted string at render time only. Changing CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO is a one-way door reserved to the client: bookings are permanent, and no row records which interpretation it was written under.
AcceptanceCriteria: CURRENCY_CODE=INR and CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO=100 are loaded and validated at boot and logged once, and the process exits non-zero at boot if the ratio is anything other than 100 while the code is INR; every money column is bigint and every money identifier carries a _paise suffix, asserted by a test that fails on any column whose name matches price, amount or total and whose type is not bigint; no float appears anywhere on the money path, asserted by grep over backend/app for float( and : float in the pricing, booking and reporting modules returning no hit; exactly one pricing function takes two integers and returns one integer, and the seat map, the checkout total, the receipt, the dashboard and scripts/seed.py all call it - a second implementation of the formula is the defect this criterion hunts; three Recliner seats at 33333 paise each produce a booking total of exactly 99999 paise and never 99998, because the total is the sum of already-rounded per-seat prices and the total is never rounded; a money field that is not a valid decimal or is negative returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with 'Enter an amount as a number, for example 250.00.'; more than two decimal places returns 422 with 'An amount can have at most two decimal places.'; a SUM() over a bigint money column is cast back to BigInteger in the query rather than arriving as Decimal.
SourceRef: P-XCT-02 SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01 SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 FR-ADR-036 FR-ADR-038 E8 S7.2

Title: Write every privileged change and its audit row in one transaction
Description: Either both land or neither does. An audit row written after the commit is missing exactly the rows that crashed. The rows are written from Phase 2 even though the screen that reads them is Phase 8, because an audit trail that starts when its reader is built has a hole exactly as long as the build took.
AcceptanceCriteria: An admin changing showtime 41's base price from 25000 to 28000 paise during request a1b2c3d4 commits one audit_log row in the same transaction as the change, carrying actor_user_id 17, actor_role admin, action showtime.base_price_changed, entity_type showtime, entity_id 41, before {base_price_paise: 25000}, after {base_price_paise: 28000} and request_id a1b2c3d4; with a fault injected into the audit insert the whole transaction rolls back and SELECT base_price_paise FROM showtime WHERE id = 41 still returns 25000; with a fault injected into the change no audit_log row exists for it; actor_user_id is non-null and references a real user row, never a role name and never a service account; actor_role is the value copied at the time of the write and is never resolved by a join at read time; before and after carry only the fields that changed and never a whole-row snapshot, and before is null for a creation; occurred_at is timestamptz in UTC.
SourceRef: P-XCT-03 SRC-001 §7.6 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 FR-ADR-019 FR-ADR-012 E8 S7.3

Title: Make audit_log append-only in the database and close the action vocabulary
Description: Append-only at the database-role level rather than by convention, and a closed controlled vocabulary for action - because a filter written against a non-member returns an empty list while looking entirely correct.
AcceptanceCriteria: The application database role holds INSERT and SELECT on audit_log and no UPDATE and no DELETE, verified by SELECT privilege_type FROM information_schema.table_privileges WHERE table_name = 'audit_log' AND grantee = the application role returning exactly INSERT and SELECT; an attempted UPDATE audit_log SET action = 'x' as that role raises a permission error, the request returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR and the customer sees 'The server could not complete this request. If you need help, quote a1b2c3d4.' with no variant minted for the audit path; the same holds for DELETE; an action value outside the published controlled vocabulary is refused with 500 INTERNAL_ERROR at a boundary check that runs before the transaction opens, asserted by a test in which the shortened paraphrase base_price_changed is refused and showtime.base_price_changed is accepted; no section coins an action string of its own, asserted by a test that every action literal in backend/app is a member of the published list.
SourceRef: P-XCT-03 FR-ADR-019 E8 S7.3

Title: Answer who booked any seat, when, and what they paid
Description: Answered by the permanent booking record and not by the audit log: a customer booking a seat is the product working, not a privileged write. Rendered in Asia/Kolkata, because the date boundary is taken in the cinema's zone and never in the container's UTC.
AcceptanceCriteria: For seat 312 of showtime 41 the answer resolves booking_seat to booking_id 9008 with price_paise 28124 snapshotted at hold acquisition and never recomputed, booking to user_id 4471 with created_at 2026-08-12T18:41:03Z, and renders 'Booked by nikhil@example.invalid on 13 Aug 2026 at 00:11 (Asia/Kolkata) for ₹281.24' - 18:41:03Z on 12 August is 00:11 on 13 August in Asia/Kolkata and the rendered date is the local one; the seat-occupancy row for the pair resolves to exactly one booking, guaranteed by the unique constraint, and its absence means the seat was never sold and returns HTTP 200 with an empty result and 'This seat has not been booked.', which is a valid answer and not an error; a manager asking about a screen they are not assigned to receives 403 FORBIDDEN with 'This account does not have access to that hall.'; a customer asking about a booking that is not theirs receives 403 FORBIDDEN; the manager scope check runs on the router as a dependency and never in the handler; the test asserts a non-empty result for the manager's own screens and a denied result for another's, because a test asserting only 'denied' passes against a query that returns nothing for anybody.
SourceRef: P-XCT-04 SRC-001 §7.6 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-02 FR-ADR-012 FR-ADR-039 E8 S7.19

Title: Make nothing on a path to a booking deletable
Description: The question 'who booked this seat and when' has to be answerable at any time, which means nothing on a path that can reach a booking is ever removed. The product is not delete-free in general - a seat and a manager screen assignment are genuinely deleted - and those two are unreachable from a booking by their own preconditions.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every foreign key on a path that can reach a booking is declared ON DELETE RESTRICT and none is CASCADE or SET NULL, verified by SELECT conname, confdeltype FROM pg_constraint WHERE contype = 'f' returning confdeltype 'r' for every such constraint; booking.user_id is NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT; an attempted delete of a referenced row fails with a foreign key violation rather than succeeding silently; no pruning job, no retention window and no scheduled deletion exists anywhere in the repository; every table carries created_at and every table that mutates carries updated_at; the two genuinely deleted entities - a seat, permitted only while its hall has no showtime rows at all, and a manager_screen_assignment row - are the only mounted DELETE routes and neither is reachable from a booking.
SourceRef: P-XCT-04 P-XCT-22 FR-ADR-012 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-02

Title: Apply authorisation once, on each of the four routers, as a dependency
Description: Four routers - public, customer, reporting and admin - each with one authorisation dependency. A handler contains no role check, because a per-handler check is the pattern that eventually misses one. PROVISIONAL: the four-role set is a build-session reading of SRC-003 C-1 and one message from the client reverses it; the story is written against the reading recorded there and decides nothing.
AcceptanceCriteria: Four routers exist and each carries exactly one authorisation dependency attached at the router: public (no session), customer (/api/me, /api/bookings, /api/holds), reporting (/api/reports, role manager or admin) and admin (/api/admin, role admin only); grep -rn for a role comparison inside backend/app/api handlers returns no hit - every handler runs having performed no authorisation of its own; the caller's role is read from the user row on every request and never from a claim in the token, asserted by a test that changes a role in the database and observes the new role take effect on the next request rather than at the next sign-in; a request with no session to a non-public router returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED; a session whose JWT is expired or does not verify returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED with 'You were signed out. Sign in again to continue.'; a signed-in user reaching a router their role does not permit returns 403 FORBIDDEN; PATCH /api/admin/showtimes/101 as a manager returns 403 FORBIDDEN refused by the admin router's role dependency before the body is parsed, and this case carries its own test because it is the one SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 exists to prevent; the manager router mounts no write route at all; the four generic sentences this floor publishes are used only where the surface's own P-row publishes none.
SourceRef: P-XCT-05 SRC-001 §7.4 SRC-003 C-1 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 FR-ADR-009 FR-ADR-011 S3 S3.5

Title: Resolve a manager's screen scope from the session and never from the request
Description: A screen id in the query string may only narrow the set the dependency resolved and can never widen it. A handler that read screen_id and trusted it would hand a manager a hall they are not assigned to. Sits at Phase 8 because the reporting surface it asserts against is Phase 8; the dependency itself ships with the router at Phase 2 (S-XCT-10).
AcceptanceCriteria: With manager 88 assigned screens 2 and 5: GET /api/reports/dashboard with no screen_id returns 200 with a non-empty body covering exactly screens 2 and 5, resolved from the session; GET /api/reports/dashboard?screen_id=2 returns 200 non-empty; GET /api/reports/dashboard?screen_id=4 returns 403 FORBIDDEN and is refused rather than honoured; POST /api/reports/dashboard returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED in the product envelope and not 404, because the path exists for GET; the scope is applied in the query's WHERE clause by the dependency and never by filtering rows after they are fetched, asserted by inspecting the emitted SQL; the mandated test asserts both halves - a non-empty, non-zero figure for the manager's own screen and a denied result for another's - because a test asserting only 'denied' passes against a query that returns nothing for anybody; a manager with no screens assigned receives 200 and an empty dashboard, which is the correct state for a new account and must not render as an error; an admin runs the same queries with no screen filter.
SourceRef: P-XCT-05 SRC-001 §4.4 SRC-003 OPEN-SCOPE-01 FR-ADR-011 S3 S3.4

Title: Store credentials so they cannot be read back
Description: Our own email and password with bcrypt, off the event loop. Never Cognito. The 72-byte ceiling is enforced explicitly with its own message because bcrypt silently truncates there, and a truncation nobody sees means two different long passwords authenticate the same account.
AcceptanceCriteria: Registration with an 11-character password returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with 'Use a password of at least 12 characters.', the floor being PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH characters and not bytes; 25 Devanagari characters, which are 75 bytes, return 422 with 'Use a password of 72 bytes or fewer. Some characters count as more than one byte.' and are not silently truncated, while 72 Latin characters are accepted; a second registration at an address already registered returns 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED and not a generic 422, so the interface can offer the sign-in tab and the reset link; a wrong email or password at sign-in returns 401 CREDENTIALS_INVALID and not AUTH_REQUIRED; a unique index exists on lower(email) and the email is stored as entered; the maximum email length is 254 characters; bcrypt runs in a thread and never inside an async def, asserted by a test that issues concurrent sign-ins and observes the event loop is not blocked for the duration of a hash; sign-in against an unknown email compares against a dummy hash so response timing does not disclose whether an account exists; the plaintext appears in no log line at any level, no response body and no column.

Title: Carry the session in an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie with Secure from configuration
Description: SameSite=Lax is this product's only cross-site request defence - there is no CSRF token, no double-submit cookie and no Origin check anywhere - so the two changes that remove it are named and tested against. Touches OPEN-TLS-01, which is OPEN and DEFERRED: the criterion specifies only the surface the deferral forces and says nothing about whether TLS is or will be terminated anywhere.
AcceptanceCriteria: A successful sign-in sets the session cookie with HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ and Max-Age equal to SESSION_TTL_SECONDS (43200), and with Secure present if and only if COOKIE_SECURE is true; COOKIE_SECURE has no default and the process exits non-zero at boot naming the variable when it is absent; a boot-time cross-field check refuses COOKIE_SECURE=true unless PUBLIC_BASE_URL begins with https://, and the process exits non-zero; the JWT is never written to localStorage, asserted by grep over frontend/src for localStorage returning no hit that stores a token; no endpoint in the product changes state on a GET, asserted by a test that walks the mounted route table and fails on any GET route that writes - this is a stated security requirement and not REST tidiness, because Lax sends the cookie on a top-level GET navigation; SameSite=None appears nowhere in the repository; a session that expires mid-flow returns 401 AUTH_REQUIRED with the customer's context preserved in sessionStorage.
SourceRef: P-XCT-06 P-XCT-29 SRC-003 OPEN-TLS-01 FR-ADR-069 E8 S7.5

Title: Rate-limit per user and per IP with one atomic Redis token bucket that fails closed
Description: A token bucket evaluated by a Lua script so the read, the refill and the decrement are one atomic operation, two independent buckets per limited request, and 503 rather than unlimited access when Redis is gone. Bucket values are estimates, not measurements, and Phase 7's load test replaces them.
AcceptanceCriteria: Each limited request evaluates two buckets - one keyed on the server-derived user id, one on the resolved client address - inside a single Lua script, and both must have a token for the request to proceed; an empty bucket returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with a Retry-After header in integer seconds and details.retry_after_seconds matching it; with the Redis container stopped a limited endpoint returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with 'That is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes.' and never unlimited access, asserted by stopping Redis and issuing one limited request; a retry carrying an already-seen Idempotency-Key still consumes a token, because it is a real request arriving at the server; every bucket size is a named configuration variable and no bucket size is a literal, asserted by grep; FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS set to * exits non-zero at boot; the failure path reads nothing from Redis to build its error message or its log line.

Title: Take the real client address from the right of X-Forwarded-For
Description: A rate limiter behind a load balancer limits the load balancer. This has a wrong implementation that is silent - trusting the leftmost entry, which a client can forge - so it carries its own test rather than relying on the limiter's own tests passing.
AcceptanceCriteria: Two requests issued from the same peer carrying two different forged X-Forwarded-For values are counted in the same bucket, asserted directly as its own test; the resolved address is taken from X-Forwarded-For counting from the right and skipping exactly one trusted proxy, never the leftmost entry; the application runs with --proxy-headers and an explicit --forwarded-allow-ips, and FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS is never *, refused at boot if it is; nothing client-supplied selects a bucket key - the key is the server-derived user id or the resolved peer address and nothing else.

Title: Compute Retry-After from the bucket's refill rate and never from a constant
Description: 900 was published once as a wait, and 900 is the sign-in bucket's window rather than its refill interval. Every derivation is tabulated once in S7.20 and the header is computed at the point of refusal.
AcceptanceCriteria: Retry-After is ceil(window_seconds / capacity) for the bucket that actually refused, computed and never typed: the seat-hold per-user bucket at 20 tokens per 60 s gives ceil(60/20) = 3 and the header reads 3 with 'Too many requests. Try again in 3 seconds.'; the sign-in per-IP bucket at 30 per 900 s gives ceil(900/30) = 30 and reads 'Too many attempts. Try again in 30 seconds.'; the sign-in per-user bucket at 10 per 900 s gives ceil(900/10) = 90; registration and password-reset at 5 per 3600 s give ceil(3600/5) = 720, rendered as '12 minutes' because 720 is at or above the 120-second threshold; the value 900 never appears as a wait anywhere in customer copy; the header is always integer seconds and is never itself rendered to a customer; the number in every such sentence is interpolated from configuration and never typed as a literal.
SourceRef: P-XCT-07 P-XCT-06 FR-ADR-058 E8 S7.4 E8 S7.20 E8 S7.21

Title: Obtain the proof's fifty sessions in an untimed warm-up so the login bucket never touches the measured window
Description: Fifty sign-ins from the script's one address exceed RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_IP_PER_15MIN at its default of 30, so without the phase split the one gate this project calls never-waivable could not obtain its sessions. A warm-up removes the login bucket from the measured result without disabling anything.
AcceptanceCriteria: scripts/stress_seats.py prints RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_IP_PER_15MIN and RATE_LIMIT_HOLD_IP_PER_MIN, read from the environment under test, before the warm-up starts, and exits non-zero if it cannot read either - a run that cannot say what it ran against is not evidence; the warm-up signs fifty seeded customers in through the real POST /api/auth/login endpoint with no test hook, no injected token and no bypass, and holds their access tokens in memory; a warm-up sign-in refused with 429 waits its Retry-After and retries that same customer rather than failing or skipping it, so at the unchanged default of 30 the warm-up completes in about 600 s (30 immediate, then 20 at one token per 30 s) and the measured window is unaffected; the measured window issues zero sign-ins and exactly fifty hold requests; any 429 inside the measured window makes the run void and the script exits non-zero, because a 429 there means the run measured the limiter instead of the lock; no rate-limit control is disabled at any point and only configured bucket sizes differ.
SourceRef: P-XCT-07 P-XCT-01 SRC-002 §9.1 FR-ADR-034 E8 S7.1

Title: Re-run the concurrency proof at the close of Phase 7 against the live rate limiter
Description: The proof is Phase 4 and the limiter is Phase 7, so the Phase 4 run happens before the limiter exists and its condition that the limiter is not disabled is vacuous exactly when the proof first runs. The contradiction is resolved by re-running rather than by weakening either phase.
AcceptanceCriteria: At the close of Phase 7, with the rate limiter present and enabled, Stage A is re-run and reports exactly 1 HTTP 201, exactly 49 HTTP 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE, a start-instant spread under STRESS_CONCURRENCY_SPREAD_MS and exactly 1 booking_seat row for the pair; Stage B is re-run and produces 1 row with the constraint present, 2 rows with it dropped and 1 row with it restored, with the restore read back from pg_constraint; the Phase 4 result is recorded as covering the Phase 4 configuration only and is not treated as covering Phase 7's; both runs are recorded with operator and date; a red gate at either stage marks the story Blocked with a note and is surfaced, and is never faked, skipped or marked expected-to-fail.
SourceRef: P-XCT-01 P-XCT-07 P-XCT-27 SRC-002 §9.1 FR-ADR-034 E8 S7.18

Title: Cache the seat map and the listings cache-aside, invalidating with DEL after commit
Description: Invalidation is a DEL issued after the transaction commits and after the Redis locks are released, never a SET of the new value. The listings are the stated exception and are made unreachable by a generation value because their key set is caller-chosen and unbounded, which is the same idea rather than a relaxation; that mechanism is P-BRW-12's and is not restated here.
AcceptanceCriteria: The seat map is cached at cache:seatmap:{showtime_id} with SEATMAP_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (10) and the listings with LISTING_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (60); after a hold, a release or a booking commits, a DEL is issued for that showtime's key after the commit and after the lock release, in that order, asserted by ordering assertions in the test; grep over backend/ finds no SET of a computed seat-map value on any invalidation path; a rebuild acquires cache:seatmap:{id}:rebuild with SET NX PX CACHE_REBUILD_LOCK_TTL_MS (default 2000, never a literal), and a caller that does not get the lock waits briefly, re-reads the cache, and on a second miss reads PostgreSQL directly rather than blocking; a failed DEL is neither retried nor rolled back and the entry expires within 10 s; the code carries a comment at the stampede site naming the scenario; worst-case staleness a customer can see is 10 s cache TTL plus 3 s poll interval = 13 s, stated rather than rounded down; a stale map never causes an oversell, which the concurrency gate asserts.

Title: Behave differently for each of Redis's three jobs when Redis is gone
Description: Locks fail loudly, the cache degrades to PostgreSQL, the limiter fails closed, and readiness still returns 503. The limiter runs before the cache, so the rate-limited seat-map read returns 503 rather than 200 from PostgreSQL - the stricter of two APPROVED records, adopted without a signature.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the Redis container stopped: a hold and a confirm each return 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE on the configured client timeout with 'Seat holds are unavailable right now. Browsing still works. Try again in a few minutes.'; GET /api/movies and GET /api/showtimes return 200 served from PostgreSQL, because they are not rate-limited; GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap returns 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and not 200, because it is rate-limited, the limiter runs before the cache and it fails closed, and the sentence shown is P-BRW-12's and no variant of it; every other limited endpoint returns 503 with 'That is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes.'; /health/ready returns 503 naming redis within READINESS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (3 s); the Redis client carries explicit connect and command timeouts so an unreachable node produces a 503 rather than a hung request that exhausts the connection pool; grep over backend/ finds no code path that falls back to PostgreSQL for locking; after a Redis restart every live hold is gone and those customers see 'Your seats were released. Choose them again if they are still free.'

Title: Serve /health/live and /health/ready with deliberately different behaviour
Description: A liveness check that touches a dependency turns every dependency outage into a restart loop; a readiness check that does not touch one keeps a broken instance in the load balancer. Collapsing the two defeats why they exist. Which endpoint goes where is Zone C and the client wires it.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /health/live returns 200 with body {status: 'live'} while the process can serve HTTP, and issues no database query, no Redis command, no disk read and no network call - asserted by stopping both PostgreSQL and Redis and still receiving 200 within the same latency; GET /health/ready runs SELECT 1 against PostgreSQL and PING against Redis on a short timeout and returns 200 with {status: 'ready', checks: {postgres: 'ok', redis: 'ok'}, payment_provider: <PAYMENT_PROVIDER>}; with PostgreSQL stopped it returns 503 naming postgres while /health/live still returns 200; with Redis stopped, 503 naming redis; with both stopped, 503 naming both; with SES, SQS or S3 unavailable it still returns 200, because the API serves almost every request without them; the readiness check fails fast on its own timeout rather than timing out at the caller; the result is cached for READINESS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (3); neither endpoint is authenticated and neither returns a version, a hostname or a connection string, PAYMENT_PROVIDER being the one deliberate disclosure; both are Zone B files and every line that exists for a production reason carries a comment saying what breaks without it, including one on /health/live saying why it deliberately does nothing; docs/30 Deployment/ states that the load balancer target group health check points at /health/ready and any container-level restart check points at /health/live, and that reversing them turns a recoverable outage into a restart loop.
SourceRef: P-XCT-10 SRC-002 §7.4 FR-ADR-055 FR-ADR-041 E8 S7.7 EP-XCT-01 EP-XCT-02

Title: Return one error envelope with a stable code, and show a request id on 5xx only
Description: The interface branches on code, never on message - branching on 409 alone produces one screen for five situations. The framework's own validation error shape is replaced, because a default 422 body would break the contract on exactly the errors a form hits most.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every error response, including the framework's own validation failure and its own method-not-allowed, is the envelope {error: {code, message, details, request_id}}, asserted by a test that forces one failure on every mounted route and validates each body against that shape; the interface branches on code and grep over frontend/src finds no branch on message; an unhandled exception returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with 'The server could not complete this request. If you need help, quote a1b2c3d4.' and the stack trace in the log only; a body that fails validation returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with the failing fields in details; a path or resource that does not exist for any method returns 404 NOT_FOUND with 'That page does not exist.'; a unique-constraint violation on seat occupancy returns 409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE and never INTERNAL_ERROR, because it is the guard working; a 4xx carries request_id in the body and the interface does not display it, while a 5xx displays it; no response body anywhere contains a stack trace, SQL, an exception class, a hostname or a table name; the five 409 codes SEAT_UNAVAILABLE, HOLD_EXPIRED, SALES_CLOSED, IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT and VERSION_CONFLICT each drive a different interface branch, asserted by five separate interface tests.

Title: Answer a method no route serves with 405 in the product envelope, from one global handler
Description: A route mounted only to say no is a route somebody will later make work, so the never-deleted entities get no DELETE route at all and a global handler renders the envelope instead. The message is generic and entity-blind by necessity: routing failed before any handler ran, and a sentence naming the entity would be a claim the code cannot support.
AcceptanceCriteria: POST /health/live returns HTTP 405 carrying the product envelope with code METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED and message 'That action is not available. Nothing was changed.', rendered by one exception handler mounted on the application and on no router; a DELETE addressed at any of movie, showtime, screen, cinema or the four lookup vocabularies returns the same 405 and none of those DELETE routes appears in the mounted route table, asserted by walking the route table; DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} is a real mounted route that returns success while its hall has no showtime rows at all, and never reaches this handler; the same 405 is returned for any non-GET method addressed at a path on the read-only reports router, because that path exists and serves GET; a path that exists for no method at all returns 404 NOT_FOUND and not 405, so 'no such address' and 'not that verb' stay separable; the 405 message names no entity and carries no 'what to do next', because there is nothing to do; the code appears in no endpoint block's errors array until the merge owner adds it to VALID_CODES in docs/03 PRD/api/generate_api.py, and a lane finding it absent from contract.json has found the expected state.
SourceRef: P-XCT-11 P-XCT-05 FR-ADR-052 FR-ADR-012 E8 S6

Title: Emit JSON logs to stdout with a request id we generate
Description: One object per line to stdout, never a file. An inbound X-Request-Id is never trusted for correlation. Eight lowercase hex characters is a length chosen so a person can read it aloud or type it from a screen, and it is a correlation aid rather than a key - about a half chance of a collision by 77,000 ids, stated rather than glossed.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every log line is one JSON object on stdout carrying timestamp, level, logger, message, service, instance_id and request_id; no code path writes a log file, asserted by grep over backend/ for FileHandler, RotatingFileHandler and open( on a log path returning no hit; the request id is generated per request from a random source and matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$ - eight lowercase hexadecimal characters, which is what a1b2c3d4 in every published string is; a client-supplied X-Request-Id is recorded as the separate field client_request_id and is never used for correlation; every response carries the generated id in the X-Request-Id header; exactly one INFO line is written per completed request carrying route, method, status_code and duration_ms; a SEAT_UNAVAILABLE outcome is logged at INFO with a counter and never at WARNING, because logging correct behaviour as a warning trains the operator to ignore warnings; health-check polls are not logged at INFO while their failures are; nothing joins on request_id and no column is unique on it.

Title: Propagate the request id from the confirm into the worker's receipt job
Description: Without the propagation the worker's line is unfindable from the API's, and 'what happened to this booking' cannot be answered end to end from one search. The consequence that makes the whole logging specification worth having is Zone C: container stdout dies with the container unless the awslogs driver is configured, which the prep queue carries with a needed-by of Phase 1.
AcceptanceCriteria: The booking's outbox row carries the originating request_id, it travels in the queue message payload, and it is bound to the worker's logging context for the whole job; one search for request_id = a1b2c3d4 across the log group returns both the API line ({service: 'api', route: '/api/bookings', status_code: 201, booking_id: 9008}) and the worker line ({service: 'worker', job_id present, booking_id: 9008, message: 'receipt sent'}), asserted end to end in an integration test; the migration run logs the same way as the API and the worker; docs/30 Deployment/ carries a specification for the awslogs log driver with a needed-by phase of Phase 1 and states that with the default driver the record of a crash loop is destroyed by the restart that caused it.

Title: Redact centrally, and never log a credential or a reference beside an email address
Description: A denylist applied on the logging pipeline rather than at the call site, because a redaction that has to be remembered at each call site is a redaction that is forgotten at one. No card data exists in this system and the rule stays stated so nobody adds a card-shaped log field out of habit.
AcceptanceCriteria: A redaction filter is installed on the logging pipeline and applies a denylist of field names centrally, asserted by a test that logs a structure containing password, password_hash, jwt, authorization and cookie and finds every value replaced in the emitted line without any call-site change; no log line at any level contains card data, a password, a password hash, a JWT, a session cookie, an Authorization header, a resolved secret value or a full request body; no line carries a booking reference and the customer's email address together, because together they are enough to walk into a hall, asserted by a test over the receipt and booking log paths; LOG_LEVEL defaults to INFO in every environment and DEBUG is refused in the deployed environment by the runbook rather than by code.
SourceRef: P-XCT-12 SRC-002 §7.6 FR-ADR-056 E8 S7.8

Title: Expose /metrics in Prometheus format, and record in writing that nothing scrapes it
Description: Built because SRC-002 §7.7 requires it and because it is a learning deliverable. Nothing in the approved stack scrapes it, nothing stores its history and nothing alerts on it, and that is said plainly rather than absorbed. Adding Prometheus, Grafana Cloud or a CloudWatch Prometheus scrape needs the client's permission first and is not designed around.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /metrics on the container's port returns Prometheus text exposition format with content type text/plain; version=0.0.4 carrying all eight series - http_requests_total{route,method,status}, http_request_duration_seconds{route}, seat_locks_held, queue_depth, seat_conflicts_total, booking_confirmations_total{outcome}, receipt_dispatch_total{outcome} and outbox_pending; the API runs a single uvicorn worker per container, so a scrape returns the whole process's counters rather than one worker's view; the worker serves its own /metrics on WORKER_METRICS_PORT (default 8001), which differs from API_PORT (default 8000) and is refused at boot if equal or outside 1024-65535; seat_locks_held is read from an O(1) Redis counter maintained by the acquire and release paths and never by a SCAN per scrape, and its drift is reconciled by a bounded SCAN on the worker's existing loop and not on a schedule; queue_depth returns the last cached value with its age when SQS is unreachable, and a scrape does not become an AWS API call each time; docs/30 Deployment/ states that no load balancer listener rule may match /metrics and what is disclosed if one does - traffic volumes and internal route names; the runbook records that nothing scrapes this endpoint, nothing stores its history and nothing alerts on it.
SourceRef: P-XCT-13 SRC-002 §7.7 SRC-002 §5.3 FR-ADR-057 E8 S6 EP-XCT-03

Title: Specify the one alarm, set missing data to breaching, and publish the unwatched list
Description: One alarm was ruled and adding five more would be inventing scope and doing the client's Zone C work in one move. The alarm, the topic and the subscription are all Zone C. There is one operator and no backup decider, so there is no escalation path and there cannot be.
AcceptanceCriteria: docs/30 Deployment/ carries a specification for exactly one CloudWatch alarm - the ECS service's running task count below 1, delivering through SNS to the operator's own address - and the repository contains no second alarm specification and no alarm definition of any kind; the specification states that missing data must be treated as breaching, and says why: with the default treatment a deleted service or a metric that stops being published leaves the alarm in INSUFFICIENT_DATA and it never fires, which is worse than no alarm because it is believed; the acceptance criterion is stated as: stop the service, receive an email; the alert address appears nowhere in the repository and lives only in the SNS subscription the client creates and in a local .env; the specification publishes the unwatched list worst first with dead letter queue depth named first, and includes S3 poster-bucket size and object count as the one store in the product with no deletion path and no bound; a dead-letter-queue alarm is recommended in writing and is explicitly not adopted; the build session creates none of the alarm, the topic or the subscription.
SourceRef: P-XCT-14 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-01 SRC-001 §8.2 FR-ADR-068 E8 S7.14

Title: Load every setting from the environment and exit non-zero at boot when one is wrong
Description: Validation runs at import time, before the application accepts a request. A container that starts and then fails on its first booking is worse than one that never starts, because the container runtime reports it healthy. A sensible default so the app starts locally is forbidden for exactly that reason.
