AcceptanceCriteria: With DATABASE_URL unset the process exits non-zero with a message naming DATABASE_URL and never begins accepting requests, and the same holds for REDIS_URL, QUEUE_URL, JWT_SECRET and COOKIE_SECURE, none of which has a default; a variable failing its type or bound exits non-zero naming the variable and the bound; twelve cross-field checks run at boot in the order S7.9 lists them, and each is asserted: PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS = 200000 against SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS = 180 is refused by PAYMENT_SIMULATED_DELAY_MS < SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS * 1000 * 0.1 while 1500 is accepted; CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO other than 100 with CURRENCY_CODE = INR exits non-zero; a CINEMA_TIMEZONE that does not resolve in the zone database exits non-zero; COOKIE_SECURE true without PUBLIC_BASE_URL beginning https:// exits non-zero; API_PORT and WORKER_METRICS_PORT are each between 1024 and 65535 and are not equal, checked at boot in both processes; the resolved configuration is logged exactly once with secret values redacted and PAYMENT_PROVIDER logged prominently; grep finds no ENVIRONMENT=production style switch anywhere; .env.example lists every variable with a comment saying what it does and what breaks without it, carries obviously-placeholder values, and contains no real value and no credential; every declaration in the Zone B configuration file carries a comment saying what breaks if the variable is wrong or absent.

Title: Read secrets from SSM through the task definition and never from the application
Description: The application reads an ordinary environment variable and knows nothing about SSM - no SDK call for configuration, no client, no bootstrap fetch, no IAM dependency at read time. AWS Secrets Manager is forbidden. Locally the same variables come from a .env file so the code path is identical in both environments.
AcceptanceCriteria: grep over backend/app for ssm, get_parameter and boto3 client construction for configuration returns no hit - the application reads JWT_SECRET, DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL as ordinary environment variables; docs/30 Deployment/ specifies the parameter naming /frontrow/<environment>/<VARIABLE_NAME> matching the variable name exactly, SecureString type for those three only, encryption with the AWS-managed key for SSM rather than a customer-managed KMS key, and delivery through the ECS task definition's secrets block using valueFrom with the parameter ARN; the specification names the execution role grants ssm:GetParameters on /frontrow/* and kms:Decrypt on the AWS-managed SSM key, and states that putting ssm:GetParameters on the task role instead makes the task fail to start with an error that does not obviously say why, because ECS resolves the parameter before the container starts; it states that changing a parameter takes effect only on a new task deployment and that rotating JWT_SECRET invalidates every live session with no rotation mechanism; a SecureString is not specified for any value that appears in this document, such as SEAT_HOLD_TTL_SECONDS; .env is git-ignored, the staged diff is scanned before every push, and no credential is committed; the build session creates no parameter, no role and no task definition, and never reads a SecureString's decrypted value into a log or a document. Needed by Phase 1.

Title: Drain on SIGTERM and release this instance's holds through a Redis registry
Description: The registry is a set in Redis and not process memory: statelessness forbids local state, and a process SIGKILLed after the grace period loses in-memory state before it can act on it. Correctness never depends on the release running - the locks expire in three minutes - which is the property that makes this safe to get wrong. The lock-release half has nothing to release until Phase 4 and is re-checked there.
AcceptanceCriteria: On SIGTERM the API stops accepting new connections, waits out the deregistration delay so in-flight requests already routed complete, finishes them bounded by SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (20), reads instance:{instance_id}:holds and runs the compare-and-delete release for each key, then exits - asserted by sending SIGTERM to a running container mid-request and observing that request complete with its normal response and the keys gone from Redis; each API instance generates its id at boot and adds each granted hold's keys to its own registry set with the same 180-second TTL as the holds, so an instance that vanishes leaves no permanent garbage; grep finds no in-process hold registry anywhere in backend/app; a key whose token no longer matches is a no-op and cannot free another customer's lock, asserted by expiring a hold, re-acquiring it as a second customer, then draining the first instance and observing the second customer keeps the seat; with the release skipped entirely, the seats are unbuyable for at most 180 s and no booking is affected; on SIGTERM the worker stops polling, finishes the message it is handling, completes any outbox relay batch in progress and exits; docs/30 Deployment/ states that the ECS stop timeout must exceed the deregistration delay plus SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, names all three values as the client's, and says that SIGKILL arriving during the drain skips the release.

Title: Keep every container stateless
Description: Killing any container mid-request must not corrupt data. A file is state on a stateless container and dies with it; a rate-limit counter in process memory multiplies its own limit by the number of processes while appearing to work. Both images declare a read-only root filesystem as their intended runtime mode and enforcing it is Zone C.
AcceptanceCriteria: Both images run with a read-only root filesystem and serve requests without error, asserted by starting the compose stack with read_only: true on both and running the API and worker test suites against it; logs go to stdout and no file is written to local disk, asserted by comparing the container filesystem before and after a run; poster uploads stream to S3 and never touch the container's disk; the guest's seat selection across the sign-in round trip lives in the browser's sessionStorage and never server-side; the per-instance hold registry and the rate-limit counters both live in Redis and grep finds neither in process memory; both images run as a non-root user created in the Dockerfile, and a container asked to bind a port below 1024 exits at boot - the API listens on API_PORT (default 8000) and the target group, the security group's ingress rule and the container's published port are all built against that number; SIGKILL sent to a running container mid-request leaves no partial booking, no orphaned payment and no stranded lock, asserted as a real signal test against a running stack and not as a unit test; a replacement container serves the retry identically and nothing about a request depends on which instance served the previous one.

Title: Run migrations as a separate explicit step and never on boot
Description: There is no code path in the API or the worker that can apply a migration - not at import, not in a lifespan hook, not in the entrypoint's default path, not behind a flag. Alembic does not take an advisory lock, which is widely believed and is not true, and removing that race is the reason for the rule.
AcceptanceCriteria: grep over backend/app for alembic and upgrade( returns no hit - no application code path can apply a migration; the container entrypoint accepts exactly four commands, api, worker, migrate and seed, and only migrate runs alembic upgrade head and exits with the migration's status, while api and worker start a long-running process and touch no migration; starting the image with api against a database one revision behind starts the process, passes /health/live and /health/ready, and fails at the first query touching a new column with a 500 rather than at boot, and the runbook names that symptom; every Alembic downgrade is a stub that raises, and a bad migration is corrected by a new forward migration; a migration touching audit_log or the seat-occupancy table carries a comment saying what it locks and for roughly how long; every migration is backwards-compatible with the running code, because the old code runs against the new schema for the deploy window; the local compose stack creates a restricted application role without superuser; docs/30 Deployment/ states the deploy order as 1 manual snapshot, 2 one-off migrate task on the same image with the command overridden, 3 verify the task exited 0, 4 update the service to the new image, and says that reversing 2 and 4 runs new code against an old schema and that skipping 1 makes 2 unrecoverable after seven days.

Title: Specify the backup, and rehearse the restore with a recorded outcome
Description: A restore that has never been rehearsed is not a recovery. Enabling backups, setting the window and running a restore are all AWS commands that create or modify infrastructure, so they are Zone C and the build session performs none of them. Needed by Phase 2 - the first phase that creates data worth losing - and announced now rather than on the day it blocks.
AcceptanceCriteria: docs/30 Deployment/ specifies RDS automated backups enabled with retention 7 days (which also enables point-in-time recovery), a backup window outside the cinema's busy period, and a manual snapshot before every migration; it states in the client's own terms that a restore creates a new RDS instance with a new endpoint rather than restoring in place, so recovery includes a configuration change and a deploy; that deleting an instance without a final snapshot deletes its automated backups with it; that a corruption discovered in week three is not recoverable from an automated backup and only from a manual snapshot that happened to be taken; and that forever retention and a 7-day backup window are different guarantees; it records that Redis is not backed up because it holds locks and cache, and that S3 posters are not backed up because nothing deletes a poster and a new poster is a new key; the Phase 7 rehearsal restores to a new instance, points a local application at it, and confirms a known booking is present and correct by booking reference, seats and total in paise - for example FR-K7M2-QX9B, seats C12 and C13, total 56248 paise - with the outcome, the operator and the date recorded, and an undated claim that it was run is not evidence; the AWS prep queue carries the backup row with a needed-by of Phase 2.
SourceRef: P-XCT-20 SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-02 SRC-002 §5.2.2 FR-ADR-070 E8 S7.15

Title: Fit three processes inside roughly 1 GB, with explicit limits and measured replacement
Description: Three long-running processes, not four - the scheduler is deleted and there is nothing left for it to run. Every figure in the budget is reasoned from typical figures and not observed, because no part of this application has ever run. Say it rather than work around it is the binding rule: a measured figure over its limit is reported with the number and what it would take to fit.
AcceptanceCriteria: Exactly three long-running processes exist - API, worker and a static frontend container which is not a Node process - and no fourth, asserted against docker-compose.yml and against the deployment specification; docs/30 Deployment/ gives each container an explicit memory limit and states that no container runs unlimited, that a container exceeding a hard limit is killed by the kernel with no slowdown, no warning and no application log explaining why, that one process's leak takes the host down when no limit is set, and that a second task of the same service cannot start on the one instance at these limits with a fixed host port so ECS's default deployment configuration deadlocks; the API runs one uvicorn worker per container and the database pool size is set deliberately rather than defaulted, against roughly 110 maximum connections on db.t3.micro and multiplied across processes; both images are multi-stage and the final backend image measures under 250 MB, reported by docker image ls with the figure recorded, against ECR's 500 MB free tier; at the close of Phase 1 the resident set size of each container is measured at idle and under load and the estimated table - API ~200 MB, worker ~150 MB, static frontend ~15 MB, budgeted ~365 MB against 624-724 MB available after 300-400 MB for the operating system, Docker daemon and ECS agent - is replaced with the measured figures, each labelled measured rather than reasoned.
SourceRef: P-XCT-21 SRC-002 §5.4.1 SRC-002 §13.6 SRC-003 OPEN-PROC-01 FR-ADR-064 E8 S7.12

Title: Introduce no scheduled job of any kind
Description: A design constraint and not merely an absence: no later design may introduce one. Each place a periodic job would otherwise be reached for has a named replacement, and anything that would otherwise be 'the nightly job will fix it' has to be correct when it is written, which is stricter and deliberate.
AcceptanceCriteria: The repository contains no scheduler process, no cron container, no EventBridge rule, no Lambda on a timer and no periodic task inside a process, asserted two ways: docker-compose.yml declares exactly three application services plus PostgreSQL, Redis and ElasticMQ with no cron or scheduler service, and a case-insensitive grep over backend/, frontend/ and docker-compose.yml for cron, apscheduler, celery beat, schedule( and eventbridge returns no hit outside a comment that says why there is none; an abandoned hold becomes available with no process running - with the injected clock advanced to T+181s against HOLD_TTL_SECONDS=180 the seat reads available on GET /api/showtimes/{id}/seatmap and no cleanup job executed; idempotency records are never expired, because a key that expires is a key whose later retry creates a second booking; nothing is ever pruned; stuck outbox rows are relayed by the worker's existing receive loop checking for pending rows older than a short threshold before each poll, and the seat_locks_held counter is reconciled by a bounded SCAN on that same existing loop, neither on a timer; a stale cache entry is removed by its own TTL.
SourceRef: P-XCT-22 SRC-003 OPEN-PROC-01 SRC-002 §E E-4 FR-ADR-005 FR-ADR-012

Title: Add no service or dependency outside the approved list
Description: The stack is fixed by SRC-002 §4 and anything outside it needs the client's permission first. Permission has been sought and granted exactly twice - Amazon SES, now on the approved list, and ElasticMQ for local development only. A dependency that is not obviously necessary costs the client a decision, and there is only one decider.
AcceptanceCriteria: backend/requirements.txt and frontend/package.json contain no task-queue library (RQ, Dramatiq or Celery), no component library, no CSS framework, no CSS-in-JS runtime and no Argon2 package, asserted by a dependency allowlist test that fails on any package not on the recorded list; a case-insensitive grep over backend/, frontend/ and docs/30 Deployment/ for eks, fargate, nat gateway, secretsmanager, managed grafana and opensearch returns no hit except in the sentence that forbids them; the runtime specified is Docker on ECS backed by EC2 with an Application Load Balancer, RDS PostgreSQL, ElastiCache Redis, SQS, SES, S3, SSM Parameter Store, ECR and CloudWatch Logs, and nothing else; MinIO and MailHog are absent and the resulting gap is stated in writing - local development does not fully exercise the poster upload path without AWS credentials and does not exercise SES at all; CloudFront, a bastion host and a VPC interface endpoint are absent; any further addition is put to the client with what it buys and what it costs before it enters the design, and the answer is recorded.
SourceRef: P-XCT-23 SRC-002 §4.12 SRC-002 §5.3 SRC-003 OPEN-EMAIL-01 SRC-003 OPEN-QUEUE-01 FR-ADR-001

Title: Adopt WCAG 2.2 AA as the target, compute every contrast figure, and record the one deviation
Description: Nobody asked for AA; adopting a stricter option needs no signature. Every contrast ratio is computed and recorded rather than asserted, and no conformance is claimed because a claim would need testing this project has not done. OPEN-SEAT-02 ruled out accessible-seat marking, which is a product feature about wheelchair spaces and says nothing about interface accessibility.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every colour token in docs/05 B DesignSystem/tokens.css carries a machine-readable annotation naming what it is and which grounds it may sit on, and contrast.py fails the build on any colour without one, so a colour cannot enter the system unmeasured; CONTRAST.md is generated by contrast.py and no contrast figure anywhere in the product is typed by hand; every recorded pair meets 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text and for non-text interface components, in both themes; every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard, focus order follows visual order, and the focus indicator is visible against every background it can appear on; every input has a programmatically associated label, and every error is associated with its field and announced through a live region rather than only coloured; each of the four seat states is distinguishable without colour perception by fill lightness, a mark and a border; the seat map is a single tab stop with arrow-key grid navigation and never 220 tab stops; exactly one deviation is recorded - the three-minute hold cannot be extended, because the limit exists to release a scarce resource - with its mitigation of a limit displayed from the start, a warning at 60 seconds and the selection restored on expiry, and no second deviation is recorded anywhere; no conformance statement and no accessibility statement is published.
SourceRef: P-XCT-24 SRC-001 §5.2.2 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-02 FR-ADR-051 FR-ADR-044 E8 S7.13

Title: Render the largest hall on a 375-pixel phone, and say who scrolls the map and to where
Description: A container that scrolls is only half a specification; the other half is who scrolls it and to where, and nothing anywhere moved it, so arrow-key focus routinely landed on a seat nobody could see. ASSUMED: the 220-seat hall and its 11 x 20 grid come from OPEN-SCALE-02's 'pick random' and never harden into a constraint - a larger hall simply scrolls further and the rule does not depend on the number.
AcceptanceCriteria: At a 375-pixel-wide viewport the 220-seat hall's seat map renders at --fr-seat-size 24px with --fr-seat-gap 4px and is never shrunk to fit, because 24px is the WCAG 2.2 target-size minimum; the page body never scrolls horizontally on any route, asserted by a test comparing document.body.scrollWidth against the viewport width on every screen; the map scrolls inside its own container, and the visible seat strip is 375 - 32 page gutter - 32 map-field padding - 28 pinned row gutter = 283 px, showing floor((283 + 4) / 28) = 10 of the 20 columns with 273 px hidden at any scroll position; on first paint the container is scrolled to its leading edge so seat 1 of every row is visible; when keyboard focus leaves the visible strip the container scrolls the minimum amount that brings the newly focused seat fully into view, never centred, never animated past --fr-motion-base and never moving the page body; a restored selection scrolls to the first restored seat and an error carrying details.unavailable_seats scrolls to the first named seat, both on the same minimum-movement rule; the container carries scroll-padding-inline-start: var(--fr-seat-gutter) so no focused cell comes to rest under the pinned row gutter, which would be WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11; no programmatic scroll fires on a poll or while the reader is scrolling; every poster slot reserves a 2:3 box before the image arrives so a listing does not reflow.
SourceRef: P-XCT-25 SRC-001 §6.1 SRC-003 OPEN-SCALE-02 FR-ADR-044 FR-ADR-016 E8 S7.13

Title: Write no Zone C artefact, create nothing in AWS, and give a specification instead
Description: Do not give the answer. A reference implementation marked 'reference only' is the answer with a disclaimer attached; the client will read it and the failure that would have taught them will not happen. In exchange for Zone C the build session owes advance notice - a dependency announced on the day it blocks has broken the exchange the zone split rests on.
AcceptanceCriteria: The repository contains no Terraform, no CloudFormation, no ECS task or service definition, no ALB, target group, listener or security group configuration, no VPC or subnet layout, no GitHub Actions or other CI/CD workflow and no CloudWatch alarm or dashboard definition, asserted by a check that no *.tf, *.tfvars, .github/workflows/ or taskdef*.json path exists anywhere in the repository and that no file is marked 'reference only'; every Zone C item has a specification in docs/30 Deployment/ carrying what to build, what the application expects of it, acceptance criteria, and two or three common mistakes, and none of them supplies the artefact; every AWS dependency appears in docs/30 Deployment/AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md with a needed-by phase and is stated in chat while code is still being written; every line in a Zone B file that exists for a production reason carries a comment saying what breaks without it; no aws command that creates, modifies or deletes anything has been run, and only describe, list and get have been used; every statement about how the product behaves in AWS is labelled (reasoned, not observed); a comparison between what exists in AWS and the specification produces a finding for the client and never a repair.
SourceRef: P-XCT-26 SRC-002 §6.1 SRC-002 §6.5 SRC-002 §13.2 SRC-003 OPEN-AWSREAD-01 FR-ADR-004 FR-ADR-003 E8 S7.16

Title: Deliver in eight phases and close each one by telling the client what to test
Description: Nothing is built all at once, and a phase closes only when the client has been told what to test. The client decides when a phase is done, because what 'done' means is theirs.
AcceptanceCriteria: The eight phases are delivered in order - 1 skeleton, configuration, health endpoints, structured logging and the local compose stack; 2 data model, migrations, seed data and admin CRUD for screens, showtimes and pricing; 3 public browsing, listings, the seat-map read path and caching; 4 seat locking, booking confirmation, idempotency and the concurrency proof; 5 the SQS worker, the receipt email and dead letter handling; 6 admin movie management; 7 metrics, rate limiting, the load test and the runbook; 8 the manager and admin dashboard; each phase closes only when a short explanation file exists covering what was built, why it is built that way, and what breaks in production if the deployment is got wrong, and the client has been told what to test - a phase delivered without that has not closed; a red quality gate marks the story Blocked with a note and surfaces it, and is never faked, skipped, marked xfail, commented out or deleted to reach green; a missing required variable makes the dependent story Blocked and never stubbed; work is pulled forward from a later phase only where an earlier phase depends on it, and the seed script is the recorded case - a Phase 2 deliverable and a hard dependency of Phase 4.
SourceRef: P-XCT-27 SRC-002 §12 SRC-002 §E E-3 SRC-003 OPEN-SCOPE-01 FR-ADR-006 E8 S7.18

Title: Escalate a reserved question and never invent an answer
Description: An agent that hits OPEN and fills in something sensible has committed the cardinal sin of this project. Money, anything irreversible or public, secrets, legal and data protection, what the product is, scope changes and waiving any quality check are the client's alone. Adopting a stricter option is not a waiver and needs no signature.
AcceptanceCriteria: No story, code comment, screen, migration or document in this repository supplies an answer to an open Article X row, asserted by a review pass that matches every OPEN row against the surfaces that touch it; the four rows this lane touches are each named and left open with only what may be specified written down - OPEN-TLS-01: COOKIE_SECURE is environment-driven with no default and is off in the deployed environment, and nothing anywhere states that TLS is or will be terminated; OPEN-ATTRIB-01: demonstration content uses obvious placeholders and no image from anywhere, and no real title, poster, brand or source appears; OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01: no withdraw-showtime capability exists in v1 and no withdrawal endpoint, screen or refund behaviour exists, the fail-closed position because an unbuilt capability is recoverable and an unrefunded customer is not; OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01: the mechanism ships and no sentence shown to a customer whose receipt definitively failed after payment is written anywhere, including in SCR-XCT-01, and the omission is stated in the screen itself; a reversible reserved matter is decided and then batched for the client to reverse, and a reserved-and-irreversible matter stops and waits; no timeout default is applied past a reserved matter; a 'you decide everything' instruction leaves reserved matters reserved.
SourceRef: P-XCT-28 SRC-003 OPEN-TLS-01 SRC-003 OPEN-ATTRIB-01 SRC-003 OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01 SRC-003 OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01 FR-ADR-049 FR-ADR-007

Title: Never call the deployed environment production, and put no real customer data in it
Description: OPEN and DEFERRED on OPEN-TLS-01, which is the client's. This story specifies only the surface the deferral forces and decides nothing about TLS. Setting Secure without TLS is not the stricter option, it is broken - the browser would never send the cookie over HTTP and nobody could stay signed in.
AcceptanceCriteria: A case-insensitive grep for the word production across docs/, backend/ and frontend/ returns no hit that names the deployed environment as production, and every remaining hit is a generic statement about production infrastructure; COOKIE_SECURE is a required variable with no default so no deployment starts without stating what it intends, and a boot-time cross-field check refuses COOKIE_SECURE=true unless PUBLIC_BASE_URL begins with https://; only seeded demonstration data is loaded in that environment and every row carries a DEMO prefix on its name or an address at the reserved .invalid domain; nothing is designed around the absence of TLS - grep finds no plain-HTTP-specific workaround, no token in a query string and no alternative session mechanism; no self-signed certificate is used anywhere; docs/30 Deployment/ records the one-step route the client takes when a domain exists (request an ACM certificate validated by DNS, add an HTTPS listener redirecting HTTP to it, set COOKIE_SECURE=true, verify the domain in SES with DKIM and SPF, set PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the HTTPS address) and notes that all but the last two are Zone C and no application code changes; the row closes by a new superseding record and never by editing the existing one.
SourceRef: P-XCT-29 SRC-003 OPEN-TLS-01 FR-ADR-069 FR-ADR-067 E8 S7.16

Title: Seed one cinema, six halls, the lookup vocabulary and eight published placeholder films
Description: Demonstration content that is obviously demonstration content. The hall sizes, the grids, the category names and the uplifts are ASSUMED under OPEN-SCALE-02 and OPEN-SEAT-01 and never harden into a constraint. The one placeholder poster is authored in this repository as a flat design-system shape, so OPEN-ATTRIB-01 - which is about real posters and their licensing - is untouched and stays exactly as open as it was.
AcceptanceCriteria: scripts/seed.py creates DEMO CINEMA with zone Asia/Kolkata; six screens of 90, 120, 150, 180, 200 and 220 seats laid out 9x10, 10x12, 10x15, 12x15, 10x20 and 11x20, checked against themselves before the first write so that rows x columns equals the stated seat count, the three bands sum to the row count and every band is at least one row, exiting non-zero naming the screen if not; rows are labelled A onward with the letter I skipped, so Screen 1's nine rows end at J and no seat label anywhere contains I; seats are numbered 1 upward left to right as the audience faces the screen, labelled row letter plus number with no separator (A1, A10, J20), unique within a screen; category bands are computed and never typed as standard_rows = ceil(rows * 0.5), premium_rows = ceil(rows * 0.3), recliner_rows = rows - standard - premium, giving Screen 1 rows A-E Standard (50 seats), F-H Premium (30) and J Recliner (10); three categories at 0, 1250 and 3333 basis points, producing 24999, 28124 and 33331 paise against the seeded base price of 24999 paise; twelve DEMO-prefixed lookup rows are created before the first film - DEMO LANGUAGE A/B/C, DEMO RATING 1/2, DEMO GENRE 1-4, DEMO FORMAT 1/2; eight films DEMO MOVIE 01 to DEMO MOVIE 08, every one published and inside its display window and every one pointing at one flat placeholder poster committed to the repository, uploaded once through the ordinary poster path and carrying no text, logo or anything resembling a title; assignment is deterministic with language[i mod 3], certification[i mod 2] and genres {genre[i mod 4], genre[(i+1) mod 4]} for i = n - 1, so DEMO MOVIE 04 carries DEMO LANGUAGE A, DEMO RATING 2 and genres DEMO GENRE 4 and DEMO GENRE 1; every one of the twelve lookup rows is referenced by at least one visible film; a fresh seed followed by a customer landing-page request returns a non-empty catalogue and never 'Nothing is showing right now.'; no realistic movie title is generated, no film artwork is invented, no image is fetched from anywhere, no fake-data library is used for names or emails, and no card-shaped data appears in any fixture.
SourceRef: P-XCT-30 SRC-003 OPEN-SEED-01 SRC-003 OPEN-ATTRIB-01 SRC-003 OPEN-SCALE-02 SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-01 FR-ADR-067 FR-ADR-007

Title: Seed 720 showtimes, deterministic occupancy and 11,003 bookings, idempotently
Description: Varying occupancy was specified and no rule was: a random occupancy makes the dashboard a different number on every run and makes any test asserting a revenue figure flaky by construction. The window is centred on the injected clock so the Past group, every dashboard period beyond today and include_past=false all have something to show. Every figure here is ASSUMED and never hardens.
AcceptanceCriteria: The seed creates 6 halls x 4 starts x 30 days = 720 showtimes at local start times 11:00, 14:30, 18:00 and 21:30 in Asia/Kolkata, stored as timestamptz, every start computed from the injected clock and none hardcoded; day index d = 0..29 maps to a local date offset of d - 15, giving 360 past and 360 from today onward; the placeholder identity is (screen_id, starts_at), and on every run after the first the anchor is the local date of the earliest existing seeded showtime rather than the clock, so a second run recomputes the identical 720, finds every one and inserts nothing - asserted by running the seed twice and observing the row count unchanged and no film reassigned; film_index = (k + d) mod 8 over k = 0..719 in ascending (day, slot, screen) order gives every film exactly 90 showtimes; runtime_minutes = 90 + i * 10 for i = 0..7; ends_at is computed once and stored as starts_at + runtime_minutes + SEED_CHANGEOVER_MINUTES with the changeover 20, so the 21:30 slot with the 160-minute film ends at 00:30 the next local day and the longest occupancy of 180 minutes sits inside the 210-minute slot spacing with no overlap on any screen; format alternates by index within each hall so both format rows are carried by a visible showtime and the format filter renders; occupancy_percent = 10 + (k mod 9) * 10 and booked_seats = floor(seat_count * occupancy_percent / 100), taken contiguously from row A seat 1 onward, never reaching 0% and never 100%; booking_size = min(1 + (booking_index mod 10), seats remaining on this showtime) and owner = customer[booking_index mod 50] with booking_index counting from 0 globally, producing exactly 58,800 booked seats in exactly 11,003 bookings at a mean size of 5.344, 220 or 221 per customer so no seeded account has an empty bookings list; 960 seats across six halls x 120 showtimes per hall = 115,200 showtime_seat rows; every seeded booking carries a payment in captured state so the seeded dashboard is non-empty and never reads zero; every seeded booking carries a receipt_dispatch row in state suppressed with attempts = 0 and no dispatch timestamp, and the seed enqueues no receipt job for any of them.
SourceRef: P-XCT-30 SRC-003 OPEN-SEED-01 SRC-003 OPEN-SCALE-02 FR-ADR-067 FR-ADR-038

Title: Write no audit row from the seed, and warn before the layout freezes
Description: The seed creates the first admin itself, so at its earliest writes no user row exists that an actor column could point at - and P-ADM-19 forbids both substitutes, a role name and a service account. The absence is specified rather than left open, and it is the only exemption from the same-transaction audit rule anywhere in the product; no application code path inherits it. Touches OPEN-SEATLABEL-01, whose deadline is Phase 2: the story warns and does not decide.
AcceptanceCriteria: SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log after a fresh seed returns 0; no seed or system service account row exists and no audit row is written with a null or placeholder actor_user_id; every seeded row is identifiable as seeded by a DEMO prefix on its name or by an address at SEED_EMAIL_DOMAIN; the seed prints exactly one line before its first showtime write naming what is about to become permanent and which halls it affects, and it is a notice rather than a prompt - the seed does not stop and wait for input, because a script that blocks on input cannot run as a one-off container task; the write ordering is vocabulary, then screens and seats, then films, then showtimes, and a film inserted before its vocabulary exists makes the seed exit non-zero without a partial catalogue; the seed is idempotent, keyed on the placeholder identifiers, and skips what exists, including an account whose password the client changed by hand; a separate, explicitly named wipe-and-reseed command exists, is not the default, and docs/30 Deployment/ states in those words that it is never run against the deployed environment and that seeded rows there are permanent because nothing is ever deleted; the specification tells the client to settle seat labelling before running the seed against a deployed environment and says why in the same breath - the first showtime write freezes all six halls, so renumbering a seat, removing a seat and moving a seat between categories are all refused with 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN from then on, and locally the route back is wipe and reseed while in the deployed environment there is none; a handler that writes without an audit row remains a defect.
SourceRef: P-XCT-30 P-XCT-03 FR-ADR-019 FR-ADR-012 SRC-003 OPEN-SEED-01

Title: Contain no artificial-intelligence feature and send no customer data to a model
Description: Ruled and reserved: legal. This governs the product. That the product is built by reading this repository is a separate matter, and it is why the repository holds no credential and no real customer data.
AcceptanceCriteria: The application's outbound network paths are exactly six - S3, SQS, SES, SSM Parameter Store, ECR and CloudWatch Logs - and none is a model endpoint, asserted by an outbound-host allowlist test that fails on any other host; a case-insensitive grep over backend/ and frontend/ for openai, anthropic, bedrock, sagemaker, huggingface, embedding, inference and recommend returns no hit outside the sentence that forbids them; no recommendation model, generated customer-facing copy, classifier or assistant exists in the product; listings sort by the customer's chosen filter, defaulting to newest first, computed by ordinary code and never by a ranking model; no customer data is sent anywhere for inference, at any point, by any process.
SourceRef: P-XCT-31 SRC-003 OPEN-MODEL-01

Title: Give every seeded account a password it can sign in with, without committing a credential
Description: Known and unbuilt, and it stops Phase 2 and Phase 4. Hashes cannot be read back and the only specified route to a first password is the reset flow, which needs SES - sandboxed, refusing any unverified recipient, and every seeded address is at a domain that can never be verified. Without this, Phase 2 has no admin who can sign in and Phase 4 has no fifty customers for the concurrency proof.
AcceptanceCriteria: scripts/seed.py reads SEED_DEFAULT_PASSWORD from the environment, which has no default and is read by the seed and by nothing else - the API and the worker never read it, so no container refuses to boot over a value it has no use for; absent, the seed exits non-zero before its first write naming the variable, and the database is exactly as it was, with no warning and no generated value; shorter than PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH (12) characters - a character count, matching what the registration path enforces - or longer than 72 bytes, the seed exits non-zero naming the bound, each bound checked in its own unit, because bcrypt silently ignores the excess past 72 bytes and a shorter password would then work; equal to the .env.example placeholder, the seed exits non-zero, refused by value; the value is hashed once at BCRYPT_COST through the same hashing function the registration path uses, and that one hash is reused across all 63 accounts - one bcrypt run and not sixty-three; the addresses are deterministic - admin-01@, manager-01@ through manager-12@, customer-01@ through customer-50@, all at SEED_EMAIL_DOMAIN, which defaults to demo.frontrow.invalid, reserved by RFC 2606 and guaranteed never to resolve; the seed prints the addresses grouped by role with a count of each and never prints the password, not to stdout, not to a log line and not to a file; no password and no hash is committed anywhere; the twelve managers map to screens by screen_number = floor((m - 1) / 2) + 1, so manager-01 and manager-02 hold Screen 1; after the seed, POST /api/auth/login as admin-01@demo.frontrow.invalid with the value that was set returns a session cookie, and all fifty seeded customers authenticate through the same endpoint.
SourceRef: P-XCT-32 SRC-003 OPEN-SEED-01 SRC-002 §9.1 FR-ADR-067 FR-ADR-050 FR-ADR-060 FR-ADR-034 E8 S7.9

Title: Specify the deployed seed run as a one-off task on its own task definition family
Description: The same shape as the migration run, deliberately, so the client learns one pattern rather than two. A separate family rather than a command override, because a secret must be in a family to be resolved from it and putting it in the shared family is exactly what the seed-only rule forbids. Two families, one image, so the code and the seed stay the same build. All of it is Zone C and the build session builds none of it.
AcceptanceCriteria: The container entrypoint accepts seed as its fourth command alongside api, worker and migrate, runs scripts/seed.py and exits with its status, and no long-running process runs the seed and no flag makes one; docs/30 Deployment/ specifies a one-off ECS task on a task definition family that is the seed's alone and never the service's, using the same image, run once and deliberately by the client; it specifies SEED_DEFAULT_PASSWORD as an SSM SecureString at /frontrow/<environment>/SEED_DEFAULT_PASSWORD referenced by valueFrom from that family alone, so the service's task definition never carries the parameter; it names the extra ssm:GetParameters resource the execution role needs for that parameter; it gives the acceptance criterion as: sign in as admin-01@ with the value that was stored; docs/30 Deployment/AWS_PREP_QUEUE.md carries a row for it with a needed-by phase of Phase 2, announced while code is still being written; the build session creates none of the task definition, the SSM parameter, the role grant or the run, and has no write access to anything in AWS.
SourceRef: P-XCT-32 P-XCT-16 P-XCT-26 FR-ADR-054 FR-ADR-003 E8 S7.9
